proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy-preserving execution, secrets management, and runtime security guardrails across agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to establish security threat models, privacy architectures, runtime defense specifications, and operational guardrails for autonomous and multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Functioning as an intersecting architectural layer across the foundation, the working group reviews and bolsters the deliverables of adjacent groups against agent-specific vulnerabilities, including capability escalation, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and rogue agent failure modes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer and conducts bi-weekly sessions using GitHub, Discord, and collaborative working drafts to advance charter milestones and technical outputs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. Operating in close synchronization with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group also coordinates pre-competitively with external domain initiatives including OWASP Agentic AI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Charter Themes
The working group structures its active charter and technical workstreams across distinct security domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:

- **Privacy and Protected Data**: Identifying sensitive data boundaries, PII obfuscation techniques, and assessing whether autonomous agents introduce novel classifications for regulated data domains (such as HIPAA)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Privacy-Preserving Agentic Workflows**: Architecting mechanisms where agents operate against encrypted data without unauthorized external egress, utilizing zero-knowledge (ZK) verification and hardware-attested Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Sensitive Data and Secrets Management**: Formulating standards for separating runtime execution credentials (such as API keys and environment variables) from proprietary context and model memory layers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Rogue Agent Containment and Blast Radius Mitigation**: Defining runtime policy-as-code interception, capability fencing, blast radius metrics, and out-of-band [kill switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) mechanisms to contain misbehaving agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce and Payment Security**: Establishing strict technical guardrails to mitigate account drainage, credential leakage, and unauthorized transactional scope in autonomous payment agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Domain Taxonomy**: Developing an internal vocabulary of security and privacy definitions before bubbling unified terms up into the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

## Cross-Working-Group Boundaries
To ensure focus and eliminate duplication of effort, the working group maintains defined jurisdictional boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:

- **Governance and Ethics**: Value judgments, AI bias, and regulatory compliance frameworks are explicitly deferred to the [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Baseline model hallucination analysis and evaluation benchmarks reside with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), while edge cases involving non-malicious agent misbehavior and operational derailment remain monitored by Security and Privacy for guardrail development[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Identity and Trust**: Agent-to-agent capability delegation, DID structures, and cryptographic identity primitives are coordinated jointly with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17**: Working group orientation session hosted by Linux Foundation AI leadership, establishing governance structure, chair nomination processes, and open problem ideation across agent attack surfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer confirmed as working group chair; working group formalized charter scope decisions, expanding protected data privacy themes, bounding commerce security, and delegating ethics to governance bodies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream tasked with analyzing regulatory compliance requirements, risk assessment frameworks, and policy baselines for autonomous and multi-agent systems. The working group bridges global regulatory instruments—such as the EU AI Act and eIDAS 2—with concrete technical architectures, risk-scoring methodologies, and operational guardrails for enterprise deployments.

# Architecture / Specification
Operating under Linux Foundation antitrust and pre-competitive collaboration policies, the working group maintains a biweekly meeting cadence and relies on shared running documentation alongside community Discord channels for ongoing collaboration.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77] Operational records and meeting minutes follow a standardized template and automated agent-driven synthesis workflow.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a]

The group executes against a structured three-step deliverable pipeline:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Cataloging existing international standards, regulatory mandates, and enterprise risk practices across regulated sectors, including GDPR privacy controls, the EU AI Act, and digital identity standards.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
2. **Gap Analysis**: Pinpointing structural deficiencies where traditional AI governance and software compliance models fail to address emerging autonomous agent behaviors, multi-agent coordination, and non-deterministic execution risks.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Formulating reference frameworks, risk protocols, and implementation baselines for organizational deployment and human oversight interactions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]

Working group governance operates in alignment with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md). Leadership is established via elected chair and co-chair positions tasked with drafting the group charter, driving 90-day execution plans, and presenting charter milestones to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] External engagement encompasses alignment with global policy makers, such as Singapore regulatory authorities, as well as collaboration across related foundation initiatives.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]

# Lifecycle History
The working group launched on 2026-02-19 with an inaugural kickoff meeting defining governance rules, leadership nomination procedures, and initial focus areas.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] On 2026-03-05, the group formally adopted its three-step operating model and initialized the landscape analysis phase.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation managing working groups, project intake, and technical lifecycle policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), established by the Governing Board (GB) to evaluate project intake proposals, oversee technical working groups, and apply foundation lifecycle policies.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941] Formally operating under a charter adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC facilitates collaboration across Technical Projects and the broader open-source ecosystem.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

# Architecture / Specification

## Purpose and Composition
- **Composition**: Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to serve as a voting TC Representative.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Officers**: The TC elects a TC Chair and an optional Co-Chair annually to preside over meetings and execute procedural responsibilities.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Authority Scope**: If conflicts arise between the TC Charter and the AAIF Charter or GB actions, the AAIF Charter and Governing Board control.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

## Operational Responsibilities
Under section 2.3 of the Charter, the TC is responsible for:
1. Establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF working groups, such as [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
2. Coordinating collaboration across Technical Projects, establishing community technical priorities, and setting an overarching technical vision.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
3. Recommending proposed projects to the GB for acceptance as official Technical Projects.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
4. Applying and maintaining the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and deciding transitions in project lifecycle stages.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
5. Recommending technical resource priorities and funding allocations to the Governing Board.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

## Decision-Making and Voting Procedures
- **Consensus & Lazy Consensus**: The TC strives for consensus. Routine proposals utilize lazy consensus under a "silence-as-agreement" model, passing automatically if no voting member registers a formal objection within 72 hours.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Quorum & Formal Voting**: Formal decision votes require a quorum of at least 50% of the voting members present. In the event of an objection to lazy consensus, electronic decisions require approval from a simple majority of all TC voting members.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Deadlock Escalation**: Any voting member may refer an unresolved vote to the GB for resolution.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Amendments**: Charter amendments require a two-thirds majority vote of the TC followed by Governing Board approval.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-03**: Formal Charter of the AAIF Technical Committee adopted by the Governing Board.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP-WG) is an AAIF technical collaboration workstream dedicated to establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35] Co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google), the group develops open threat models, shared taxonomies, and architectural design patterns enabling providers, consumers, and peer working groups to maintain trustworthy, resilient agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

# Architecture / Specification

## Mission and Mandate
On March 31, 2026, the working group adopted its formal mission statement:
> "The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem. Producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI."[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

## Scope Areas
- **Security Architecture & Design Patterns**: Specifying runtime isolation, boundary protections, and safe packaging standards for [agent skills](../standards/agent-skills.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Privacy Engineering**: Prioritizing concrete technical controls—such as data minimization, memory isolation, secure scratchpads, and sensitive data handling—over legal regulatory interpretation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Threat Modeling**: Formulating practical threat models evaluating prompt injection resistance, tool poisoning, social engineering, and autonomous execution attack surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Forensics and Runtime Governance**: Designing audit logging guidelines, behavioral anomaly detection, and operational [kill switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]

## Cross-Workgroup Collaboration
The SP-WG coordinates actively across peer AAIF bodies to prevent domain overlap:
- **Identity and Trust**: Defers identity issuance and delegation mechanisms to the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), while focusing SP-WG efforts on execution bounding, authorization checks, and audit logging.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Observability and Traceability**: Coordinates with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on anomaly monitoring and audit trail telemetry.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
- **Agentic Commerce**: Coordinates via cross-group representation with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) on payment authorization constraints and financial guardrails.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Governance, Risk, and Regulatory**: Partners with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) for regulatory baseline tracking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

## Key Deliverables
1. **Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions**: Living vocabulary defining security and threat concepts in multi-agent environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
2. **Agentic AI Threat Model Framework**: Structured framework mapping multi-agent attack surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Architectural catalog for containment and policy enforcement.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
4. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: Practical operational handbook for builders and deployment teams.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
5. **Cross-Workgroup Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Verification checklist assessing security and privacy requirements across AAIF technical deliverables.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing agent observability conventions, workflow-level trace models, and alignment across OpenTelemetry, OWASP, and W3C.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an AAIF technical working group organized to convene practitioners, platform vendors, and standards bodies to develop a unified understanding of agent observability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88] Led by primary contact Pavan Sudheendra, the group operates as a coordination forum that identifies telemetry gaps, aligns external standards efforts, and formulates guidance or specifications only when existing industry bodies cannot fulfill practitioner needs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

# Architecture / Specification

## Purpose and Problem Statement
The OT-WG provides visibility into what AI agents do, how they execute steps, and their impacts across external systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88] The group addresses three primary industry problems:
1. **Telemetry Fragmentation**: Countering proprietary format proliferation and vendor lock-in across disparate agent tracing tools.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
2. **Session and Workflow Gaps**: Extending point-in-time model call tracing (such as OpenInference or OTel GenAI conventions) to cover multi-turn sessions, complex tool interactions, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
3. **Accountability and Content Lineage**: Providing verifiable audit trails and lineage tracking across multi-modal workflow transformations where content fidelity and grounding must be proven.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

## Guiding Principles
Under its charter, the OT-WG operates against six foundational principles:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: Default to aligning with and contributing upstream to active standards efforts rather than competing with them.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Interoperability over innovation**: Compose directly with existing tracing frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Observable by default**: Encourage systems that provide turnkey telemetry out of the box.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Move at the speed of the ecosystem**: Prioritize incremental delivery and iterative releases.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Adoption is key**: Value practical, implementable specifications over theoretical perfection.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Vendor and framework neutrality**: Avoid giving commercial advantage to any specific platform or vendor.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

## External Alignment and Focus Areas
The working group functions as the AAIF interface to external bodies, including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88] Its founding focus area is the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), designed to establish shared turn boundaries and session-level telemetry propagation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared threat models, defensive design patterns, security best practices, and review frameworks for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group dedicated to defining threat models, architectural security patterns, privacy engineering guidelines, and cross-workstream review criteria for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Operating under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and governed by the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), the group provides defensive patterns and practical security baselines to mitigate emergent risks such as prompt injection, tool hijacking, credential exfiltration, and unauthorized multi-agent delegation.

# Scope and Deliverables

The formal working group charter and operational scope define coverage over threat modeling, agent control and containment, and runtime safeguards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. In April 2026, the working group unanimously approved five initial deliverables targeting a 3–6 month horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

1. **Taxonomy**: A living reference document defining domain-specific security and privacy terminology feeding into the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
2. **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: A research initiative evaluating whether existing frameworks (such as OWASP or NIST) sufficiently capture agent vulnerabilities or if an agent-native framework is needed to address compound threats across trust boundaries, tool delegation, and persistent memory stores.
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-focused collection of architectural patterns covering human-in-the-loop validation, hook and interceptor extensibility, logical and semantic constraints, and privacy-preserving execution.
4. **[Agentic Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Operational security guidance addressing foundational topics such as secrets management and secure tool invocation for practitioners building agentic workflows.
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: A structured review checklist designed after IETF area review models to assist other AAIF working groups in identifying security and privacy implications early in specification lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# External Alignments and Technical Touchpoints

The working group monitors and engages with external technical initiatives relevant to agent security boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors**: Participating in specification efforts to standardize execution interceptors and security hooks across MCP host and server implementations.
- **MCP Apps**: Analyzing agent browser-like interactions, site verification, and conversational boundary risks in emerging client-side application extensions.
- **Project Glasswing**: Tracking Linux Foundation advancements in automated software security evaluation for applicability to agentic workloads.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-14**: Working group unanimously approved its charter, operational scope, and initial five 3–6 month deliverables, scheduling formal presentation and ratification with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and schema-driven landscape mapping open-source agentic AI projects, standards, and ecosystem members using landscape2.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive visualization of prominent open-source software projects, open standards, and member initiatives across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Maintained in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape catalogs key frameworks, orchestration runtimes, protocol specifications, and evaluation suites to give developers and enterprise adopters a structured map of active open-source technologies[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is generated using the CNCF `landscape2` compilation toolchain and published daily from configuration data maintained in the AAIF landscape repository[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. The data source is defined primarily within `landscape.yml` and paired with SVG visual assets stored in the repository[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Inclusion and Categorization Criteria
Entries submitted for inclusion in the landscape must satisfy defined community and governance criteria[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open-Source Requirement**: Projects must be genuine open-source software. Closed-source products, proprietary standards, and proprietary solutions wrapping open-source technologies are explicitly excluded[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Star Threshold**: Open-source repositories must generally possess at least 1,000 GitHub stars and fit clearly into an established category[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Single-Category Placement**: An organization or project is generally mapped to a single category representing its primary or best-known offering, preventing multi-box duplication across the taxonomy[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Commercial Versions**: Commercial distributions of open-source projects are generally omitted in favor of the upstream open-source project itself[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Trademark Control**: Organization metadata must correspond to the entity controlling the software or trademark[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Asset and Metadata Standards
Submissions must follow standardized graphical and metadata conventions[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **SVG Vector Logos**: Logos must be vector SVG files containing English text, using transparent or white backgrounds (no reversed color fills), and utilizing vertically stacked orientations when multiple variants exist[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Extra Fields**: Detailed technical information, documentation URLs, and project summaries are specified via the `extra` configuration block in `landscape.yml`[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# References
- Upstream Engine: [cncf/landscape2](https://github.com/cncf/landscape2)
- AAIF Portal: [aaif.io](https://aaif.io)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body focused on establishing shared threat models, defensive design patterns, security controls, and privacy standards for agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. It operates under oversight from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates across workstreams on unified taxonomies, protocol boundary defenses, and runtime isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its deliverables and community tracking across several technical domains:
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy**: The group drives initial terminology extraction for foundational security and privacy concepts, contributing its baseline definitions to the wider [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security Interceptors**: Active monitoring and specification analysis of Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors to incorporate hooks for privacy filtering, data loss prevention, and token redaction [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Client and UI Boundary Protection**: Assessing runtime isolation risks introduced by initiatives such as MCP Apps, where embedding user interfaces breaks standard browser sandbox boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Multi-Agent Guardrails**: Formulating reference guardrails and boundary definitions for multi-agent delegation in coordination with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, the working group charter was submitted to the Technical Committee; while reaching consensus without substantive objection, administrative quorum votes were disrupted by GitHub infrastructure outages, prompting the group to advance deliverable formation pragmatically [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Operational cadence transitioned toward concise checkpoint meetings alongside asynchronous, self-organizing sub-workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation managing working groups, project intake, and architectural coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governance body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for charter approvals, project lifecycle transitions, and cross-working-group architectural alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. It provides authoritative oversight over foundation working groups and technical projects in accordance with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
The TC operates as the governing board for foundation scope and community initiatives:
- **Working Group Charter Approval**: Acts as the formal approval gate validating working group scopes, charters, and cross-organizational balance prior to formal incorporation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Intake Governance**: Oversees standardized proposal intake via `aaif/working-group-proposals`, enforcing member affiliation prerequisites and scheduled review cycles [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Cross-Group Harmonization**: Coordinates joint initiatives across working groups, such as foundation-wide taxonomy alignment championed by groups like [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, Manik succeeded Matt as AAIF CTO, guiding technical strategy and meeting cadence across international time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Concurrently, the TC established an intake staging window accepting initial working group proposals, setting the formal evaluation start date to June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the standardized intake procedure, eligibility criteria, and metadata requirements for proposing new technical working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. All proposals must be submitted through the official GitHub issue template in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository to ensure consistent evaluation under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification
Proposals require explicit submitter identification and structural alignment before committee consideration:
- **Submitter Affiliation**: Submissions must originate from an authorized representative of an AAIF Member Organization, indicating whether the company holds Platinum or Gold membership status [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Proposal Metadata**: The intake form requires full legal name, professional email address, parent organization, and professional role title [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Intake Pipeline**: New submissions automatically receive the `New` label and are assigned to Foundation program operations for intake triage [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Review Timeline**: While the Technical Committee continuously accepts proposals via the structured form, official formal reviews for chartering begin on June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, the submission template schema was cleaned up to eliminate duplicate YAML top-level headers and fix textual typographical errors [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1], formalizing the submission intake ahead of the June 2026 review window [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards and viewpoints for agent identity, authentication, delegation, and cross-organizational trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Led by primary contact Grant Miller, the group enables agents to be discovered across platforms, prove identity, represent human or organizational sponsors, and declare runtime authorizations and approval histories across organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

The working group operates in coordination with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates with adjacent workstreams including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's technical scope and boundary definitions address six primary areas [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Defining how agents identify, authenticate, and communicate their origin, operators, software dependencies, and runtime context.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Structuring how agents represent delegation on behalf of a human, team, role, service, or process, and constraining the propagation depth of delegated authority.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Conveying actionable bounds, time-to-live restrictions, policy rules, and human consent or sign-off history required for short-lived, fine-grained agent authorizations.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Enabling multi-tenant and inter-organizational evaluation frameworks to verify foreign agent credentials and permission claims safely.
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Specifying directory formats, description metadata, and discovery interfaces supporting interoperability and auditability.
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts**: Addressing both enterprise governance workflows and consumer interaction patterns.

### Boundary and Scope Constraints
The group maintains clear boundaries relative to other initiatives [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- Does not act as a formal standards development organization (SDO) or ratify formal standards independently; it informs and contributes to upstream standards bodies.
- Does not define comprehensive agent runtime security architectures or threat defenses, leaving execution security to the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md).
- Avoids authoring broad public policy positions or normative Responsible AI declarations unless directly tied to identity, accountability, or consent representation.
- Avoids building production-grade identity cloud infrastructure or operating proprietary certification programs.

# Lifecycle History
The Identity & Trust charter was submitted and established within the AAIF working group framework under the leadership of Grant Miller [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing agent observability conventions, workflow-level trace models, and standards harmonization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to develop a shared understanding of agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra, the group functions as a vendor-neutral coordination forum rather than a standalone competing standards organization, aligning existing industry initiatives and authoring specifications only when distinct gaps exist [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

The OT-WG addresses fragmentation across proprietary tracing formats, bridges the structural gap between individual LLM call instrumentation and multi-turn workflow-level visibility, and enables verifiable agent accountability in production systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical mission around several guiding principles and chartered focus areas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]:

- **Coordination and Upstream Contribution**: The default approach prioritizes coordinating with and contributing upstream to established specifications, including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context, rather than creating overlapping standards.
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Serves as the founding focus area, standardizing session- and workflow-level execution paths, state transitions, tool invocations, and multi-turn causality across disparate execution frameworks (see [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)).
- **Interoperability and Practical Adoption**: Prioritizes pragmatic, implementable schemas and conventions that integrate cleanly with existing agent ecosystems without favoring specific platforms or runtimes.
- **Multi-Modal and Multi-Turn Lineage**: Investigates telemetry requirements for content fidelity, modality transformations, and long-running agent workflows where standard API-level tracing is insufficient.

# Lifecycle History
The working group was ratified by members on 2026-04-15 and formally approved on 2026-05-13 under the leadership of primary contact Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining intake criteria, submission forms, review gates, and Technical Committee engagement for prospective AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process establishes the operational intake workflow for introducing new open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Operating in alignment with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) and supervised by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), this process standardizes proposal metadata, submission requirements, and automated validation gates.

The procedure ensures that prospective projects meet baseline open-source licensing, architectural relevance, and community governance requirements while maintaining clear distinctions between mandatory submission prerequisites and optional indicators [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification
Submissions proceed through the standardized project intake issue template within the `aaif/project-proposals` repository [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

### Field Requirements and Alignment
To prevent artificial intake barriers, the proposal submission form strictly aligns required form fields with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:
- **Mandatory Disclosures**: Core project identity, mission, repository location, license compliance, and scope applicability within agentic AI.
- **Optional Disclosures**: A published roadmap and the OpenSSF Best Practices badge status are explicitly optional at initial intake [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Applicants may supply them if available, but their absence does not block proposal submission or automated issue validation.

# Lifecycle History
Initial proposal templates enforced strict completion of roadmap and security badge fields; PR #23 updated `project-proposal.yml` to mark roadmap and OpenSSF badge fields optional, directly synchronizing the intake form with the project lifecycle policy [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining shared threat models, defensive patterns, privacy standards, and containment frameworks for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Formed to address structural risks specific to autonomous agents—including prompt injection, confused deputy attacks, authorization boundary violations, tool invocation risks, and agent memory exploitation—the working group produces open threat models, architectural patterns, and cross-cutting checklists for ecosystem-wide adoption [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on technical control architectures, runtime boundaries, and ecosystem standards across five defined operational areas [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]:

- **Threat Modeling and Attack Analysis**: Developing threat representations for multi-agent persuasion, indirect prompt injection, and expanded blast radiuses in delegated autonomous execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns**: Standardizing technical countermeasures, including hook interception mechanisms and runtime policy gates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Formulating baseline requirements for runtime privilege isolation, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and kill-switch patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
- **Data Protection and Privacy**: Mitigating sensitive data handling risks, unintended state leakage across tool chains, and long-term memory poisoning [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Authoring review criteria to integrate security and privacy baselines into specifications produced by peer AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

Explicitly excluded from the group's scope are subjective value judgments and AI ethics (deferred to governance bodies), formal regulatory and legal compliance interpretation, and commercial product certifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Deliverables pair technical execution patterns in the catalog with broad operational guidance in `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`, anchored by analytical findings in `../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was initiated under the leadership of Chair Alex Frazer and Co-Chair Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Following initial drafting and community review, charter voting moved to the Linux Foundation LFX platform ahead of formal approval in May 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. During May 2026, the working group aligned deliverable roadmaps to sequence threat modeling gap analysis ahead of pattern cataloging, transitioned taxonomy deliverables into a foundation-wide cross-working group initiative, and initiated external standards coordination on agent hooks and security protocols [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and schema-driven landscape mapping open-source agentic AI projects, standards, and runtime frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive, schema-driven landscape cataloging agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and global regulatory regimes across the open-source agentic AI domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Managed under the guidance of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape visualizes ecosystem boundaries and adoption tiers using the CNCF Landscape 2 engine.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is built on CNCF Landscape 2 (landscape2) and deployed as a Next.js static application to GitHub Pages under the path /ws-taxonomy-landscape/landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

### Visual Configuration and Hierarchy
Configuration maintained within settings.yml establishes the visual styling and categorical grouping of ecosystem entries:
- **Project Tiers**: Projects are classified across four color-coded tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]:
  - `Graduated`: Top-tier mature foundation projects (`#00f5d4`).
  - `Incubating`: Accelerating projects under active foundation development (`#9b5de5`).
  - `Member`: Technologies and products contributed by AAIF member organizations (`#00b4d8`).
  - `External`: Relevant open-source and proprietary ecosystem solutions outside direct AAIF governance (`#f15bb5`).
- **Brand Palette**: Styled using slate navigation bars (`#1e293b`), deep slate canvas background (`#0f172a`), and blue accent indicators (`#3b82f6`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Default Display**: Renders entries in card mode with organization logos and inline capability descriptions enabled[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

### Automated Preview Pipeline
Pull requests modifying landscape.yml, settings.yml, or assets in hosted_logos trigger an automated GitHub Actions preview workflow[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00]. The workflow executes a GitHub Script comment action that computes a dynamic overlay preview parameter set pointing to the preview harness[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00]:
- `overlay-data`: Pulls the PR branch's raw landscape.yml data file.
- `overlay-settings`: Pulls the PR branch's raw settings.yml configuration file.
- `overlay-logos`: Ingests logos staged under the PR branch's hosted_logos path.

This mechanism allows contributors and reviewers to inspect metadata and layout modifications in an interactive web harness before changes are merged into the main catalog branch[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining technical project admission requirements, the Growth, Impact, and Emeritus lifecycle stages, and the annual review process.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal process for open technical projects to join the Foundation, navigate lifecycle stages, and undergo annual operational evaluations [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Governed by the Technical Committee in alignment with the AAIF Charter, the framework provides structured progression, mentorship, and access to foundation resources across all maturity levels [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Requirements
Prospective projects must submit formal proposals to the `aaif/project-proposals` repository detailing [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Project identity, scope, historical origins, and architectural value proposition.
- Explicit alignment with the AAIF mission and integration points with existing foundation initiatives.
- Evidence of real-world adoption, practitioner use cases, and leadership decision-making structures.
- An identified Technical Committee sponsor to provide mentorship.
- Licensing under an OSI-approved permissive open-source license, alongside public issue trackers and repository URLs.
- Documented automated CI/CD validation, public release processes, and specification contribution pathways.

## Lifecycle Stages
The policy governs three sequential maturity stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Initial intake stage for maturing projects with functional codebases, initial contributor bases, and active community interest seeking deeper foundation alignment and mentorship [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade projects demonstrating sustained cross-organizational adoption, stable governance practices, diverse maintainer distribution, and critical architectural importance to the agentic ecosystem [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Emeritus Stage**: End-of-life stage for projects that are no longer actively maintained or have minimal development activity, preserving code repositories and historical artifacts under foundation stewardship [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Annual Review Process
All admitted projects undergo a mandatory annual review administered by the Technical Committee to verify ongoing health, evaluate stage progression criteria, confirm governance compliance, and address infrastructure requirements [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
The policy took effect on March 18, 2026, establishing standardized intake criteria and stage definitions administered via the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Clarifying typographical corrections across the Emeritus Stage definitions and issue intake templates were integrated subsequently [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Intake guidelines, eligibility constraints, required proposal sections, and charter timelines for proposing new Agentic AI Foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the formal requirements, structural criteria, and evaluation workflow for proposing new technical and policy working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working groups convene subject matter experts to tackle domain-specific challenges, formulate vendor-neutral standards, and deliver actionable technical guidance on critical agentic AI initiatives [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Submitter Eligibility
Working group proposals are exclusively accepted from active Agentic AI Foundation member organizations in good standing across all membership tiers [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Submissions from outside foundation membership are not eligible for review [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Required Proposal Sections
Every proposal submitted to the Foundation must incorporate eight structured components [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Proposer identity, organizational affiliation, role, contact details, leadership availability, and membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
2. **Working Group Identity**: A concise name and one-sentence non-jargon focus summary [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Articulation of the agentic AI gap or opportunity and alignment with foundation priorities [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Target outputs, including technical reports, specifications, datasets, benchmarks, software tooling, or policy guidance [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Target meeting cadence, milestone roadmap, and anticipated lifecycle duration, normally structured around a 12–24 month charter cycle [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Necessary participant skill sets and commitments from interested individuals or organizations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Analysis of industry need, competitive urgency, and ecosystem benefits [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
8. **Resource Considerations**: Hosting, infrastructure, tooling, or staff support requirements [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Governance Interaction
Approved working groups operate according to the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), progressing through sandbox and active charter phases under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive visualization and structured catalog of open-source projects, specifications, and foundational initiatives across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. Managed via GitHub and validated against CNCF Landscape2 tooling, the resource indexes key industry software while delineating AAIF member contributions from broader open-source developments [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification

## Catalog Structure and Groups
The landscape utilizes declarative YAML metadata to group and categorize ecosystem entries [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]:
- **Project Watchlist**: Highlights leading open-source agentic AI software projects and monitors emerging technologies across the industry [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Member Projects**: Explicitly separates and highlights projects contributed or led by AAIF member organizations from external open-source initiatives [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Ecosystem Momentum Sync**: Supports alignment and data synchronization with the LFX Insights Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard to monitor project growth and contributor activity [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

## Automated CI Validation
The landscape repository enforces automated pull request and merge group verification via GitHub Actions [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]:
- `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` executes against `landscape.yml` to confirm data integrity, required fields, and category schemas [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].
- Settings validation executes against `settings.yml` to verify UI configuration and display parameters [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group cataloging open specifications, reference architectures, and interoperability models across agentic commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to catalog, align, and harmonize open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of individuals, enterprises, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the working group maintains protocol neutrality and does not author competing proprietary commerce protocols, functioning instead as a collaborative forum across merchants, wallets, payment networks, identity providers, and AI platforms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's scope is strictly bounded by interfaces, signaling formats, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and the broader commerce ecosystem, deliberately excluding underlying system internals such as specific payment rail operations or fraud detection mechanics[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### In-Scope Domain Areas
- **Discovery and Negotiation**: Standardizing agent-merchant exchanges concerning product offers, stock availability, commercial terms, and fulfillment options[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart and Checkout**: Defining structured cart composition, validation checks, and checkout transaction handoffs between agent runtimes and merchant platforms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity and Delegated Authority**: Collaborating with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) to convey buyer identity credentials, scoped delegation parameters, and verifiable user consent records[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Specifying intent, authorization, and settlement signals connecting agents to payment wallets and card, real-time, or on-chain settlement rails[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling**: Establishing risk-posture interchange between agents and fraud platforms without specifying proprietary mitigation logic[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Human-in-the-Loop & Autonomy Boundaries**: Formulating confirmation checkpoints, escalation policies, and autonomy level declarations in alignment with [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Post-Purchase Operations**: Interfacing claims, dispute escalations, chargeback signaling, and real-time order lifecycle tracking[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### Explicit Non-Goals
The working group explicitly treats the internal implementations of payment rails, core fraud engines, identity provider directories, and marketplace backends as out of scope[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Additionally, general societal-impact AI policies, consumer point-of-sale hardware, non-agentic legacy commerce standards, and the direct creation of competing foundation-owned commerce protocols are excluded[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-15**: Formal charter approved and ratified under co-chairs Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body dedicated to establishing comprehensive threat taxonomies, defensive runtime patterns, security best practices, and privacy standards across autonomous agent ecosystems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Following formal charter approval in May 2026, the working group coordinates cross-industry security evaluations, runtime review checklists, and reference architectures across AAIF initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates through specialized workstreams structured with self-selected community leadership and contributor cohorts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:

- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops actionable engineering standards and operational security guidance, addressing model sandboxing, tool boundary defense, and credential hygiene (aligned with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework Design**: Analyzes multi-agent evasion, prompt injection, and persuasion threats, liaising closely with the cross-working group Taxonomy workstream to apply security classifications to ecosystem tooling (aligned with [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security & Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Formulates reproducible architectural mitigation patterns, such as [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Provides structured security and privacy gate evaluation criteria for incoming Foundation reference architectures and project submissions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

### Ecosystem Collaborations
The group collaborates directly with the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), chaired by Junjie Bu, to ensure that emerging runtime security guardrails, gateways, and firewalls are harmonized with broader Foundation terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-26**: Formal charter approval confirmed; community leads organized across four primary workstreams, Junjie Bu confirmed as Landscape/Taxonomy lead, and deliverable schedule adjusted to accommodate working group ramp-up[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open-source catalog, schema, and visualization matrix tracking technologies, protocols, frameworks, and tools across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. Managed under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape groups projects into standardized functional categories mapped directly to Agentic AI Foundation working groups and technical initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is maintained declaratively via structured definitions in `landscape.yml`, organizing projects into seven core domains aligned with Foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Captures autonomous agent frameworks (e.g., Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, Google ADK) and orchestration engines (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, Diagrid Dapr, LangGraph), aligning with the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Documents interoperability specifications and registry systems, aligning with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Tracks policy proxies, threat mitigation layers, and sandboxes in collaboration with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Classifies telemetry emitters, OpenTelemetry instrumentation pipelines, and execution trace stores, aligned with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Maps transaction gateways, checkout handlers, and agent payment wallets, aligned with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Synthesizes regulatory frameworks, compliance monitoring suites, and risk assessment schemas, aligned with the [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Catalogs automated evaluation frameworks, simulation harnesses, and benchmark datasets, aligned with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05**: Taxonomy and Landscape workstream organized under Junjie Bu; schema structured to categorize Foundation member projects and external open-source tooling across seven primary agentic AI architectural layers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining intake criteria, triage status labels, review gates, and Technical Committee voting rules for foundation-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process defines the operating intake procedure and governance pathway for open-source initiatives applying to become foundation-hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Administered through the `aaif/project-proposals` repository, the intake process structures how candidates submit structured applications, complete preliminary staff triage, present before the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), and transition into the governance tiers defined in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Application Submission and Tracking

Applicants begin by opening a formal Project Proposal Application issue template within `aaif/project-proposals` [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Once submitted, the application enters the public Project Proposals Board where its operational progression is tracked across standard status labels [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:

- `New`: The application is logged in the intake backlog pending initial triage [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have posted specific inquiries or requested additional technical documentation [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Too Early`: The proposal does not yet meet foundational readiness criteria; feedback is provided for future resubmission [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Approved`: The project has received favorable TC review and Governing Board ratification [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Declined`: The proposal is formally rejected with explanatory commentary recorded on the issue [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

### Technical Committee Review and Voting Gates

Following backlog triage, applicants collaborate with AAIF operational staff to construct a project review presentation [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. The application is then scheduled for evaluation during a formal meeting of the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:

1. **Tier Classification**: The TC determines whether the proposed project qualifies under the Growth or Impact lifecycle stage [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
2. **Voting Threshold**: Admission requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all seated members of the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Governing Board Ratification**: Once TC approval is secured, the proposal is referred to the AAIF Governing Board for final administrative approval [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

### Membership and Reapplication Provisions

- **Organizational Membership Independence**: Project acceptance is not contingent upon corporate membership in the AAIF; projects from non-member organizations are eligible for adoption [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Conversely, successful project intake does not confer corporate membership status (such as Silver, Gold, or Platinum tiers) or a seat on the Governing Board upon the submitter [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Reapplication Cooldown**: Projects receiving a `Declined` determination may submit a revised proposal after a mandatory cooldown period of at least three months, provided demonstrable and tangible progress addressing the TC's feedback has been achieved [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Lifecycle History

- **Repository Establishment**: Intake processes and review board templates originally hosted under `aaif/project-proposals` [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Submission Guide Revision**: Documentation updated to clarify intake criteria, staff presentation assistance, TC voting standards, and community reapplication timelines [^evt-project-proposals-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Intake guidelines, issue template workflows, status tracking labels, and Technical Committee approval rules for chartering new working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the formal submission, triage, and review framework for establishing new working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Managed through the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository, the process outlines how prospective working group organizers author proposal charters, navigate open community commentary, and obtain Technical Committee approval under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Architecture / Specification

### Submission Workflow

Proponents submit a new working group application through the structured issue template within the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Each proposal is tracked publicly on the foundation's Working Group Proposals Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

### Review Status Taxonomy

Proposals are triaged using five formal operational labels [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:

- `New`: The proposal is unreviewed and placed into the initial intake backlog [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Waiting on Comment`: The proposal requires additional details, scope boundary adjustments, or responses to reviewer feedback [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Too Early`: The proposal is immature or lacks sufficient initial momentum; guidance is recorded for prospective resubmission [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Approved`: The working group charter has been accepted by the Technical Committee and confirmed by the Governing Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Declined`: The proposal is rejected with documented rationale logged in the issue thread [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

### TC Review and Voting Requirements

Following initial triage, proposals are scheduled for live review during a regular [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) meeting [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:

- **Approval Threshold**: Formation requires a simple majority vote of all members of the Technical Committee [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- **Governing Board Ratification**: Approved working group formations remain subject to final administrative consent from the AAIF Governing Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Lifecycle History

- **Intake Process Codification**: Working group charter intake established via the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository and tracking board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an active technical workstream within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) charged with establishing vendor-neutral instrumentation architectures, telemetry schemas, and distributed execution trace specifications for autonomous agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. The group addresses the observability challenges of multi-step, multi-agent workflows, including model invocation context, dynamic tool execution spans, causal attribution, and agent-to-agent protocol boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Groups and Workstreams

To manage its charter deliverables, the working group coordinates specialized focus areas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:

- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Focuses on trace propagation, causal dependency tracking, and distributed consensus telemetry across concurrent subagent swarms and multi-agent interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Observability and Protocols**: Addresses boundary telemetry standards across Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and runtime tool bridges [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Formulates telemetry conventions and execution records capturing planner decision logic, self-reflection cycles, and runtime verification checkpoints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

### Cross-Working Group Integration

The working group participates directly in the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize shared terminology surrounding execution spans, turn boundaries, and observability artifacts across all AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

### Operating Methodology

Technical deliverables, specification proposals, and meeting minutes transition from preliminary drafting platforms to asynchronous GitHub pull requests and tracked issue backlogs within `aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability` to ensure community transparency and verifiable provenance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# References

- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group dedicated to defining threat models, defensive patterns, and operational security guidelines for autonomous agents and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. It collaborates closely with cross-cutting foundation initiatives, providing security and privacy reviews across technical workstreams.

# Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs across several active workstreams and designated lead roles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing criteria for auditing agentic systems and reference architectures.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, maintaining operational guidelines like [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, assessing gaps in existing frameworks like [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas (pending confirmation), cataloging patterns such as [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md).
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent the working group in the cross-cutting [taxonomy-and-landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream.

# Governance and Operations
The working group reports asynchronously to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through monthly GitHub updates rather than formal synchronous approval gates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Workstream leads coordinate contributor engagement using dedicated channels, interest-form lists, and open communication models.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
