proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF body chartered to establish common terminology, resolve conflicting definitions, and maintain decoupled, machine-readable landscape data [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream operates across all foundation groups to harmonize vocabulary.

# Cross-Cutting Delegate Model
Taxonomy and Landscape operates as a decoupled, foundation-wide effort where contributions are open to all community members, while individual working groups appoint dedicated delegates to review terms and resolve conflicting definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. For example, the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) appoints delegates to represent security and privacy domain semantics.

# Reporting and Governance
The workstream submits monthly asynchronous progress reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) using a pull request workflow against `reporting/` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32]. Reports are submitted by the last business day of the month, followed by a seven-calendar-day review window by the Technical Committee before merging.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group focused on benchmarking, evaluation harnesses, and verification mechanisms for autonomous agent execution. Co-chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group develops quantitative frameworks for evaluating agentic outputs and deterministic execution boundaries [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].

The working group coordinates with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and cross-links with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](./observability-and-traceability.md) to define testable performance and correctness standards.

# Governance and Operations
Operating under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), the group maintains monthly asynchronous reporting to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].

Monthly reports track:
- Progress against stated benchmark and verification objectives.
- Operational blockers and risks affecting deliverable timelines.
- Explicit decisions and intake requests requiring Technical Committee review.
- Prioritized focus items for the subsequent month.

Reports must be submitted as repository pull requests by the final business day of each reporting period, with a standard seven-calendar-day Technical Committee sign-off period [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group responsible for developing threat taxonomy models, runtime defense architectures, and privacy engineering patterns for autonomous agents. Working in conjunction with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group documents security mitigation controls and evaluates vulnerabilities across agentic systems.

# Repository Structure and Deliverable Governance
The working group organizes its codebase and public deliverables across three designated subdirectories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]:
- `charter/`: Contains the foundational working group charter, designated as a draft document until formal review and ratification.
- `deliverables/`: Houses published deliverables, such as the draft security threat taxonomy, defense guidelines, and architectural pattern profiles.
- `meeting-notes/`: Serves as the repository of chronological working group meeting notes and action items.

# Meeting Operations
Meeting minutes follow a canonical template and standardized naming convention based on meeting dates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31]. Each session log captures links to session transcripts and recordings, topics discussed, formal decisions, identified deliverables, and assigned action items with specified owners and target dates.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defense architectures, cross-WG review checklists, and reusable security design patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with evaluating threats, curating defensive architecture patterns, and serving as a security review layer across all foundation working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. The working group establishes reference guidance for agentic-specific threats, authoring reusable patterns and providing structured security and privacy oversight across AAIF initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical activities into focused workstreams and cross-foundation collaborations:

- **Threat Modeling Workstream**: Evaluates existing frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic AI vulnerabilities such as multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation hazards, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply-chain integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Documents reusable architectural patterns and anti-patterns across execution hooks, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, privacy-preserving execution (zero-knowledge proofs, trusted execution environments, encrypted vector stores), blast radius containment, secure memory retention, and agent containment or runtime intervention (kill switches, permission downgrades)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Co-led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Operates as a lightweight audit mechanism reviewing deliverables across the foundation, targeting agent identity and authorization in the Identity & Trust WG, audit logging and anomaly detection in the Observability & Traceability WG, and payment guardrails in the Agentic Commerce WG[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: The working group's initial terminology effort was transitioned into the centralized [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), with ongoing representation provided by appointed delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

# Lifecycle History
Working group deliverables operate under a formal lifecycle governance model:
- **Draft**: New deliverables carry a `DRAFT-` filename prefix and are cataloged as in-progress work[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Deliverables can only advance from Draft to Final upon explicit approval documented in the decisions section of recorded working group meeting notes, triggering removal of the `DRAFT-` prefix[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: When deliverables migrate to cross-working-group workstreams or external repositories—such as the transfer of terms to `ws-taxonomy-landscape` on 2026-06-22—the original document is preserved as a redirect note to maintain link integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation of existing AI threat frameworks against agentic-specific threats like multi-agent persuasion, tool risks, and supply-chain integrity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an ongoing technical deliverable produced by the Security and Privacy Working Group's threat modeling workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. It systematically evaluates established enterprise AI threat modeling frameworks—such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP AI Security guidelines, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—to determine whether existing frameworks adequately cover threats specific to autonomous and agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The analysis targets structural threat vectors unique to agentic execution that remain under-specified in standard ML threat models:
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion and Collusion**: Deceptive signaling, peer manipulation, or compromise cascades across autonomous agent networks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Unauthorized parameter alteration, indirect prompt injection execution, and side-channel exposure during runtime tool and function calling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across downstream tools, subagents, and third-party APIs executing on behalf of human users[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Supply-Chain Integrity**: Tamper-evident verification of system prompts, foundation model provenance, and tool manifest declarations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Lifecycle History
Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), this workstream establishes whether gaps necessitate an entirely new framework or extensions to existing standards, feeding findings directly into the [Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide and the Design Patterns Catalog[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group AAIF body established to maintain a unified agentic AI vocabulary and curate the open-source ecosystem landscape[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Chaired by Junjie Bu, the workstream serves as the centralized home for harmonizing terminology, resolving conflicting definitions, and managing terminology updates across the foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates through delegates appointed by each AAIF technical working group to ensure consensus across domains:
- Delegate representatives review proposals and harmonize terminology between specialized workstreams and the universal taxonomy corpus[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- For the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) represent security and privacy terminology requirements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- Contributions and definitions are maintained as decoupled data assets managed through open pull request workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-06-09, working groups agreed to merge domain-specific terminology efforts—including the Security and Privacy Working Group's Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions—into this consolidated cross-WG workstream, officially transitioning on 2026-06-22[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to identify vulnerability vectors, define defense architectures, and produce prescriptive implementation standards for secure agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. The group operates with public repositories and uses GitHub as its primary system of record for technical deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical program into five core workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling (`threat-modeling/`)**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), focusing on gap analysis across established industry frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog (`design-patterns/`)**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), capturing reusable secure patterns in a problem-context-solution-tradeoffs schema [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Best Practices Guide (`best-practices/`)**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), providing practical practitioner guidance across secrets management, tool invocation, and guardrails [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist (`review-checklist/`)**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), standardizing lightweight security and privacy reviews across deliverables from other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy (`taxonomy/`)**: Transferred to the cross-WG `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` initiative, with Security and Privacy WG representation provided by designated delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group originated the foundation-wide taxonomy effort before handing off centralized ownership to Junjie Bu and the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream on 2026-05-12 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. In June 2026, the AAIF opened the working group's repositories publicly, adopted formal monthly Technical Committee update cadences, and established sub-workstream folders [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Prescriptive security guidance and external framework recommendations for engineering secrets management, tool invocation, guardrails, and forensics in agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, high-level engineering and operational guidance for developers building agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. While the companion Design Patterns Catalog defines concrete architectural implementations, the Best Practices Guide directs builders on recommended strategic approaches and curates pointers to established external security frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide is maintained under `workstreams/best-practices/` within the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` repository, co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

Core topic areas covered include [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]:
- **Secrets Management**: Safe storage, delegation, and ephemeral injection of sensitive credentials into tool and execution boundaries.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Principle of least privilege, input parameter validation, and defense against prompt injection during tool execution.
- **Guardrails**: Implementation of deterministic, non-AI-modifiable boundary controls and policy filters surrounding model inference [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Standardized testing and benchmarking methodologies to audit agent robustness against manipulation and jailbreaks.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Logging, execution trace preservation, and boundary telemetry enabling causal reconstruction of compromised agent actions.
- **Curated External References**: Direct mappings to external industry standards and frameworks (including OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS) to avoid re-deriving established security baselines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation of existing AI security frameworks against agentic-specific threats, covering excessive agency, blast radius, tool invocation, and supply chain integrity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an authoritative analysis deliverable produced by the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), the project benchmarks established industry AI threat frameworks—specifically OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—against agentic failure modes to identify architectural security gaps [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification
The report synthesizes comparative coverage metrics across existing taxonomies and expands beyond baseline AI model vulnerabilities into agentic-specific execution vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:

- **Excessive Agency & Blast Radius**: Inadequate bounding of agent permissions leading to uncontained systemic side effects across infrastructure.
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Exploitation of tool descriptions, parameter manipulation, and unverified API interactions.
- **Memory and Context Poisoning**: Tampering with agent persistent state, prompt context, or retrieval-augmented generation sources.
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion and Sabotage**: Inter-agent manipulation, rogue agent behavior, and degraded alignment in cooperative swarm environments.
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Ambiguities in consent, delegation chains, and credential propagation across autonomous agents.
- **Supply Chain Integrity**: Third-party tool, plugin, and model provenance verification.
- **Commerce and Payment Risk**: Autonomous financial transactions and unchecked economic commitments executed by agents.

The findings from this gap analysis directly inform the `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md` and the upcoming Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

mutations.rationale: Update the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream concept to reflect cross-working-group intake mechanisms, working group delegates, and coordinate review structures.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a foundation-wide initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with creating common terminology, standardizing conceptual domain models, and reconciling conflicting vocabulary across all technical working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream maintains its canonical repository at `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` and coordinates contributions through working group delegates and asynchronous pull request workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream gathers domain terms across working groups to eliminate duplicate definitions and establish cross-discipline consensus [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:

- **Security and Privacy Integration**: Initiated from the original `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` draft deliverable, with ongoing harmonization supported by designated delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, incorporating concepts such as agent capability archetypes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Accuracy and Reliability Alignment**: Integrates modular taxonomy JSON slices across system boundaries, evaluation subjects, failure vocabulary, reliability dimensions, and output metrics from `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md` [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Observability and Traceability Coordination**: Harmonizes core observable execution concepts across orchestration, execution, protocol, and reasoning planes with telemetry models developed by `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History
The taxonomy effort originally began within the Security and Privacy Working Group before being elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative on 2026-05-12 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Junjie Bu was appointed workstream lead on 2026-05-26, and member working groups subsequently appointed formal review delegates to govern intake [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

mutations.rationale: Updates the working group scope and workstreams to document active focus groups, issue tracking on GitHub, and tracing specification planning.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing agent observability conventions, workflow-level trace models, and runtime evaluation frameworks across AI runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing standard telemetry conventions, causal execution tracing models, and runtime evaluation frameworks across multi-agent workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. The working group operates via public GitHub issue tracking, bi-weekly community meetings, and monthly reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

A primary deliverable is establishing an evaluation and decision framework for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to decide whether to adopt existing standards, extend established telemetry protocols, or draft new foundation specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical responsibilities across four specialized focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:

- **LLM Primitives**: Conducts landscape surveys and gap analyses auditing model invocation, token generation, and protocol observability interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agent State and Context**: Evaluates short-term conversation context, state hydration, and persistent memory frameworks across academic and industry implementations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Investigates multi-agent delegation topologies, state handoffs, and inter-agent coordination signals[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Formulates telemetry for dynamic chain-of-thought steps, white-box execution traces, and cognitive planning loops[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

Cross-group coordination includes reviewing core terms with the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) initiative and aligning interface discovery requirements with [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned deliverables tracking to public GitHub issue boards and established bi-weekly community presentation slots[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. Issue #12 established formal planning criteria for the 12-month tracing recommendation milestone[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

mutations.rationale: Clarifies the standard's planning process, evaluation criteria, and decision path between adopting, extending, or creating specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Planned AAIF telemetry specification and causal execution trace standard defining turn boundaries and cross-boundary runtime attribution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardization effort within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) defining causal execution traces, turn boundaries, and state attribution across autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]. As part of the working group's 12-month roadmap, the model follows an evidence-based intake decision framework: adopt an existing industry standard, extend an active upstream effort, or publish an independent specification only if landscape gap analysis proves existing formats insufficient[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation plan establishes explicit criteria before specifying new schemas or protocols[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]:

- **Candidate Comparison**: Benchmarks existing distributed tracing models and emerging AI observability conventions against multi-agent interaction profiles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
- **Evaluation Dimensions**: Assesses fidelity in recording tool invocations, turn boundaries, causal planning graphs, and execution provenance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
- **Workstream Inputs**: Ingests findings from landscape surveys conducted across LLM primitives, state and context management, orchestration, and agentic reasoning focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
- **Upstream Contribution Preference**: Prioritizes contributing extensions to established open-source telemetry projects over maintaining redundant foundation specifications where feasible[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

# Lifecycle History
Tracked under working group Issue #12, the evaluation rubric and milestone decision path were chartered to prevent premature specification authoring prior to completion of the landscape gap analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate ratified charter scope, guiding principles, operational assumptions, and reconciled deliverable structure.

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing benchmarks, failure taxonomies, and architectural recovery patterns for agent accuracy and reliability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation established to define standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices ensuring artificial intelligence agents operate accurately and reliably in enterprise environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco), the group addresses non-deterministic failure modes in agentic systems by classifying failure categories, designing resilience and recovery mechanisms, and defining criteria for autonomous operation versus human intervention[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Charter and Strategic Objectives

The working group focuses on four core strategic objectives[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:

- **Shared Understanding:** Formulating a common vocabulary and taxonomy of reliability and accuracy across agent systems.
- **Measurement and Detection:** Developing reference methodologies to quantify reliability, benchmark accuracy, and detect drift or performance degradation in production environments.
- **Correction Patterns:** Standardizing recovery patterns, delineating actions addressable autonomously from those requiring compensatory workflows or human intervention (such as a [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)).
- **Design Guidance:** Providing architectural guidance that treats reliability and accuracy as primary, proactively engineered properties rather than reactive patches.

# Scope and Boundaries

The working group delineates clear technical boundaries to maintain focus and vendor neutrality[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:

### In Scope
- **Accuracy and Reliability Frameworks:** Categorizing agent failure modes, defining evaluation metrics, and establishing quality thresholds for autonomous workflows.
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns:** Proactive structural mechanisms such as verification loops and grounding against authoritative enterprise data.
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions:** Defining state restoration specifications, rollback semantics, automated compensation mechanisms, and human intervention handoffs.

### Out of Scope
- **Model Internals and Training:** The group assesses agent systems holistically; foundation model pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering are out of scope.
- **Trace and Log Mechanics:** The working group specifies required observability signals and metrics, delegating logging formats and telemetry transport to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
- **Commercial Tooling and Platforms:** Production guardrail products and runtime platforms are excluded in favor of open blueprints and normative standards.
- **Domain Regulatory Policy:** Legal and jurisdiction-specific regulatory mandates are excluded, delegating legal policies to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).

# Operational Assumptions and Dependencies

The ARWG charter operates under explicit assumptions regarding the broader agent ecosystem[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:

- **Operational Predictability:** Agent execution frameworks are expected to provide standardized hooks for trajectory management and state recovery.
- **Immutable Agent Identity:** Evaluation auditability requires persistent, cryptographically verifiable identity standards, coordinating with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Versioning for Reproducibility:** Metrics require frozen, reproducible snapshots encompassing model versions, prompts, and tool configurations.
- **Authoritative Trust Anchors:** High-stakes autonomous tasks require authoritative systems of record against which agent outputs can be systematically verified.

# Deliverables and Lifecycle

The working group organizes its deliverables into a canonical set spanning foundational taxonomy, best practice guides, and normative standards (D1–D6 alongside internal deliverable I1)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]. Planned progression occurs in three phases: Phase 1 establishes definitions and taxonomies (0–3 months), Phase 2 covers architectural best practices and recovery mechanisms (3–6 months), and Phase 3 targets normative verification standards (6+ months)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group tasked with establishing standardized vocabulary, architectural frameworks, benchmark surveys, and evaluation protocols for agentic accuracy and operational reliability [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. The group addresses production failure modes, output quality degradation, and enterprise trust barriers across agent deployments.

Formally chartered on May 15, 2026, the working group operates under the co-chairmanship of Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical roadmap across staged deliverables designed to balance theoretical framing with empirical enterprise needs [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]:

- **D1 (Accuracy & Reliability Taxonomy):** Establishes an architectural framing of terminology, evaluation subjects, output quality metrics, grounding definitions, symptoms, root causes, and recovery mechanisms. D1 directly informs the cross-foundation vocabulary led by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Applied Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey):** Led by Sanjeev Suresh, this track captures operational requirements from B2B enterprise personas (including product managers, deployment operators, evaluators, and data scientists) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. D2 synthesizes industry benchmark gaps and interoperability needs to ground evaluation standards in real-world production constraints.
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol):** Scoped by outputs from the D2 gap analysis, defining concrete benchmarking and evaluation methodology [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Organization and Governance

The working group alternates biweekly main plenary sessions with dedicated deliverable working sessions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. ARWG coordinates actively across foundation groups, appointing dedicated liaisons to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for maintaining a standardized agentic AI vocabulary and publishing a comprehensive ecosystem landscape directory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Its charter targets the elimination of terminology silos and duplicated research across AAIF technical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

The workstream operates as a consensus-driven coordination body comprising nominated delegates and domain editors from each foundation working group, including the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream implements a PR-driven, asynchronous contribution pipeline governed by strict metadata and formatting standards [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]:

- **CNCF-Style Metadata Schema:** Taxonomy definitions and landscape catalog entries adopt standardized schemas inspired by CNCF ecosystem tooling, incorporating two-tier text structures comprising an L0 quick summary and an L1 comprehensive scope description [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Intake and Review Pipeline:** Working group delegates collect raw terminology in shared review spreadsheets to identify duplicate or conflicting definitions prior to pull request submission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]. All definitions must transition into formal GitHub pull requests reviewed by domain editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Standards Alignment and Style Guide:** Terms are actively aligned against international standards bodies such as ISO and NIST, with required documentation for intentional deviations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]. A formal definitions style guide and AI usage policy mandate human oversight for all term contributions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Landscape Federation:** Ecosystem mapping efforts integrate with the interactive landscape catalog at [resources/agentic-ai-landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) and landscape.aif.io [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (`ws-taxonomy-landscape`) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative established to eliminate siloed terminology, prevent duplicative research across working groups, and maintain an ecosystem directory.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates official delegates from member working groups to curate core terms and map agentic technologies.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Architecture / Specification

### Data Schemas and Web Portal
The workstream operates a decoupled data architecture and web portal (`aaif.github.io/ws-taxonomy-landscape`):[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
- **Taxonomy Data Schema**: Formatted according to a SKOS Lite (Simple Knowledge Organization System) schema to model concepts, synonyms, and hierarchical relationships.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Structured using a CNCF-style landscape configuration format categorizing runtimes, frameworks, and tools.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

### Governance and Review Workflow
The workstream relies on an asynchronous, PR-driven GitHub workflow paired with global cross-workgroup term reconciliation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
1. **Delegate Term Ingestion**: Each working group submits 10–20 foundational domain terms to a unified terminology review tracking spreadsheet to de-conflict naming collisions globally.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
2. **Domain Editor Sign-off**: Designated domain editors review and approve proposed definitions to resolve semantic disputes before merging into the central schema.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
3. **TC Reporting Cadence**: Monthly status updates follow a standard template and are submitted to the Technical Committee by the last business day of each month for a 7-day async review window.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting establishing the charter, SKOS Lite schema, and weekly Monday meeting cadence.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
- **2026-06-30**: Initial v1.0 term ingestion completed from almost all member working groups, web portal CI/CD deployed, and unified conflict tracking launched.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# References

- [ws-taxonomy-landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape)
- Related Governance: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- Related Standards: [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)

# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (`wg-observability-and-traceability`) defines standardized telemetry conventions, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and execution evidence structures across AI agent workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group coordinates research across LLM primitives, agent runtime execution, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Group Structure
The working group organizes technical deliverables into focused tracks that report progress back to the wider group:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Consolidated focus group evaluating boundary protocol calls, tool interactions, and underlying model invocations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Focus group covering agent-to-agent coordination, orchestration tracing, and swarm communication topologies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **Agentic State, Context, and Reasoning**: Focus group examining memory provenance, context assembly, and intermediate thought step inspection.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

### Deliverables and Cross-WG Alignment
- **Use Case & Gap Analysis**: Formulating empirical use cases and landscape gap analyses to benchmark current observability tooling capabilities.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Developing standardized turn boundaries and causal trace representations for asynchronous multi-step execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Direct participation in the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to standardize observability terms.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)**: Interfacing with ARD catalogs and dynamic registries for agent capability resolution and trust manifests.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-29**: Submitted June 2026 monthly report detailing focus group charter kickoffs, GitHub-first issue tracking migration, and initial gap analysis PRs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **2026-07-09**: Decided to merge LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups to resolve attendance overlap, and reviewed the ARD specification proposal.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

# Overview

The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (`wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory`) evaluates international regulatory frameworks, policy obligations, and risk-management standards affecting autonomous AI agents.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454] Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates legal requirements into technical specifications for compliance, liability tracing, and agent accountability.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Architecture / Specification

### Landscape Assessment and Comparative Policy Mapping
The working group systematically catalogs policy instruments across jurisdictions to identify requirements applicable to autonomous agent systems:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]
- **Framework Cataloging**: Mapping existing AI risk frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act) against autonomous operational risks.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]
- **Comparative Gap Analysis**: Assessing disparities between static AI risk guidance and dynamic agentic behaviors, including unauthorized delegation, non-deterministic state change, and boundary crossing.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]
- **Policy Baseline Identification**: Formulating objective operational baselines against which agent compliance and control efficacy can be formally audited.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-01**: Delivered initial 3-month milestone completing landscape assessment of existing agentic AI policy frameworks, standards, and best practices; initiated comparative gap analysis sprint.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

- Related Patterns: [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), [Hard Constraint Gate](../patterns/hard-constraint-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Resource Discovery
proposed_concept.description: Decentralized specification and discovery architecture enabling agents to find and verify AI resources via static catalogs and dynamic registries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification is a decentralized architecture enabling AI agents to discover, evaluate, and verify tools, models, skills, and remote capabilities.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a] Developed in collaboration across industry partners, ARD pairs static capability indexing with dynamic query endpoints and cryptographic trust manifests to prevent rogue tool execution and untrusted capability invocation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

# Architecture / Specification

### Dual Discovery Modalities
ARD defines two complementary mechanisms for discovering agentic resources:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
1. **Catalog (Static Indexing)**: Declarative, machine-readable manifests publishing static metadata, schema signatures, natural language search keywords, and security parameters for offline indexing and compilation.
2. **Registry (Dynamic Service)**: Active query interface providing REST APIs for dynamic runtime lookup, health state, latency metrics, and real-time capability routing.

### Trust and Identification Layer
To ensure resource authenticity, ARD embeds decentralized identity standards:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **SPIFFE Support**: Cryptographic workload identity verification for containerized agent tools and endpoints.
- **ANS Integration**: Compatibility with Agent Network Standards (ANS) for inter-agent routing and capability discovery.
- **Trust Manifests**: Signed resource attestation records validating publisher provenance and security posture before admission to runtime contexts.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-09**: Presented to the Observability & Traceability Working Group following a joint multi-company announcement; alignment identified with agent identity and registry focus areas.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

# References

- Related Working Groups: [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- Related Standards: [Agent Network Protocol](agent-network-protocol.md), [Agent Skills](agent-skills.md)
- Related Resources: [MCP Gateway Registry](../resources/mcp-gateway-registry.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), dedicated to establishing security architectures, threat mitigation models, design patterns, and baseline security best practices for autonomous agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. The group interfaces directly with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through monthly reports and coordinates cross-ecosystem security alignment with external bodies including OWASP, AARM, and FINOS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group executes its charter through five structured workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, benchmarking existing frameworks against agentic-specific threat surfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing prescriptive developer implementation guidance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating reusable architectural patterns for securing agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing verifiable security evaluation criteria across AAIF deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

### Operating and Reporting Procedures

The working group adheres to formal reporting obligations governed by the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:
- Monthly status reports must be submitted as pull requests by the final business day of each reporting month[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- The TC review window closes 7 calendar days after submission, after which reports are merged upon TC sign-off or window closure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- Reports evaluate four charter Success Metrics: Adoption, Quality, Community (averaging ~27 attendees per meeting), and Timeliness[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-30**: Transitioned from formation to execution; established five active workstreams and submitted June 2026 monthly report to the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **2026-07-07**: Completed initial drafts of the threat modeling gap analysis deliverable and security best practices guide, began design pattern catalog formatting, and evaluated external alignments with OWASP, AARM, and FINOS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an Agentic AI Foundation cross-cutting initiative led by Junjie Bu, responsible for unifying vocabulary, classification schemas, and ecosystem mapping across all AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. The workstream operates through designated delegates embedded in each domain-specific working group, curating terminology to eliminate conceptual collisions across specifications and reference architectures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream structures terminology consolidation through an iterative, pull-request-driven and spreadsheet-backed intake workflow[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]:

- **Unified Working Spreadsheet**: A central review sheet aggregates candidate terms submitted across working groups (~250 terms total), recording WG relevance and delegate ownership[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Target Scope for v1.0 Release**: Each working group selects 10 to 20 key terms to establish the foundational release baseline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Consensus Cull and Debate Process**: Terms are categorized as universal, domain-specific, debate-worthy (e.g. "identity", "agent" vs "bot"), or marked in a consensus-driven "cull" column if they do not provide distinct value to agentic conversations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Contentious terms are surfaced in community Discord channels before resolution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Universal Boundary Terms**: Core terms categorized as universal are prioritized at the top of the vocabulary taxonomy to provide consistent foundations for downstream working group specifications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting reviewing initial charter and PR-driven workflow[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-06-22**: Formally confirmed charter status, welcomed working group delegates, and stood up the shared cross-WG spreadsheet[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-07-06**: Entered the execution review phase; established consensus cull criteria, prioritized universal terms, created front-matter instructions, and extended sync meetings to one hour[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation of existing AI security frameworks against agentic-specific threats, covering excessive agency, multi-turn state corruption, and tool hijacking.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a technical deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. It assesses the extent to which established cybersecurity and AI risk frameworks—specifically MITRE ATLAS, OWASP AI/LLM Top 10, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF)—address threat vectors unique to autonomous, tool-executing AI agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification

The gap analysis evaluates framework capabilities across eight identified technical domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:

- **Baseline Framework Synthesis**: Maps existing controls from MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF to determine where legacy paradigms handle agent risk versus where fundamental coverage gaps persist[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agent-Specific Vulnerabilities**: Analyzes autonomous execution vulnerabilities including indirect prompt injection via tools, dynamic capability escalation, tool-call rug-pull attacks, and multi-turn state poisoned memory[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Control Recommendations**: Proposes defensive architectural gates, runtime attestation mechanisms, and boundary verification criteria to remediate uncovered framework deficiencies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-30**: Initial gap analysis draft presented and endorsed for depth and formatting in the June monthly TC update[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **2026-07-07**: Fernando Lucktemberg submitted Deliverable 4 covering the complete eight-area gap review for ingestion into the working group repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Prescriptive security guidance and implementation recommendations for secrets management, tool sandboxing, input sanitization, and runtime attestation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a developer- and practitioner-facing implementation guideline maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. It provides technical standards and design practices for securing autonomous agents at execution time, addressing tool credential boundaries, untrusted payload sanitization, and execution containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

The guide focuses on tangible mitigation practices across key integration boundaries:

- **Secrets Management**: Isolating API keys, service credentials, and execution tokens from prompt contexts and model reflection logs.
- **Tool Execution Sandboxing**: Enforcing strict host isolation, cgroup restrictions, and capability filtering on tools invoked by agent runtimes.
- **Runtime Verification and Attestation**: Leveraging signed tool manifests and runtime attestations to prevent tool-substitution and rug-pull attacks during multi-step execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Output Validation**: Implementing deterministic evaluation gates prior to committing irreversible downstream side effects.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-30**: Initial content drafting commenced following workstream kickoff[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **2026-07-07**: First complete draft submitted for working group review, with bi-weekly review meetings scheduled[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream (`ws-taxonomy-landscape`) is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation established to harmonize shared agentic AI terminology and maintain a unified ecosystem architecture map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Rather than having individual technical working groups develop conflicting vocabularies or duplicate research, the workstream provides federated terminology arbitration and centralized landscape curation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Organization and Governance
The workstream was formally chartered on June 21, 2026 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. It is led by Chair Junjie Bu (Google) and Co-Chair Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. The group convenes weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT and coordinates via the `ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io` mailing list and `#ws-taxonomy-landscape` Discord channel [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

The workstream operates under a federated governance model where each technical working group—including `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` and `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`—nominates active delegates who serve as domain editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]. The workstream prioritizes consolidation over creation by reconciling vocabularies submitted by domain working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture and Deliverables
The workstream manages two core public assets:
- **Shared Taxonomy:** Curated vocabulary terms standardized using a SKOS-Lite metadata schema containing fields such as `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Ecosystem Landscape Map:** An interactive, CNCF-style ecosystem map driven by `landscape.yml`, categorizing open-source runtimes, protocols, security tooling, and frameworks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

Automated CI/CD workflows assemble and deploy the interactive Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape web portal to GitHub Pages on every push to the default branch [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group serves as an operational bridge between emerging global AI public policy developments and the technical architectures of agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group translates statutory and standard-setting requirements into actionable engineering guidance and control baselines.

# Governance and Operations
The working group is led by appointed leadership serving terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]
- Chair: Ryan Hagemann (IBM)
- Co-Chair: Deborah Eng (JP Morgan Chase)

Working group meetings occur bi-weekly on Thursdays at 10:00 AM PT on the Linux Foundation LFX platform.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] Public discussions and collaboration take place via the mailing list (`wg-governance-risk-regulatory@lists.aaif.io`) and the dedicated AAIF Discord community channel.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] Participation adheres to the [Linux Foundation Antitrust Policy](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and requires individual neutrality independent of corporate representation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

# Cross-Foundation Initiatives
The group collaborates across peer AAIF bodies, including [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and the cross-cutting [Taxonomy & Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream, ensuring consistent regulatory terminology and control definitions across agent lifecycles.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows conducted by autonomous AI agents on behalf of consumers, merchants, and automated software platforms.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563] The group provides vendor-neutral reference architectures and interoperability guidance across the entire transaction lifecycle while deliberately refraining from authoring competing proprietary commerce protocols.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group covers end-to-end agentic transactional interactions, including:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- Product and merchant discovery mechanisms.
- Dynamic negotiation protocols and constraints.
- Checkout workflows, payment orchestration, and credential delegation.
- Post-purchase lifecycle events such as order fulfillment tracking, refunds, and dispute resolution.

Findings and recommended harmonization paths are submitted upstream to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to drive industry convergence.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Governance and Operations
The group's leadership was appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members for the term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- Chair: Ilya Grigorik (Shopify)

Working group sessions are convened bi-weekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT via LFX Zoom, with public communications routed through `wg-agentic-commerce@lists.aaif.io` and the AAIF Discord server.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes a shared workflow execution model, standardized operational primitives, and common semantics for agentic AI systems across diverse runtime environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56] Operating under a charter approved on May 13, 2026 and revised on July 23, 2026, the working group standardizes how autonomous agents interact with external services, deterministic orchestration engines, and human decision-makers.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Scope and Technical Focus
The working group's scope is organized across three primary domains:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Defining universal [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) (tasks, tool calls, branching, handoffs, subagent spawning, and retries), standardized structural representations, and execution ordering semantics across frameworks.
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution**: Formulating patterns for multi-hour or multi-day executions, workflow state persistence, replayability, idempotency, and audit logs of step outcomes and decision points (distinguished from runtime telemetry managed by [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)).
- **Tool Invocation and External Coordination**: Specifying interoperable patterns for agent orchestration across APIs, CLIs, and external enterprise software.

# Governance and Leadership
The working group is co-chaired by:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- Chair: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)
- Co-Chair: Adam Seligman (Workato)

The working group coordinates closely with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and maintains open deliverables in its official repository (`aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration`).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group formulates technical threat models, secure operational patterns, and privacy standards to protect autonomous agents and their execution environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91] The working group collaborates with external security consortia such as OWASP while driving core foundation deliverables under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Active Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical production across dedicated workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, providing systematic threat evaluations for agent components.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, authoring baseline implementation standards for secrets management and sandboxing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, cataloging architectural controls across agent runtime boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing cross-cutting review criteria and evaluating scope overlaps with peer groups such as [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent the group to align security and privacy terms (such as session replay risks and constraints) with the foundation-wide catalog.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Technical Architecture
The group evaluates attack surfaces—such as prompt injection and Model Context Protocol (MCP) cache and tool poisoning—by disaggregating monolithic agent stacks into distinct functional archetypes: input/output channels, core language models, conversation state history, and tool/prompt orchestration components.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

proposed_concept.title: Action Record
proposed_concept.description: Tamper-evident, content-private, and independently verifiable record proving what an agent executed for counterparties, auditors, and courts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An Action Record is a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of a single consequential action taken by an agent.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] It provides cryptographic and evidentiary proof answering "what did this agent verifiably do?" for counterparties, auditors, or legal authorities, distinct from internal operational logs.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Boundary Distinctions
The Action Record occupies a distinct technical boundary from observability telemetry and identity tokens:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Observability and Tracing:** Internal execution telemetry answers "what is my agent doing?" for the operator managing execution flow.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] Action records answer "what did this agent verifiably do?" for an external recipient or verifying counterparty.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Identity and Authorization:** Identity artifacts and OAuth tokens authorize an agent to act, whereas the action record proves what specific consequence occurred under that authority, maintaining content privacy through selective disclosure.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Consent Receipts:** Consent artifacts establish authorization granted by a principal, whereas an action record binds that consent and delegation chain to the executed state changes.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Architecture / Specification
Within the [WG Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) framework, Action Records incorporate several architectural requirements:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Tamper Evidence:** Cryptographically signed and structured so that post-execution modifications invalidate verification proofs.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Content Privacy and Selective Disclosure:** Verifiers can confirm that an authorized action took place within valid parameters without exposing sensitive internal payloads or operational context.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Delegation Binding:** Binds actions back through the agent delegation chain to ensure permissions do not exceed initiating user entitlements.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards and reference architectures for agent identity, delegation, authorization, and verifiable records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral standards, architectural patterns, and foundational taxonomy for agent identity, verifiable delegation, and execution trust.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] The working group is chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Sub-Working Groups and Scope
The working group organizes technical delivery across three specialized tracks:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Taxonomy:** Defines normative terms including [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md), Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop, enforcing functional separation between operator observability and counterparty audit verification.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Reference Architecture:** Develops a component specification encompassing Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] A foundational architectural assumption is that delegated sub-agents cannot hold permissions exceeding their parent delegator, which cannot exceed initiating user permissions.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Critical Use Cases:** Evaluates agent lifecycle patterns across Internal, B2B, and B2C operational scenarios spanning naming, dynamic per-request authorization, selective disclosure, and principal-attested revocation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# External Inputs and Proposals
The group incorporates industry frameworks into its reference architectures and formal proposals to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md):[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Baseline:** Proposes profiling OAuth 2.0 as the normative standard for how agents present authorization, token formatting, scope expressions, and delegation chains across platforms, while backend policy enforcement remains autonomous to internal systems.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace (SAW):** Evaluates NVIDIA's reference design, including its four-layer identity model (user/sponsor, workspace device, logical agent, tool call), delegation records, OpenShell policy enforcement sandbox, and Open Delegation and Identity Standard (ODIS).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **OpenID Foundation Collaboration:** Assesses alignment with the OpenID Foundation whitepaper on Identity Management for Agentic AI regarding agent identity and token delegation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing protocol-neutral interfaces, capability models, and trust signal frameworks for agentic transactions and commerce workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393] The group is chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group operates under an approved charter focusing on open interoperability across six core phases of agent-driven commerce:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393] discovery, delegated authority, checkout, payment, fraud signaling, and post-purchase.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

Key initiatives include:
- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map:** The primary deliverable cataloging standardized interfaces and boundary signals across participant roles (shopper, agent platform, merchant, payment provider, and risk systems).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Payment Abstraction Model:** Evaluates payment execution around three reusable concepts: handler, instrument, and credential.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393] The group analyzes differences between static payment capability discovery and transaction-specific eligibility, delegated tokenization, and wallet attachments.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Cross-Protocol Analysis:** Evaluates payment handler composition models across the [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) (ACP), Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), and Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), analyzing MPP's challenge-credential-receipt flow.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Fraud and Trust Signaling:** Investigates how fraud and risk signals propagate across merchant and payment provider boundaries, separating agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
