proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing protocol-neutral capability maps, lifecycle handoffs, and trust signals across agent-driven commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to provide a protocol-neutral framing, capability map, and gap analysis for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents conducting commercial transactions across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase lifecycles.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760] Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses merchant integration fragmentation, protocol interoperability, and bounded trust signals without prescribing a single competing commerce protocol.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]

# Scope and Deliverables

The working group focuses on external commerce interfaces rather than internal platform implementations.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760] Its primary activities encompass:

- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**: Decomposing commercial interactions across four phases—discovery (feed-based vs live merchant querying, source discovery, freshness, trust), checkout and negotiation (stateful merchant-authoritative negotiations, transport bindings, human handoff), payment (credentials, instruments, dynamic eligibility), and post-purchase (order observation vs state mutations such as returns, refunds, cancellations, and disputes).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Protocol Comparative Analysis**: Evaluating existing specifications and protocols—including ACP, UCP, AP2, MPP, and x402—against capability requirements and transport bindings.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Fraud and Trust Signals**: Analyzing signal visibility across agent, platform, merchant, payment provider, and risk systems to distinguish agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk while minimizing indiscriminate data sharing.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

The group coordinates closely with cross-cutting AAIF efforts, specifically [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Launched initial survey of agentic commerce challenges, identifying friction points in discoverability, execution, delegated authority, and merchant burdens.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]
- **March 2026**: Established a lifecycle-oriented methodology across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]
- **April 2026**: Formulated working group charter and advanced capability mapping for discovery and stateful checkout negotiations.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **June 2026**: Evaluated fraud mitigation and signal provenance across distributed multi-party transaction boundaries.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]
- **July 2026**: Began post-purchase workflow evaluations (order visibility vs state changes) and assessed agent wallet integrations and payment mandates.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative dedicated to standardizing core agentic AI terminology via a unified taxonomy and maintaining an open catalog of the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103] Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates conceptual definitions across foundation working groups to eliminate ambiguity and build consensus.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

# Operations and Review Methodology

The workstream operates on a structured review pipeline evaluating term submissions across universal, domain-specific, and working group categorizations:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

- **Two-Stage Admission Process**: Terms undergo initial admission before entering detailed definition drafting, deferring detailed fields (`definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm`) until initial inclusion consensus is reached.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]
- **Working Group Harmonization**: Sequential reviews resolve naming and semantic divergence across working groups, tracking contested terms where groups hold differing definitions (such as `Agent`) in a dedicated debate backlog.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]
- **Artifact Repositories**: Candidate definitions and debate logs migrate from collaborative review spreadsheets into public pull requests and portal releases to preserve discussion history alongside published taxonomy entries.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Transitioned from term collection to active group arbitration, reviewing 46 terms across universal and [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md) domains.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]
- **August 2026**: Merged PR #33 shipping the initial 13 admitted taxonomy terms to the public portal and progressed review backlog to 67 terms evaluated.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Pattern Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized structure, header conventions, invariant definitions, and runtime mapping matrix for AAIF workflow patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Workflow Pattern Template standardizes the authoring of workflow patterns within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054]. Under the [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](../guidelines/job-oriented-architecture-model.md), patterns represent independently adoptable, context-free solutions to recurring workflow sub-problems, distinct from complete [reference architectures](../guidelines/reference-architecture-template.md) that compose them [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

# Architecture / Specification
Every pattern document authored for the working group must adhere to standard section conventions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054]:

- **Naming Convention**: Pattern names must name the architectural fix rather than a particular use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Header Metadata**: Required metadata lines including `Solves`, `Used in` (linking to reference architectures), `Requires capabilities` (identifying necessary capability roles), and `Related patterns` (linking to complementary patterns such as [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Problem & Why This Is Hard**: Formulates the recurring sub-problem recognized by practitioners and lists the competing engineering tensions that prevent naive solutions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Solution Shape**: Context-free diagram or structure restricted to 2–4 boxes without vendor, runtime, or use-case specifics; solutions requiring more boxes must be structured as reference architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Invariants**: Core guarantees that must hold across any implementation, expressed in product-agnostic terms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Failure Modes When Violated**: Concrete breakdowns and operational hazards corresponding directly to each violated invariant [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Implementation Approaches Table**: Illustrative runtime implementations categorized along a pattern-specific differentiation axis (such as execution families or enforcement boundaries), documenting the mechanism, platform-provided capabilities, and developer-added controls [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].
- **Known Uses Outside Agents**: Pre-LLM historical precedents demonstrating the pattern was discovered rather than invented, noting the conceptual delta introduced by autonomous agents [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural decision record organizing workflow reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than agent topology or agent count.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model is an architectural decision adopted by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to structure reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural agent counts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. It formalizes the distinction between reusable [workflow patterns](../guidelines/workflow-pattern-template.md) and complete reference architectures composed of capabilities, boundaries, guarantees, and exit states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Architecture / Specification
The decision establishes explicit criteria for organizing and reviewing workflow architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]:

- **Practitioner Jobs Over Topology**: Generic single-agent and multi-agent workflow scaffolds are replaced because agent count is a design outcome rather than an operational need [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. Single-agent and multi-agent descriptors remain structural characteristics within architectures rather than top-level categorization axes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Reference Architecture Composition**: Reference architectures provide a complete composition of reusable patterns, required capabilities, boundary controls, guarantees, and exit states for an explicit operational job, such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Pattern Separation**: Patterns serve as independently adoptable solutions to individual recurring problems, retaining their own invariants, failure modes, and implementation approaches [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Scenario Validation**: Real-world use cases validate reference architectures; scenarios that fail to fit indicate a missing variant, an uncaptured pattern, or an entirely distinct job [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Lifecycle History
The decision was formally proposed as an Architecture Decision Record on 2026-07-20 in the Workflows and Process Integration repository [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. It deprecated generic multi-agent templates in favor of job-specific architectures such as [bounded-autonomous-remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, execution trace specifications, and runtime observability frameworks across agent boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]. The working group collaborates with external standards bodies such as the IETF and IRTF, as well as peer-to-peer networking initiatives, to define verifiable telemetry and causal execution models for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
Key workstreams and active initiatives include [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]:

- **Agentic Trace Model & Telemetry**: Defining application-layer interoperability across tracing libraries and formalizing recommendations for the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) core specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Composable Trust Blueprint**: Developing joint trust architectures combining Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) using CBOR42 encoding to decouple telemetry semantics from cryptographic proofs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Peer-to-Peer Observability**: Collaborating with LibP2P and GossipSub implementations to monitor distributed agent throughput, latency, and discovery metadata across Python and Go runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability Models**: Modeling boundary telemetry propagation and Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) observability across agent boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Focus Groups**: Maintaining dedicated working tracks for State and Context, Orchestration and Coordination, and universal taxonomy curation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation established to define common workflow models, shared vocabularies, and architectural design patterns for multi-framework agent systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]. Its mission centers on enabling interoperable agent workflows that operate reliably across heterogenous tools, runtimes, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Operational Structure
The working group is led by appointed chairs serving an initial term from March 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]:
- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)
- **Co-Chair**: Adam Seligman (Workato)

The group convenes biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM PT and conducts public technical exchanges via its mailing list (`wg-workflows-process-integration@lists.aaif.io`) and official Discord channel[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Key Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across several interrelated workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]:
- **Taxonomy**: Establishes a foundational shared vocabulary (`terms.md`) to disambiguate workflow state, transitions, and execution concepts across specifications[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Reference Architectures**: Defines concrete architectural patterns—such as [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and [Single Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)—implementing governed execution boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Formulates empirical business and engineering scenarios validating workflow abstractions against real-world production constraints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

# Related Concepts

- [Workflow Primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)
- [Workflow Pattern Template](../guidelines/workflow-pattern-template.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open standards, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for tracing, observing, and evaluating agentic AI behavior across distributed runtime boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]. Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group coordinates technical deliverables spanning protocol-level telemetry, agent state transitions, and causal execution tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Operational Structure
In July 2026, the working group restructured its operational execution model by consolidating five focus groups into three active focus tracks to streamline technical participation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability** (Lead: Zayne Turner): Focuses on protocol-level telemetry propagation, cross-boundary gap analysis, and observability for [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) and skill execution state[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination** (Lead: Ty Smith): Focuses on telemetry and causal propagation models for multi-agent delegation, orchestration topologies, and cross-agent communication[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Agentic State & Context** (Lead: Govindaraj): Integrates agent reasoning and execution state observability, developing landscape analyses and gap models for contextual memory and decision progression[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Key Initiatives
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md): Dedicated recommendation track led by Matthew Lee to specify standardized execution traces across turn boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md): Systematic analysis of telemetry propagation across tool, agent, and gateway protocol boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- Cross-WG Taxonomy Coordination: Collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to standardize observability-specific terminology[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Prescriptive security guidance and implementation recommendations covering secrets management, tool sandboxing, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides engineering guidelines, threat mitigations, and implementation controls for securing autonomous agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. Developed as Deliverable 4 within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide organizes architectural recommendations around a structured failure-pattern, control, and decision-framework model[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide delineates prescriptive defensive controls across five core operational domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
1. **Secrets Management**: Securing credential access, mitigating key exfiltration during model context construction, and isolating runtime credentials.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Defending tool integration pipelines, addressing supply-chain risks, and securing Model Context Protocol (MCP) server interactions.
3. **Guardrails**: Implementing runtime boundary filters, prompt-injection defenses, and output policy enforcement.
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Systematically benchmarking defensive posture, red-teaming tool invocations, and validating policy enforcement prior to deployment.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Preserving tamper-evident execution logs and capturing agent decision histories to reconstruct security incidents.

The specification includes a curated tool reference matrix evaluating industry security tooling by maturity, implementation cost, and deployment constraints[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Boundary and Scope Exclusions
Identity architectures and delegated authorization standards (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693 OAuth Token Exchange) are explicitly excluded from this guide's scope and remain the jurisdiction of the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Related Concepts
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)
- [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and defense-in-depth guidance for autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to analyzing threat models, security design patterns, and defense-in-depth principles across autonomous agent architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group establishes technical consensus on vulnerabilities unique to agentic workflows, such as indirect prompt injection, unconstrained tool use, rug-pull vector exploitation, and credential exposure across multi-agent environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

The working group coordinates with external standards efforts including ETSI TC SAI and OWASP, and reports monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical production into five primary workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, this workstream performs comparative gap reviews across established cybersecurity frameworks—including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF—to develop an agent-native threat assessment methodology.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] Initial drafts are tracked in [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, this workstream develops prescriptive implementation guidance covering safe tool execution, credential isolation, and memory boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] Initial content is cataloged under [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, this initiative documents reusable architectural design patterns addressing containment, boundary verification, and privilege separation in agent runtime topologies.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, this track produces actionable security verification criteria for architectural templates and project intakes submitted across AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Liaised by Jay White and Katherine Druckman, aligning working group security and privacy concepts with the broader foundation glossary managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

# Lifecycle History
Formed in mid-2026 under the AAIF working group governance model, the working group moved from initial chartering to active deliverable execution in June and July 2026, transitioning early collaborative drafts from working documents into formal repository pull requests.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body standardizing telemetry, causal event tracing, and operational visibility across autonomous agent execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff] The group develops vendor-neutral trace formats, spans, and semantic conventions—including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)—to capture multi-turn reasoning, tool invocations, multi-agent delegation, and distributed state transitions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

All deliverable tracking and governance decisions are managed openly through GitHub, adhering to documented working methods that ensure transparent tracking for community contributors and monthly status reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

# Architecture / Specification

## Operating Cadence and Governance
The working group follows a transparent cadence centered on GitHub as the single durable source of truth:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Pre-Meeting Review**: Issue triage scanning for blocked work, stale next steps, and agenda items before each working group session.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Session Minutes**: Recording actionable decisions and tracking assignments directly linked back to repository issues and pull requests.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Post-Meeting Updates**: Reconciling issue ownership and tracking status so non-attendees can follow execution state.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Monthly Reporting**: Synthesizing merged deliverables, open pull requests, and recorded decisions into regular reports for the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

## Work Item Tracking Model
Each deliverable or coordination thread is tracked via structured issue templates requiring an explicit outcome, assignable workstream, owner, concrete next step, and acceptance criteria.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50] Work items strictly cycle through standardized status terms:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `needs owner`: Valid task needing an assigned driver.
- `scoping`: Boundaries, outcomes, and inputs are under active definition.
- `in progress`: Active drafting, research, or cross-group coordination.
- `ready for review`: Awaiting critical review or stakeholder consensus.
- `blocked`: Progress impeded by missing dependencies, external reviews, or explicit decisions.
- `done`: Merged, completed, or formally closed.

## Pull Request and Publication Standards
Technical specifications and documentation enter the repository via pull requests that link tracking issues, identify concrete review focus areas, outline remaining follow-ups, and assert freshness markers for living documents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b2496e80299b-e136231b] While early exploratory drafting may occur in external collaborative documents, durable artifacts are migrated to GitHub for formal review and archival publication.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

# Lifecycle History
The group established its formal working methods and contribution templates to provide transparent execution tracking as its core telemetry and trace model specifications progressed through the AAIF project lifecycle.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and cross-working group privacy controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) advances the Agentic AI Foundation mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group develops open threat models, shared architectural design patterns, security guidelines, and review checklists that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for a term extending from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. Meetings occur biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into specialized workstreams and cross-group initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates established enterprise frameworks against agentic-specific threat surfaces, producing the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Best Practices**: Authors prescriptive implementation guidance in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), scoping application-level controls and human-user-agent interactions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Catalogs defensive and isolation patterns for agent execution runtimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Develops horizontal evaluation criteria to review deliverables across peer AAIF bodies for security and privacy risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Taxonomy and Terminology**: Coordinates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define agent-specific security, guardrail, and constraint terms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

Under governance decisions adopted in August 2026, the working group operates an autonomous review and merge model: pull requests within the working group's approved charter may be reviewed and merged directly by the group without requiring prior approval from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), with progress reported via monthly TC reports [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. All meeting recordings, notes, repositories, and Discord discussion channels default to open public access [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its initial orientation on February 17, 2026, and its formal charter was unanimously approved on April 14, 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]. In July 2026, the working group requested TC guidance to formalize external liaisons with OWASP, AARM, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ACS group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10]. Workstream overlaps regarding identity attribution and authorization are coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation of existing security frameworks against agentic AI threats, covering OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF, STRIDE, and PASTA.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis evaluates traditional software and contemporary AI security frameworks against the novel attack surfaces introduced by autonomous, tool-calling agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable identifies areas where existing threat taxonomies fail to capture agent autonomy, recursive delegation, and external environment mutations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis assesses the coverage and limitations of major frameworks when applied to multi-turn agentic workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:

- **OWASP**: Evaluates LLM Top 10 and related project coverage against non-deterministic execution and dynamic tool chaining [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **MITRE ATLAS**: Maps adversarial tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) targeting AI artifacts to multi-agent environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **MAESTRO and NIST AI RMF**: Analyzes systemic risk management profiles and AI trust characteristics across agent execution lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **STRIDE and PASTA Alignment**: Evaluates how traditional engineering threat methodologies (STRIDE and PASTA) can be extended to model agent-specific trust boundaries and threat motivations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Protocol and Interface Boundaries**: Incorporates threat vectors across tool integration protocols, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification and User Interface / Human-User-Agent (HUA) interaction models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
The deliverable was authored by Fernando Lucktemberg as a Draft v0.1 pull request in the Security and Privacy Working Group in July 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10]. In August 2026, the workstream scheduled biweekly cadence meetings and incorporated feedback regarding UI/HUA boundary concerns and newly published MCP specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Prescriptive implementation recommendations covering agent tool execution boundaries, secrets management, and human-user-agent oversight.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides prescriptive engineering standards and operational recommendations for designing, deploying, and monitoring autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide translates threat modeling analysis into concrete deployment safeguards and execution constraints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification
The best practices guide addresses key security domains across the agent lifecycle [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:

- **Human Accountability and Execution Separation**: Establishes that while autonomous agents perform actions and invoke tools, ultimate responsibility and legal accountability remain with human principals [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Human-User-Agent (HUA) Considerations**: Covers interface protections, intent confirmation prompts, and boundary integrity when agents interact through direct UI or user proxy channels [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Identity and Authorization Boundaries**: Identifies authentication requirements for agents and service accounts; foundational identity primitives and credential delegation models are co-developed with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Tool and Environment Defense**: Guides the containment of tool execution, input validation on external tool outputs, and prevention of supply-chain attacks in agent plugin ecosystems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
The guide's initial skeleton draft was submitted via pull request in July 2026 by Fernando Lucktemberg [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Workstream revisions in August 2026 expanded coverage to include Human-User-Agent interaction controls and established formal handoffs to the Identity and Trust Working Group for identity management sections [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining technical project admission requirements, the Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus stages, and annual review processes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy governs how open technical projects formally join and progress through the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Effective March 18, 2026, the policy outlines project admission criteria, expectations across maturity stages, and the annual review process that evaluates advancement, retention, or retirement of projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification
The lifecycle policy specifies mandatory submission requirements and four defined project stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:

## Submission Requirements
Projects seeking intake must file a submission via the AAIF project proposals repository [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. The submission must include:
- Mission alignment and relationship to existing AAIF technical initiatives [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Adoption evidence and documented use cases [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Assigned Technical Committee sponsor (if identified) [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- An OSI-approved permissive open-source license [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Publicly accessible repository, automated validation/delivery mechanisms, issue tracker, and documented governance processes (`GOVERNANCE.md`) [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Maintainer roster, dependency licenses, and infrastructure requirements [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Project Stages
1. **Sandbox Stage**: Entry-level stage for experimental, early-stage, or emerging initiatives requiring foundation mentorship and community building [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
2. **Growth Stage**: Intermediate stage for projects demonstrating active adoption, functional release processes, and growing contributor diversity [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
3. **Impact Stage**: Mature stage for production-ready, mission-critical projects demonstrating ecosystem stability, widespread deployment, and sustained multi-organizational governance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
4. **Emeritus Stage**: End-of-lifecycle state for projects that have concluded active development, completed their objectives, or transitioned maintenance elsewhere [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Annual Review Process
Project health, progression, and stage status are systematically re-evaluated through an annual review conducted by the Technical Committee [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Lifecycle History
The Project Lifecycle Policy became effective on March 18, 2026, establishing a standardized framework across all incoming and graduated AAIF open-source technical projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing inside hardware-attested environments while intentionally keeping agent execution outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime is an architectural security pattern for agentic deployments where infrastructure operators sit within the threat model, isolating the policy decision point and evidence signer within a hardware-isolated environment while gating data release on appraisal by an independent verifier[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Crucially, the pattern keeps agent logic itself outside the trusted execution boundary to prevent attacker-influenced prompt inputs from compromising the trusted computing base[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

Introduced within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design-patterns workstream, the pattern addresses trusted execution environments (TEEs) and hardware attestation, leaving zero-knowledge proofs and encrypted vector databases for separate specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern specifies four mandatory core elements along with the operational failures resulting from omitting them[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
1. **Isolate Enforcement Point Outside Agent Logic**: The policy decision point (PDP) and enforcement mechanisms reside inside the hardware-isolated boundary, but the agent runtime remains outside. Because agent code regularly consumes adversarial, untrusted inputs, placing agent execution inside the enclave would unnecessarily expand the trusted computing base (TCB) with the component most vulnerable to subversion[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation and Cryptographic Binding**: Evidence signing keys are generated inside the hardware boundary and cryptographically bound to execution evidence[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Omitting this enables rogue or external components to spoof execution claims.
3. **Policy Sealing and Measurement Release**: Policies are sealed to specific hardware and software measurements, releasing secrets only upon successful appraisal[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Omitting measurement sealing allows unverified or altered policy bundles to execute.
4. **Independent Per-Unit-of-Work Appraisal**: An independent verifier appraises cryptographically bound evidence per unit of work before data release[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

## Platform and Standards Scope
The specification is vendor-neutral and designed across multiple confidential computing architectures without mandating a specific platform[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
- **Hardware Targets**: AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Software-Only Emulation**: A legitimate software-only mode is specified to facilitate development, CI, and conformance testing for environments lacking confidential computing hardware[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Standards Alignment**: Conforms to IETF RATS (RFC 9334), CBOR Web Token (RFC 9711), Proof-of-Possession key semantics (RFC 8747), IETF SCITT, and SLSA provenance frameworks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

## Open Questions and Known Limitations
The pattern explicitly highlights several operational trade-offs and open architectural questions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
- **Trust Boundary Placement**: Debates continue on whether certain agent components should ever reside within the enclave or strictly remain external[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Measured Artifact Set**: While static artifacts (system prompts, policy bundles, tool schemas, and model weight digests) are straightforward to measure, dynamic runtime elements such as retrieved context and conversational memory require further lifecycle management standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Catalog Assurance Levels**: Collaboration with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to define shared assurance tiers across signed, attested, and transparency-anchored evidence[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Threat Model Boundaries**: The pattern does not mitigate prompt injection, side-channel leakage, uninstrumented tool actions, or verifier downtime, and introduces operational dependencies on firmware and TCB version floors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill providing automated, read-only first-pass triage of GitHub issues grounded in local repository code and historical review precedents with prompt injection defenses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill is a modular agent skill designed for maintainer-facing workflows that generates a structured first-pass analysis of filed GitHub issues[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Rather than serving as an autonomous verdict, the skill delivers a grounded triage assessment by inspecting the checked-out codebase and drawing analogies from prior maintainer reviews[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

Operated as part of the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) system, the skill enforces strict prompt injection defenses and read-only execution invariants to safeguard automated triage pipelines[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Invariants and Security Guardrails
The skill enforces three mandatory operational constraints during analysis[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:
- **Prompt Injection Containment**: All issue text is supplied inside a nonce-delimited block and treated strictly as untrusted data[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Directives embedded in issue text—such as requests to disregard instructions, execute arbitrary commands, call external tools, or exfiltrate configuration—are treated as findings rather than tasks. When detected, the agent flags `injectionSuspected`, records details in `injectionNotes`, and resumes technical analysis on the remaining contents[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Read-Only Grounding**: The agent has local repository access to verify component paths and validate behavioral plausibility, but is strictly prohibited from modifying files, executing network calls, or running build commands[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Precedent Corpus Grounding**: The agent inspects historical maintainer analyses in `references/`, matches 3–5 items by tags and affected subsystems, and cites only genuinely informative precedents under `relatedPastIssues`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Synthetic examples are excluded from historical citations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

## Standard Output Template
The skill formats findings according to a standardized analytical schema[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:
- **Summary**: Single-paragraph synopsis of the problem in maintainer-oriented terminology[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Classification**: Structured classification including:  - *Type*: `bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].  - *Severity*: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].  - *Reproducibility*: `reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, or `not-applicable`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].  - *Severity Rationale*: Concrete evaluation of user impact and available workarounds[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Affected Components**: Explicit, concrete file paths or modules (e.g., `src/queue/consumer.ts` rather than generalized subsystem labels)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Root-Cause Hypotheses**: Plausible underlying failure mechanisms paired with explicit conditions to confirm or refute each hypothesis[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Suggested Actions**: Prioritized diagnostic steps, files to inspect, or targeted questions for the reporter rather than unverified patches[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Open Questions**: Explicit gaps in reproduction environments or version scopes requiring maintainer clarification[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Related Past Reviews**: Cited precedent analyses illustrating shared failure classes or prior architectural seams[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions workflow agent analyzing repository issues via Copilot inference and publishing structured triage assessments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `submission-analyser` is a headless GitHub Actions workflow agent designed to process and assess community issue submissions via GitHub Copilot inference. Because untrusted user input from public GitHub issues is passed directly into model contexts during automated triage, the agent repository maintains a dedicated fixture test harness validating resistance against prompt injection and control plane manipulation.

The test suite aligns with defensive requirements detailed in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and relates directly to the triage workflows encapsulated by [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md).

# Architecture / Specification

### Adversarial Test Suite

The repository test harness includes adversarial regression fixtures under `tests/fixtures/injections/` covering distinct injection vectors:

- **Direct Instruction Overrides**: Simulates attempts to discard upstream system prompts, alter agent personas, and extract internal operational instructions or tool configurations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Downstream Notification Flooding**: Tests handling of mass ping directives (`@everyone`, `@here`, role tags, and maintainer mentions) designed to trick the agent into echoing abusive notification payloads into external communication channels such as Discord [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
- **Hidden Markup and Metadata Tampering**: Uses embedded HTML comment blocks to surreptitiously alter issue severity ratings, suppress security alerts (e.g., forcing `injectionSuspected: false`), and inject falsified security review attestations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Synthesized Tool Invocations**: Embeds simulated JSON tool calls, XML function schemas, and forged execution return payloads to manipulate function-calling engines or prompt unauthorized data egress [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Evasion and Encoding Obfuscation**: Evaluates resilience against Base64 encoding, ROT13 ciphers, and Cyrillic homoglyph lookalikes intended to bypass naive string-matching filters [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Invisible Characters and Role-Play Hijacks**: Evaluates defenses against Unicode right-to-left override (RLO) formatting, zero-width spaces, and jailbreak role-play personas attempting to override triage policy [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].

# References

- [GitHub Repository Test Fixtures](https://github.com/aaif/submission-analyser/tree/df50b968b54196c39fa1037cf2e90f359f1ea7ab/tests/fixtures/injections)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI agent architecture utilizing Flue 2.0 and Pi AI models to perform read-only triage and contextual issue analysis without target repository write permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is a headless GitHub Actions workflow agent engineered to analyze incoming repository issues against contextual repository documentation and historical reviews without repository write privileges.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] Built upon Flue 2.0 and Pi AI models, the agent executes inside an isolated tooling repository, receiving dispatch requests across trust boundaries and publishing structured analysis reports exclusively to external destinations including Google Docs and Discord.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Runtime and Model Layer

The agent runs on Flue 2.0 (`@flue/runtime@2.0.3`) using a hooks-based architecture backed by the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` model layer.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] Primary inference runs through GitHub Copilot enterprise entitlements via the built-in `github-copilot` provider, with Google Gemini configured as an automated fallback.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] Analysis instructions are encapsulated as progressive Flue skills loaded via `useSkill()`, exposing single-line catalog summaries in the system prompt while deferring full instructions and reference assets until `activate_skill` is invoked.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]

## Cross-Repository Trust Boundary

Target repositories trigger analysis via `.github/workflows/request-issue-analysis.yml` by firing a GitHub `workflow_dispatch` into the analyst repository (`flue-issue-analyst`).[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] Authentication uses an `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN` scoped strictly to `Actions: read and write` on the analyst repository.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] The architecture explicitly rejects `repository_dispatch` because that event requires `Contents: write` permissions, which would permit a compromised caller to push code modifications and achieve arbitrary execution with the analyst repository's credentials.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]

## Threat Model and Defense in Depth

Because the agent consumes arbitrary, untrusted issue text written by public GitHub users while maintaining shell execution capabilities in the runner checkout, strict boundary controls are enforced:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]

1. **Zero Write Access on Originating Repositories:** The agent intentionally drops commenting capabilities on originating issues, eliminating repository write tokens and mitigating prompt injection privilege escalation.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]
2. **Immutable Dependency Pinning:** All third-party GitHub Actions in execution workflows are pinned to full commit SHAs rather than mutable version tags, preventing supply-chain token interception.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]
3. **Secret-Free Offline CI:** Automated pull request validation executes with zero environment secrets using in-memory model and egress mocks (`FLUE_FAUX=1 flue run ... --json`), validating frontmatter schemas, CLI envelopes, and exit codes safely.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]
4. **Unidirectional Egress:** Deliverables are published as immutable Google Docs and Discord webhook notifications without establishing persistent inbound listeners or stateful HTTP daemons.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]

# References

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Agent Telemetry Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Product analytics and telemetry reference architecture capturing pseudonymous agent behavioral funnels and operational metrics via direct Capture API calls and client-side PII sanitization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

PostHog functions as a product analytics and behavioral event telemetry sink for AI agent frameworks, exemplified by its reference integration in Goose.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75] Rather than capturing low-level function spans or kernel call graphs, PostHog ingests discrete session lifecycle events, feature adoption statistics, and error states while enforcing strict client-side privacy sanitization.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]

# Architecture / Specification

## Ingestion Pipeline

Agent runtimes communicate directly with PostHog's Capture API (`https://us.i.posthog.com/capture/` or self-hosted instances) via HTTPS POST operations containing a project API key (`phc_*`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75] Ingestion does not require heavy SDK runtimes or local telemetry daemons; the agent runtime constructs and dispatches typed JSON payloads directly.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]

## Telemetry Payload and Identity Model

The core transmission unit is the `CaptureEvent` payload, containing:
- `api_key`: Client project identifier embedded in the agent distribution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]
- `event`: Lifecycle action name (such as `session_start`, `error`, or `onboarding_*`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]
- `distinct_id`: Pseudonymous installation identifier generated as a random UUIDv4 stored on the local filesystem, avoiding association with user account identities or network hardware addresses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]
- `properties`: Metadata map detailing operational properties and execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]
- `timestamp`: UTC event generation time.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]

## Client-Side PII Sanitization

To preserve operational privacy, the client telemetry module (such as Goose's `posthog.rs`) routes all outgoing property fields through regex-based sanitization pipelines before serialization.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75] The filter scrubs filesystem paths, API keys, email addresses, authorization tokens, and arbitrary UUIDs, ensuring that local workspace context and sensitive developer credentials are never transmitted to analytics storage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]

# References

- `../resources/goose.md`
- `../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`
- `../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md`
- `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Kernel-level driver observability architecture combining structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, subsystem-specific tracers, and devcoredump crash records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux driver tracing provides a layered observability architecture designed for device drivers across storage, networking, GPU accelerators, and peripheral buses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1] It enables developers and system administrators to inspect hardware communications, I/O request flows, and internal driver states without recompiling kernel modules or modifying driver codebases.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Observation Primitives

Driver observability spans several kernel facilities operating at distinct points along the hardware interaction path:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

1. **Structured Logging (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_err`):** Device-aware logging macros that prefix messages with device topology names and bus addresses, routing structured text into the kernel log buffer.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
2. **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`):** Controlled via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control`, allowing runtime activation and deactivation of `dev_dbg` callsites without kernel recompilation. Debug points can be selectively enabled by driver filename, module, line number, or function.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
3. **Static Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`):** High-throughput, low-overhead binary tracepoints exposed under `/sys/kernel/tracing/events/`, consumable by `perf`, `trace-cmd`, or LTTng for low-latency hardware event timelines.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
4. **Subsystem-Specific Tracers:** Purpose-built inspection mechanisms including `blktrace` for block layer queue latency and request dispatch, as well as `usbmon` for raw USB packet capture.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
5. **Post-Mortem Analysis (`devcoredump`):** Automatic crash snapshot infrastructure that captures controller registers and memory state upon driver fault or timeout, exposing snapshot dumps under `/sys/class/devcoredump/`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

## Hardware State and Counter Model

Unlike userspace tracing models oriented around causal spans, driver observation operates on continuous hardware state queries and discrete event streams.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1] System performance counters monitor hardware health via PCIe Advanced Error Reporting (AER) counters, NVMe controller metrics via sysfs, and GPU performance monitoring units (PMUs), correlating device-level events with operating system dispatch latency.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

# References

- `../resources/linux-tracing-comparison.md`
- `../resources/ftrace.md`
- `../resources/linux-perf.md`
- `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI triage agent utilizing Flue 2.0 and Pi AI to parse, validate, and evaluate incoming GitHub issue submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is a headless continuous integration (CI) agent designed to perform automated, read-only first-pass triage and structural review on incoming GitHub issue submissions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Built on Flue 2.0 and the `pi-ai` runtime, the analyzer runs in an isolated CI runner, evaluates issue contents against community contribution guidelines, identifies suspected prompt injection attacks, and publishes triage summaries without write access to the source repository.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

The analyzer executes the [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md) using harness-tool orchestration to deliver structured assessments while enforcing strict credential boundaries.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# Architecture / Specification
The analyzer architecture centers on Flue 2.0 agent execution, built-in model catalogs, and least-privilege integration boundaries:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

- **Model Provider Integration**: Utilizes `pi-ai`'s built-in `github-copilot` provider (covering Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok model families) authenticated through GitHub token exchange via `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Model selection is submission-scoped through `useModel()`, falling back to alternative Copilot-catalog models such as `gpt-5.4` on primary service failure.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Credential & Secret Protection**: Validation routines in `src/env.ts` explicitly guard against credential leakage by logging variable names rather than raw inputs during parse failures, preventing sensitive tokens from appearing in error traces.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Integration Tool Constraints**: Operational interfaces enforce strict isolation:
  - `src/integrations/github.ts`: Provides read-only issue retrieval (`fetchIssue`), verifying `authorAssociation` and bot status with strict character size caps.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
  - `src/integrations/discord.ts`: Posts alert summaries with mention parsing explicitly disabled (`allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }`) to prevent mention hijacking.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
  - `src/integrations/google-docs.ts`: Generates documents via single multipart Google Drive file creation uploads without invoking permissions modification APIs.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Prompt-Injection Mitigation**: Structured output schemas require explicit evaluation of `injectionSuspected` and `injectionNotes`, treating detected injection attempts as structured triage findings rather than uncaught agent failures.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-19**: Phases 0 through 7 completed in `TODO.md`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Custom endpoint reverse-engineering was dropped in favor of native `pi-ai` Copilot provider support; continuous delivery pipelines were configured with PR injection tests and daily canary executions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill providing automated, read-only first-pass triage and adversarial injection detection for GitHub issue submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill (`skills/issue-analysis`) is a modular agent skill that packages domain prompts, schema templates, and evaluation criteria for performing automated, read-only first-pass triage of GitHub issues.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Orchestrated within the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) harness, the skill inspects incoming bug reports, feature requests, and vulnerability reports to verify submission completeness and detect prompt injection attempts.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill conforms to the packaging conventions established in the AAIF [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md):[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

- **Manifest & Skill Loading**: Defined at `src/skills/issue-analysis/SKILL.md` and explicitly loaded into the agent via `useSkill()`, avoiding ambient directory auto-discovery to guarantee deterministic loading.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] The skill manifest is strictly validated by Flue at process startup prior to invoking model completions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Reporting Template**: Uses `template.md` to structure generated triage documents, categorizing submissions by problem type, required reproduction steps, missing environment context, and suggested triage labels.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Reference Grounding**: Ships with synthetic reference analyses under `references/` covering bug reports, feature proposals, and security disclosures, marked with explicit `example: true` banners to ensure clarity during few-shot context assembly.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- **Injection Detection Schema**: Enforces structured outputs containing `injectionSuspected` (boolean) and `injectionNotes` (string), allowing the agent to capture, isolate, and flag adversarial prompt payloads within untrusted issue bodies.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-19**: Skill implementation finalized in `src/skills/issue-analysis/` under `TODO.md`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Adopted explicit `useSkill()` invocation over implicit discovery and incorporated synthetic benchmark suites alongside automated prompt-injection test harnesses.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, multi-agent trace models, and full-stack agent observability frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal execution trace formats, and full-stack observability frameworks for autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512] The group addresses critical monitoring blind spots where conventional application performance monitoring fails to capture multi-agent interactions, contextual reasoning transitions, and cross-layer operational anomalies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group directs ongoing research, focus groups, and standards tracks across several core domains:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

- **Specialized Focus Groups**:
  - *Protocols and Primitives*: Standardizes low-level protocol bindings, wire formats, and telemetry primitives for agent tool interactions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
  - *State, Context, and Reasoning*: Addresses memory graphs, contextual decision tracing, session replays, and semantic reasoning evaluation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Five-Layer Observability Stack**: Formulates a full-stack observability reference model evaluating gaps across five system layers, highlighting that existing tooling such as OpenTelemetry focuses primarily on Layer 5 (application tier), leaving lower tiers (hardware accelerators, kernel scheduling, network fabrics, and container cgroups) uncoordinated with agent decision telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Tamper-Evident & Cryptographic Tracing**: Investigates Merkle link graph architectures, Agent Action Capsules, and cross-layer per-field data encryption to preserve private reasoning data while enabling verifiable audit trails.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Core Specifications**: Maintains and develops the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) in coordination with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-15**: Working group charter approved by members; formally submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee on April 21, 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]
- **2026-08-19**: Group ratified initial observability taxonomy terms, opened focus group participation across the community, evaluated the five-layer telemetry gap model, and scheduled Agent Action Capsule review cycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

proposed_concept.title: Context Exhaustion
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining the session failure mode where task-required information exceeds model context window capacity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Context exhaustion is the failure mode in which the information an agent needs for its current task no longer fits within the model's context window at the same time, because accumulated content has reached the window's capacity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].

The primary discriminator of context exhaustion is that required information is displaced specifically by window capacity limits, distinguishing it from adjacent operational conditions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46]:
- **Populated context**: A large or heavily populated context window that still accommodates all task-relevant information is not exhausted [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].
- **Degraded attention**: Attention degradation across an expansive but non-overflowed context represents an attention quality defect rather than exhaustion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].
- **Retrieval failure**: Failure to retrieve or load relevant information into context represents an upstream retrieval defect rather than exhaustion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].

Context exhaustion specifically identifies the condition where window capacity itself prevents the agent from observing required task information [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].

# Architecture / Specification

Context exhaustion is a runtime property of an execution session rather than an intrinsic characteristic of a model [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].

Common engineering mitigations—such as context summarization, external vector memory retrieval, and task decomposition across [taxonomy/subagent](../taxonomy/subagent.md) boundaries—do not prevent exhaustion; rather, they trade hard capacity exhaustion for lossy compression, shifting observable operational failures into compression and retrieval artifacts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46].

### Taxonomic Relationships
- **Related Terms**: `Session`, `Harness` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-46]
- **Core Dependencies**: Directly relates to [taxonomy/context](../taxonomy/context.md) and task partitioning under [taxonomy/subagent](../taxonomy/subagent.md)

mutations.rationale: Captures the universal taxonomy definition distinguishing packaged instructions from external execution tools established in working group issue 47.

proposed_concept.title: Skill
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining a packaged, reusable set of instructions loaded into context on demand to guide agent task performance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

A skill is a packaged, reusable set of instructions and supporting resources that changes how an agent performs a class of task, loaded into the model's context when relevant rather than built into the model or executed as code [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47].

The fundamental discriminator of a skill is that it instructs rather than executes, establishing a clear architectural boundary between a skill and a tool [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47]:
- **Skill**: Informs and alters what the model itself does next by injecting behavioral guidance, schemas, or domain procedures into [taxonomy/context](../taxonomy/context.md). Removing a skill affects how well or in what style possible actions are executed [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47].
- **Tool**: Executed external to the model runtime across APIs, filesystems, or services. Removing a [taxonomy/tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) restricts what actions are possible [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47].

# Architecture / Specification

A skill is characterized by explicit packaging, lifecycle loading, and agent-agnostic consumption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47]:
- **Packaging and Lifecycle**: Raw instructions pasted into an isolated prompt constitute ad-hoc [taxonomy/prompt](../taxonomy/prompt.md) input, not a skill. A skill is uniquely named, versioned, discoverable, and loaded on demand across sessions and disparate agent harnesses [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47].
- **Authoring Orthogonality**: Whether a skill is manually authored by developers or synthesized dynamically by autonomous agents is orthogonal to its taxonomic qualification [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47].
- **Standardization**: Portable skill packaging formats and manifest structures are defined by [standards/agent-skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) and governed by [guidelines/agent-plugin-portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md).

### Taxonomic Relationships
- **Contrasts With**: [taxonomy/tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47]
- **Related Terms**: `Harness`, [taxonomy/prompt](../taxonomy/prompt.md), [taxonomy/context](../taxonomy/context.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-47]
