proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Workflow Documentation Blueprint
proposed_concept.description: Structural blueprint and section framework organizing the Single-Agent Workflow Reference Architecture (SAW-RA).
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Workflow Documentation Blueprint provides the standardized structural framework and organizational model for authoring the future Single-Agent Workflow Reference Architecture (SAW-RA) within the [working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) working group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

The blueprint establishes common organizational expectations to ensure reference architecture artifacts remain accessible to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, facilitate designing new workflows, evaluate existing implementations, and foster reusable patterns over ad-hoc solutions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

# Architecture / Specification

The blueprint defines a six-part architecture documentation structure [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b]:

### 1. Foundations
Establishes the foundational scope, non-goals, core concepts, design principles (such as [guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)), and architectural invariants governing single-agent execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

### 2. Architecture Model
Specifies the reference execution model, catalogs execution primitives aligning with [taxonomy/workflow-primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md), models runtime components, and specifies structural composition rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

### 3. Patterns and Selection
Provides a pattern classification taxonomy, deterministic selection matrices, and a reference pattern catalog capturing constructs such as [patterns/human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), [patterns/bounded-convergence-loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), and [patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

### 4. Enterprise Readiness
Defines control overlays spanning security, auditability, observability, and compliance requirements for production deployment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

### 5. Workflow Lifecycle
Details end-to-end lifecycle methodologies covering initial design, assessment of legacy workflows, required architectural documentation, testing and evaluation frameworks, operations, and governance conformance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

### 6. Evolution and Supporting Material
Maintains roadmap projections, migration pathways, and supplemental appendices tracking evolving agent capabilities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

mutations.rationale: Taxonomy workstream issue #52 proposes 'self-reported' as an architectural taxonomy term distinguishing an artifact's unverified write-path claims from independent substrate-vantage evidence.

proposed_concept.title: Self-Reported
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy classification denoting observation records emitted directly by an artifact about itself without independent verification outside its write path.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
In the AAIF taxonomy, **self-reported** denotes a property of an observation or record that asserts the described artifact generated the telemetry or claim about itself, without independent verification from outside the artifact's own write path[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52]. A record can be well-formed and schema-compliant yet remain self-reported, distinguishing it from records captured through external observation or a substrate-level vantage point[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52].

# Architecture / Specification
The concept establishes the foundational boundary separating conventional application observability from tamper-evident audit evidence[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52]:
- **Write Path Confinement**: Because an OpenTelemetry span is emitted directly by the runtime it describes, its contents are inherently self-reported regardless of syntax correctness[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52].
- **Substrate Vantage Contrast**: External, substrate-vantage observations or hardware-attested captures operate outside the target system's execution context, providing independent corroboration[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52].
- **Verifier Testing**: Originating in OWASP GenAI Security Project agent-control-standard discussions, the term defines the property under test for verifier-side security primitives and operational conformance checks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52].

Within the broader AAIF taxonomy framework, this property pairs against external observation models and informs evaluations of [evidence strength labels](../taxonomy/evidence-strength-labels.md) and [evidence records](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md).

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Proposed in [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) issue #52 for the cross-workgroup taxonomy definitions pass[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-52].

# References

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing shared agentic AI terminology, classification schemas, and open-source landscape registries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The **Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group** (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. It curates foundational AI agent definitions, conceptual relationship mappings, and the public [agentic AI landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) catalog across foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Deliverables & Operations
The workstream operates unified terminology reviews, definitions style guides, and landscape inclusion criteria[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]:
- **Universal Taxonomy**: Maintains consensus definitions for core primitives including Agent, Harness, Subagent, Skill, and [Self-Reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md) telemetry properties[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Landscape Catalog**: Maintains machine-readable registries across agent runtimes, protocol gateways, and emerging categories like Attestation & Verifiable Evidence (AVE)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Cross-Group Alignment**: Coordinates domain editors across [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Overview
The **Agent Behavior Trace Model** is an open telemetry specification stewarded by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. It defines causal trace boundaries, conversation-context propagation, tool-invocation lifecycles, and semantic conventions for agent execution graphs spanning heterogeneous runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Architecture / Specification
The standard addresses the architectural boundary between underlying transport telemetry and agent reasoning state[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]:
- **Causal Context Propagation**: Standardizes context identifiers across multi-turn exchanges, distinguishing an agent runtime's failure to export conversation metadata from gaps in underlying telemetry protocols like [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Gap Classification Model**: Classifies telemetry capture anomalies into four orthogonal categories: unsupported runtime behavior, instrumentation defect, guidance ambiguity, or missing semantic specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Baseline Conformance Testing**: Implements a nine-task execution plan comparing baseline captures between [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and secondary reference SDKs across support workflows to validate turn-boundary preservation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Task 2 opened under issue #40 to capture reproducible baseline telemetry in Goose and establish classified gap criteria for multi-interaction agent workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Workflow Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between candidate proposal generation and external execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Human Approval reference architecture enforces a structural break between an agent's proposal stage and the final execution or publication boundary by routing candidate artifacts through an explicit, authorized human decision gate.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

# Architecture / Specification

The workflow splits agent execution across two distinct domains:
1. **Proposal Domain**: The agent analyzes inputs, performs retrieval, and drafts a proposed change or payload.
2. **Approval Gate**: An authenticated human reviews the proposed payload against domain invariants, modifying, approving, or rejecting the submission.
3. **Execution/Publication Domain**: Upon valid human sign-off, an isolated runtime executes or publishes the artifact without further autonomous agent mutations.

Validated target operational scenarios include:
- FAQ and knowledge-base article updates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- Software release notes generation and publishing.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- Commercial catalog listing descriptions.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

# Lifecycle History

- Validated against empirical content publishing and catalog update scenarios in PR #36.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry protocols, trace representations, provenance capture, and cross-boundary observation mechanisms for agentic AI architectures.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its efforts across several technical workstreams and focus groups:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A structured nine-task initiative standardizing session/turn correlation across discontinuous traces and providing runnable, multi-provider reference examples.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]

- **Agent Action Capsule Exploration**: Assessment of cryptographic execution ledgers that record dispatched actions, execution outcomes, and authorization invariants.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]

- 2026-09-02: Formed consensus to address sub-L7 and syscall observability within the Primitives and Protocols focus group and evaluated Agent Action Capsule integration.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification for recording multi-turn agent interactions, step-level causality, tool invocations, and conversation continuity across trace boundaries without relying on unbounded, session-long spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]

# Architecture / Specification

The model defines standard attributes and linking strategies for agent execution:
- **Session and Turn Continuity**: Connects completed conversation turns across separate traces when runtimes resume execution or processes restart, preserving native SDK session identifiers (such as threads or conversations).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]
- **Causal Context Propagation**: Correlates tool requests with subsequent execution outcomes, strictly preventing provider-level tool-call generation events from being falsely reported as tool execution records.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]
- **Provider & Agent Extensibility Harness**: Standardized fixtures, mapping suites, and standalone API verification examples covering streaming, errors, and tool-call lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]

# Lifecycle History

- 2026-08/09: Nine-task execution plan initiated in the Observability and Traceability Working Group, defining session correlation (Task 5) and extensible runnable fixtures (Task 8).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, palette, and asset specifications governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets, reports, and public collateral.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) brand guidelines define the visual identity, typography, token-based styling, and asset usage rules for all foundation collateral and generated reports [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. All generated human-facing materials adhere to a unified design system that prioritizes flat geometry, strict surface separation, and a restrained monochromatic accent structure [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Specification

## Source of Truth and Token Pipeline

The primary design system specification is maintained as a self-extracting bundle in `design/aaif-design-system.html` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. The CSS custom properties token block (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) is generated directly from this HTML bundle via `scripts/extract_design_tokens.py`, which is validated in continuous integration via `--check` to prevent manual drift [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Color Palette and Surfaces

- **Primary Accent**: The core accent is black (`--accent: var(--ink)`), reserving spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) as secondary accents within individual surfaces rather than brand identifiers (e.g., coral is `--spec-8`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Surfaces**: Two first-class surfaces exist: white editorial (`--paper`) and black plate [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. The warm off-white (`--paper-2`) is restricted to section banding, while tinted panels use `--paper-3` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **No Dark Mode**: AAIF assets do not implement `prefers-color-scheme` inverted twins; designers deliberately select either the white editorial ground or black plate per component [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Typography and Geometry

- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans (OFL) across 400, 500, 600, and 700 weights serves as the singular typeface for both display and user interface elements [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Monospace stacks are reserved strictly for metadata and eyebrows, never for body text [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Headings**: Headings are set at weight 500, tracking `-0.02em`, and line-height 1.05–1.15, avoiding bold weights except for h5/h6 levels at weight 600 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Elevation and Radii**: The aesthetic is strictly flat with zero drop shadows; depth is conveyed via 1px hairlines, surface tinting, and inset strokes [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Cards, tables, and chips retain square corners (`border-radius: 0`), while pill rounding is restricted to interactive buttons and explicit badge pills [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Mark and Motif Rules

Official SVG assets in `assets/` (such as `aaif-mark.svg`, `aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be used verbatim without manual redrawing [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. The AAIF agent motif (constructed from the mark's geometric primitives) is permitted only for empty states, loading sequences, event graphics, and visual dividers; it is explicitly prohibited from governance, board, audit, and press publications [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) evaluates global artificial intelligence regulations, legislation, and industry standards to map them against agentic architecture principles [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Phased Deliverable Lifecycle

The group operates through a three-phase methodology leading to concrete gap analyses and framework mappings [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]:

- **Phase 1: Landscape Analysis**: Identification of initial policy instruments and governance frameworks affecting agentic AI architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Phase 2: Policy Mapping & Gap Analysis**: Mapping instruments against approximately a dozen foundational governance themes using standardized AI extraction prompts to identify regulatory and technical gaps [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Phase 3: Final Deliverable Release**: Consolidation and release of the final gap analysis deliverable; the group does not release intermediate drafts before Phase 3 completion [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, the working group achieved general consensus on the initial set of policy instruments and roughly a dozen mapping themes, formally transitioning work from the initial landscape analysis into the Phase 2 gap analysis stage [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. Reporting flows directly to the Technical Committee (see [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md)).

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry standards, distributed trace models, and boundary observability mechanisms for agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]. It coordinates both across internal Agentic AI Foundation working groups and with external standards bodies to ensure protocol interoperability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

# Architecture / Specification

## External Liaison Roster

Per charter section 8, the working group maintains formal liaison channels across key external standards and open-source initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]:

- **OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG**: Harmonizing generative AI and agent telemetry semantic conventions (see [../resources/opentelemetry.md](../resources/opentelemetry.md)) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **OWASP AOS**: Tracking security telemetry and agent threat vectors in coordination with security practitioners [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **W3C Trace Context**: Aligning distributed context propagation standards for multi-turn and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **Agent Trace**: Tracking line-level attribution tracing standards maintained at agent-trace.dev (see [../standards/agent-trace.md](../standards/agent-trace.md)) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **Monocle & AGNTCY**: Evaluating multi-agent framework instrumentation and agent trace interoperability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

## Cross-WG Coordination

The working group manages bilateral intake tracking connecting to the Technical Committee (see [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md)), hosted projects like Goose (see [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md)) and Model Context Protocol, the Security and Privacy Working Group (see [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)), and the Taxonomy & Landscape workstream (see [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining intake criteria, contribution agreements, triage roles, and joint TC and Governing Board review gates for AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process defines the intake workflow and review gates for open-source projects applying to become official AAIF Hosted Projects across the Sandbox, Growth, and Impact maturity tiers [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]. The process requires formal alignment analysis, an executed legal Contribution Agreement, and affirmative approval votes from both the Technical Committee (TC) and the Governing Board (GB) [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Triage

Applications are submitted via the structured GitHub issue template in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository labeled `New` [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]. Applicants must detail:

- Project origins, capabilities, and technical maturity [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
- Alignment with the AAIF mission and ecosystem [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
- Architectural relationship to existing AAIF hosted projects and specifications [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

## Contribution Agreement and Dual Approval Gates

1. **Contribution Agreement**: A legal Contribution Agreement is sent to designated project contacts based on submission information. This agreement must be signed before the Governing Board can conduct a formal acceptance vote [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
2. **TC and GB Approval**: Official acceptance requires affirmative votes by both the Technical Committee (see [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md)) and the Governing Board [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
3. **Linux Foundation Countersignature**: The Linux Foundation countersigns the Contribution Agreement only after a successful Governing Board vote [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
4. **Representation Restrictions**: Maintainers cannot represent their project as "donated" or "contributed" until both voting gates succeed and the Contribution Agreement is countersigned [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards and reference architectures for agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and cross-boundary trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. It addresses the architectural requirements of agentic interactions where existing identity systems—historically designed for human interactive sign-in or machine-to-machine workload authentication—fail to capture dynamic delegation chains, verifiable human approval evidence, and cross-boundary auditability [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Governance and Operations
The working group is co-led by chairs appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the foundation, serving a term from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]:
- **Chair**: Grant Miller (IBM)
- **Co-Chair**: Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)

Working group members participate as individuals in service of the foundation's mission rather than as organizational representatives [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Plenary meetings occur weekly on Thursdays, alternating between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM US Pacific Time [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Proposed presentations and outstanding discussion topics are tracked in a dedicated agenda queue prior to scheduling [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0].

# Breakouts and Collaboration
The working group divides its active development into three coordinated breakout efforts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases**: Extracts operational identity and trust requirements from enterprise and consumer scenarios (coordinated by Wei Chen).
- **Reference Architecture**: Models actors, trust boundaries, delegation semantics, and interoperability interfaces (coordinated by Brian Malone).
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Formalizes identity and trust terminology and liaises directly with the cross-working-group [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (liaisons: Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky).

Additionally, the working group engages in cross-group review with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to define OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and baggage propagation rules that carry agent identity attributes across asynchronous distributed traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Technical Reference Context
The working group evaluates relevant external architectures and protocol proposals to identify architectural gaps and inform specifications [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) for capability registry and federated agent resolution.
- Workload identity systems like SPIFFE/SPIRE, examining their fit and boundaries regarding agent-level identity, human consent propagation, and cross-domain federation.
- Production identity frameworks such as Uber Engineering's multi-hop agent token exchange and NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace reference design.
- Standards track specifications including the IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization draft.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and classification schema mapping production agentic workflows across orchestration models, autonomy levels, and structural gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory is an empirical catalog and structural taxonomy maintained by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group (`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`). It systematically maps real-world AI agent implementations across workflow primitives, coordination mechanisms, and architectural invariants defined in `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

The classification inventory audits enterprise use cases against strict architectural criteria to distinguish actual multi-agent delegation and deterministic control from loose heuristic pipelines[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
The classification schema evaluates use cases along multiple architectural dimensions, requiring verifiable source documentation of runtime execution structure:

- **Coordination and Orchestration**: Classifies execution topologies into models such as sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out, and dynamic AI-coordinated planning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. For example, lead enrichment workflows qualify as sequential pipelines when following strict waterfall data provider sequences, whereas SRE incident triage agents execute parallel fan-out with supervisor re-planning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Agent Boundary Requirements**: Differentiates between single-agent workflows and inherently multi-agent architectures where context window exhaustion (`../taxonomy/context-exhaustion.md`) or security boundary isolation necessitates context splitting across specialized sub-agents[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Structural Control Gates**: Categorizes operational guardrails, distinguishing heuristic feedback from deterministic acceptance gates (`../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md`) and bounded convergence loops (`../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
- **Schema Link Standardization**: Corrected all inventory cross-references to point definitively to the canonical schema file `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].
- **Empirical Citation Audit**: Conducted an evidentiary review of the inventory, removing unsupported convergence loop claims and verifying production multi-agent topologies against vendor technical documentation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Prescriptive implementation recommendations covering agent tool execution boundaries, secrets management, workload identity, and cross-boundary access controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides implementation standards for securing agentic AI systems across tool execution boundaries, credential management, and runtime sandboxing. Maintained by the Security & Privacy Working Group (`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`), the guideline establishes defensible isolation boundaries to mitigate prompt injection, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

In addition to runtime execution controls, the specification details token lifetime limits and IAM scoping requirements for autonomous agent workloads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# Architecture / Specification
Key areas addressed by the guidance include:

- **Workload Identity Baseline**: Recommends short-lived IAM credentials with a standard baseline limit of 1 hour (configurable lower) bounded by granular role design[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Multi-Cloud and Hybrid Federation**: Extends workload identity guidance in collaboration with the Identity & Trust Working Group (`../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`) to define OIDC federation patterns, cross-cloud role assumption, and credential rotation across hybrid environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Blast Radius and Trust Domains**: Mandates least-privilege scoping to prevent privilege escalation when an autonomous agent chain spans multiple cloud providers or interacts across heterogeneous IAM domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Execution Boundaries**: Recommends hardware-attested or containerized isolation for untrusted tool execution (`../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md`), coupled with out-of-band kill switches (`../patterns/kill-switch.md`).

# Lifecycle History
- **Multi-Cloud Identity Scope**: Expanded workload identity requirements from single-cloud IAM baselines to encompass multi-cloud role assumption and federated identity standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: AAIF telemetry specification defining multi-turn agent execution traces, causal context linkage, and semantic convention mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification defined by the Observability & Traceability Working Group (`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`). It establishes standardized telemetry schemas to record multi-turn agent execution spans, causal context linkage, sub-agent delegations, and tool interactions.

The standard establishes interoperability across runtime engines and distributed tracing backends, harmonizing span definitions with OpenTelemetry (`../resources/opentelemetry.md`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model structures agent execution telemetry through standard span attributes and context boundaries:

- **Execution Turns and Causality**: Captures multi-turn conversational workflows, tracking turn-entry spans, conversation identifiers, and parent-child causality across distributed agent boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Semantic Conventions Alignment**: Maps agentic telemetry concepts directly into OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, establishing common span naming, attribute semantics, and event structures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Terminology Harmonization**: Cross-walks telemetry span constructs with common vocabulary established by the Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group (`../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# Lifecycle History
- **Execution Plan Task 9**: Formulated an upstream contribution pipeline to feed trace model findings, runtime instrumentation patches, and entry-span identification fixes directly into upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and AAIF taxonomy definitions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for resolving bounded operational problems autonomously through isolated execution, deterministic acceptance gating, and safe escalation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a job-oriented reference architecture designed to resolve a single, explicitly bounded operational problem without requiring human approval for every attempt.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b] The architecture couples an isolated execution workspace with an independent deterministic gate and a constrained effect executor, ensuring candidate results are objectively verified before modifying external state.

Contrasting with the [human-approved operation](single-agent-human-approval.md), this architecture permits autonomous iterative convergence when machine-verifiable acceptance criteria exist, while enforcing strict boundaries against uncontrolled side effects.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Invariants

The architecture relies on four fundamental guarantees:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]
1. **Bounded Autonomy:** The agent operates strictly within the task contract, permitted tools, credentials, data, and execution budget declared for a single run.
2. **Independent Acceptance:** An external, deterministic gate—never the agent itself—determines whether candidate results satisfy declared acceptance conditions.
3. **Controlled Effect:** Only accepted, scope-validated outputs reach the constrained effect executor; the agent cannot invoke high-privilege side effects directly.
4. **Safe Non-Convergence:** When budgets expire, errors repeat, evidence is ambiguous, or operations fall out of scope, execution halts in an audited terminal state and escalates to human operational queues.

## Pattern Composition

Bounded Autonomous Remediation composes three foundational workflow patterns:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Limits agent retry loops within predefined token, time, and step quotas.
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Runs automated tests, linters, schemas, or contract validations against candidate outputs.
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Enforces an architectural boundary between candidate state generation in an isolated work area and production effect application.

## Structure and Execution Flow

An execution engine admits tasks, sequences steps, manages retries, and enforces termination. The agent operates within an isolated or non-authoritative work area (such as a temporary branch or scratchpad environment). Once the agent submits a candidate result, the deterministic acceptance gate evaluates contract compliance. If all criteria pass, the constrained effect executor applies the low-impact, reversible modification (such as opening a pull request or submitting a draft record). Non-converging runs escalate to an external queue.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]

# Lifecycle History

The architecture incorporates a formal validation record with scenarios including autonomous maintenance runs ("night shift") and multi-constraint schedule generation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37]

# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for overseeing technical standards, best practices, working groups, and technical vision across the foundation.[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]

# Architecture / Specification

## Membership and Governance

Founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for a term running from March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026.[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092] Leadership and committee membership includes:

- **David Soria Parra** (Anthropic) - TC Chair
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Microsoft) - TC Co-Chair
- **Alan Blount** (Google)
- **Bradley Axen** (Block)
- **James Ward** (Amazon Web Services)
- **Nick Cooper** (OpenAI)
- **Sambhav Kothari** (Bloomberg)
- **Steve Faulkner** (Cloudflare)

## Foundation Projects

The TC oversees open-source and specification initiatives across lifecycle stages defined in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md). Founding Impact Stage projects stewarded under the TC include the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the goose agent harness, and AGENTS.MD.[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF telemetry specification defining multi-turn agent execution traces, causal context linkage, and OpenTelemetry crosswalk conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41] It establishes causal context linkage and common data relationships across multi-turn agent sessions.

# Architecture / Specification

## Shared Contract and OpenTelemetry Crosswalk

The trace model specifies identity relationships across conversation/session scope, turns, calls, proposed actions, and observations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41] Core architectural facets include:

- **Turn and Session Scoping:** Discrete turns within an overarching conversation carry decoupled trace identifiers while preserving session context.
- **Proposal and Execution Decoupling:** Proposed actions remain separate from tool execution spans; an approval gate decision references a proposed action even if denied and no execution span is created.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]
- **Crosswalk Mapping:** Bridges AAIF trace concepts with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, accounting for approval waits, resumption, and incomplete observations.

proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and classification schema mapping production agentic workflows across orchestration topologies and autonomy models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification framework is an empirical catalog and schema maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to classify real-world agent implementations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47] It structures use cases by coordination topology, governance gating, and operational execution patterns.

# Architecture / Specification

## Coordination Topologies and Classification Ambiguities

The schema distinguishes orchestration topologies including parallel fan-out and sequential pipelines.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47] Active working group deliberations address taxonomy overlaps between:

- **Parallel Fan-out:** Topologies defined by concurrency and execution timing (concurrent sub-tasks).
- **Sequential Pipeline:** Topologies defined by data and step dependency (dependent activities feeding subsequent stages).

Because concurrency and dependency are not mutually exclusive, classification efforts evaluate whether criteria should anchor on observed execution timing, instantiated agent counts, or structural dependency graphs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology, SKOS-Lite taxonomy schemas, and ecosystem mapping across technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) that serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across all vertical Technical Working Groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Rather than authoring domain-specific definitions in isolation, the workstream ingests, harmonizes, and standardizes pre-competitive terminology and maintains a unified market landscape to eliminate siloed research and inconsistent conceptual models[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

The workstream is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), coordinating directly with appointed Domain Editors from each of the Foundation's seven vertical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. The workstream's active contribution scope is currently focused on the core taxonomy, while contributions to the ecosystem landscape remain deferred pending formal intake process approval[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Domain Editor Representation
Unlike standalone vertical working groups, the workstream functions as a horizontal coordination body composed of nominated Domain Editors from each vertical domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam
- [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish
- [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin
- [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra and Matt Lee
- [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White and Katherine Druckman
- [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana

Domain Editors shepherd terms through intake, ensure definitions preserve domain sovereignty, and hold veto authority under the workstream's anti-erasure guardrail, which prohibits deleting concepts or folding operational terms into aliases without explicit written sign-off[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

## Terminology Lifecycle and Disambiguation
Terms progress through a phased lifecycle before integration into the official vocabulary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
1. **Identification**: A candidate term is identified if it matters specifically to agentic AI, materially departs from traditional usage, and affects at least one working group (terms affecting three or more groups qualify as Universal)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
2. **Spreadsheet Intake**: Terms are cataloged in the shared intake log with statuses of `Debate`, `Keep`, or `Cull`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
3. **Paired Contrast Disambiguation**: When terms represent adjacent contrasting concepts (such as [tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) vs. [skill](../taxonomy/skill.md)), definitions must explicitly articulate differentiating boundaries and establish bidirectional links using `relatedTerms` or `contrastsWith` rather than collapsing into aliases[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
4. **Pull Request Review**: Code contributions update the machine-readable taxonomy file (`taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`) and receive review from relevant Domain Editors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

## SKOS-Lite Data Schema
The shared taxonomy is stored in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` conforming to a SKOS-Lite model[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:
- `term` (String, Required): Preferred term formatted in sentence case[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, Required): Synonyms or alternative labels[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `category` (String, Required): Broad conceptual bucket (e.g., `Agentic Threats`, `Identity & Authorization`); currently deferred as an empty string to avoid premature categorization[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `broaderTerm` (String/null, Required): Direct parent node in hierarchical mindmaps; currently deferred as `null`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `definition` (String, Required): Technical, objective definition; initial admissions use a standardized pending placeholder until formally agreed[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `scopeNote` (String, Optional): Operational provenance, meeting dates, or cross-group boundary notes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `relatedTerms` / `contrastsWith` (Arrays of Strings, Optional): Associative links enforcing paired contrast clarity[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, Required): Shepherding or owning working groups; universal terms carry an empty array (`[]`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was chartered under the AAIF Technical Committee to reconcile overlapping vocabularies across working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. On July 27, 2026, the workstream adopted a phased intake strategy: admitting terms first while deferring final definitions, hierarchical parent terms, and category classifications to prevent premature domain conflict[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]. The roster of Domain Editors was updated in September 2026[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Survey Specification
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey evaluating production agent adoption, failure rates, consequence severity, and reliability factors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Survey is an empirical, platform-neutral survey specification developed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Composed of 16 structured questions, the instrument gathers firsthand practitioner experiences from production AI systems and advanced pilots to quantify deployment stages, human intervention overhead, error detection mechanisms, and failure consequences[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

The survey findings are intended to direct the working group's benchmark priorities, identify real-world failure patterns, and guide open standards development across the agentic AI lifecycle[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility and Screening Filter
The survey enforces strict participation criteria based on firsthand exposure within the preceding six months[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:
- **Qualifying Cohorts**: Practitioners with systems in serious pilots (tested in target work settings), limited deployment (active in select workflows), broad deployment, or systems paused/retired after reaching deployment[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Exclusion Filters**: Demo, prototype, generic research, secondhand knowledge, or non-system roles exit immediately after Question 1[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

## Question Architecture and Core Inquiry Areas
The instrument standardizes four response formats: single-select, multi-select, single-response Likert matrix, and conditional inline text[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. All questions evaluate a single focal system identified during eligibility screening[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:
- **System and Practitioner Context (Q1–Q5)**: Maps practitioner activities (design, evaluation, operations, output review, strategic oversight), primary work domains, architectural topologies, and organizational size[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Benefits and Human Checking (Q6–Q8)**: Documents operational constraints, human-in-the-loop review frequency, approval gating mechanisms, and highest-value business outcomes[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Accuracy and Reliability Benchmarks (Q9–Q13)**: Measures the incidence rate of unacceptable outputs, causal reliability factors, whether anomalies are caught prior to business impact, the severity of the most critical consequence observed, and baseline evidence methods used to establish system trust[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Evaluates shared industry priorities, preferred working group deliverables, and open feedback[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Lifecycle History
The survey instrument was drafted and merged into the working group deliverables repository to establish an empirical baseline for future foundation initiatives[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing measurement methodologies, failure taxonomies, and practitioner surveys for agentic AI dependability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to establish standardized measurement methodologies, evaluation benchmarks, failure taxonomies, and operational practices for autonomous and semi-autonomous systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. The group focuses on identifying why agentic systems fail in production, establishing reproducible quality standards, and mitigating risks stemming from non-deterministic outputs and unintended agent behavior[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

To align its deliverables with production realities, the working group conducts empirical field research, including the [Accuracy & Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md), while collaborating horizontally across the foundation through the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Scope and Deliverables
The working group's scope covers foundational reliability challenges across the agentic lifecycle:
- **Practitioner Field Surveys**: Developing neutral assessment instruments, such as the 16-question [Accuracy & Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md), to quantify real-world failure frequencies, human review burdens, and consequence severity across pilot and production environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Failure Taxonomies**: Cataloging agent-specific failure modes—such as drift, tool execution errors, and context degradation—in coordination with cross-cutting taxonomy efforts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- **Evaluation and Quality Metrics**: Defining objective benchmarks for measuring output veracity, determinism, and task completion fidelity.

## Cross-Group Representation
The working group nominates Domain Editors to represent its technical domain within the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- **Casper Nielsen** ([@CasperGN](https://github.com/CasperGN))
- **Matthew Khouzam** ([@MatthewKhouzam](https://github.com/MatthewKhouzam))

Domain Editors shepherd accuracy-related concepts (such as evaluation criteria and non-deterministic error models) through the Foundation's review pipeline while maintaining domain sovereignty over specialized metrics[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Lifecycle History
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group was established as one of the AAIF's core technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. In 2026, the group ratified its practitioner survey deliverable to collect cross-industry operational data from production deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite provides deterministic CLI tooling and agent-assisted workflows for administering the Agentic AI Foundation's (AAIF) global community chapter network. It manages end-to-end operational automation across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack workspaces, encompassing channel provisioning, access management, multi-platform identity reconciliation, directory broadcasting, and chapter CRM synchronization.

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity Resolution and Intake Triaging
Chapter organizer intake records resolve multiple distinct digital identities per individual without overwriting self-reported intake details [^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- **Three-Column Model**: Intake tracking separates the intake `Email` from `Slack ID` (immutable `U…` user ID), `Slack Email` (address registered with Slack), and `Drive Email` (the specific Google account with Drive folder permissions) [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Consumer Gmail Normalization**: Automatic Slack lookup accounts for consumer Gmail dot-folding (`gmail.com` and `googlemail.com`) on lookup failure, while strictly treating dots as significant for custom Workspace domains to prevent cross-account mapping [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Safe Attribution Split**: Unambiguous email lookups may be written automatically via `--write`, whereas name-based matches remain suggestions requiring explicit operator confirmation (`--apply`) to prevent account clobbering across unrelated applicants sharing names [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Audit Classification**: Workspace audits decouple true channel invitation backlogs from intake data issues where an applicant lacks a registered Slack account entirely (`no_account`) [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Channel Provisioning and Lifecycle Enforcement
Channel configuration enforces strict boundaries between public discussion spaces and restricted chapter leadership rooms [^evt-community-events-pr-42, ^evt-community-events-pr-43]:
- **Naming Conventions**: Public regional rooms adhere to bare canonical country names (e.g., `#cyprus`, `#greece`), managed through an explicit rename registry rather than ad-hoc scripts [^evt-community-events-pr-43].
- **Organizer Room Seeding**: Private organizer rooms automatically seed verified operational accounts resolved dynamically from configuration rosters (`Ops staff email` and domain allowlists) rather than static codebase constants [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Restricted Asset Distribution**: Sensitive administrative resources—such as chapter Google Drive folder links containing local CRMs and budgets—are posted strictly in private organizer rooms to prevent unauthorized access requests [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Idempotent Messaging and Pin Guards**: Automated posting workflows inspect channel history directly to prevent duplicate announcements across repeated sync runs, isolating message-level history from pin management permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

## Country Channel Directories and Scope Invites
Multi-chapter coordination provides targeted invitation pipelines and non-destructive directory management [^evt-community-events-pr-36]:
- **Scoped Organizer Invites**: Organizers can be invited to private chapter rooms, public country channels, or both (`--scope {organizer,country,both}`), deduplicating shared country channel rosters by resolved Slack IDs [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Additive Directory Posts**: The `post_country_directory.py` service announces newly established chapters within parent country channels without modifying or overwriting existing human-authored directory postings [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## CRM Data Architecture
Chapter CRM workbooks enforce a structural separation between intake pipeline decisions and applicant role expressions [^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- **Status vs. Interest Split**: The `Status` column exclusively tracks organizational decisions (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Declined`), while the `Interested in` column independently preserves original applicant interests (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`) [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Detail Field Propagation**: Workbooks ingest role-specific professional details (`LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, `Technical expertise`) directly from intake tabs without unvetted public exposure [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Visual Token Integration**: Workbooks map lifecycle states to explicit brand color tokens via SpreadsheetML styles [^evt-community-events-pr-28, ^evt-community-events-pr-32].

mutations.rationale: Incorporates OOXML design token implementations, Office document typography standards (Instrument Sans), SpreadsheetML/WordprocessingML styling seams, and contrast verification rules.

# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines govern visual identity, typography, color palettes, and presentation standards across all Agentic AI Foundation materials. The specification ensures consistent, accessible branding across public digital properties, web deliverables, publications, and enterprise Office Open XML (OOXML) documents (.pptx presentations, .docx documents, and .xlsx workbooks) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Typographic Standards
- **Primary Typeface**: Instrument Sans serves as the universal display, heading, and body face across all digital collateral and Office documents, replacing legacy typefaces (such as Space Grotesk, Manrope, Arial, and Calibri) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Embedding and Fallbacks**: Web environments utilize WOFF2 webfonts (`assets/fonts/`). In desktop OOXML environments, WordprocessingML document tables reconcile embedded font references (`word/fontTable.xml`), pruning orphaned embedded binaries while mapping typeface declarations cleanly [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Color System and Design Tokens
The foundation maintains a vendor-neutral design token architecture mapped from `design/aaif-tokens.css` into document automation tooling [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Base Neutrals**: Neutral ramps define text and structural boundaries (`--ink-1` through `--ink-4`, `--line-1`, `--line-2`), eliminating stock Office greys and arbitrary navy tints [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Spectrum Tokens**: Semantic accent tokens (`--spec-1` through `--spec-5`) provide categorical highlights, map pins, and data visualizations (e.g., `--spec-3` for geographic map indicators) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Role-Aware Token Application**: Automation transformers distinguish identical hex colors by structural context—for instance, mapping a legacy navy fill to an AAIF black plate header while converting adjacent cell border rules into hairline divider lines [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## OOXML Seam and Document Architecture
Programmatic generation of Office documents utilizes minimal-diff XML rewriting engines (`ooxml_style.py`) to preserve underlying relationship tables and markup [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **SpreadsheetML (`xl/styles.xml`)**: Workbooks translate colors using explicit ARGB formats and indexed formatting (`dxfId`), styling CRM and tracker grids with AAIF status palettes [^evt-community-events-pr-32, ^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **DrawingML**: Presentations and deck graphics apply shape fills and strokes directly mapped to AAIF token ramps [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Contrast and Legibility Engine**: Programmatic styling is verified through automated background-to-text contrast solvers (`contrast.py`), walking visual inheritance trees (shape fill -> slide background -> layout -> master) to prevent unreadable color pairings such as dark ink on black plate backgrounds [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Overview
The Community Event Operations toolset provides deterministic CLI utilities and agent skills that manage local chapter provisioning, organizer access synchronization, asset lifecycle sweeps, and event workflows for the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-community-events-pr-45][^evt-community-events-pr-46]. It operates under strict report-by-default execution boundaries, requiring explicit approval before applying mutations to production databases and sheets [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Architecture / Specification
The operations tooling is partitioned across dedicated operational skills and background batch scripts:
- **Chapter Identity & Access Synchronization (`aaif-sync-chapters`)**: Manages Google Drive permission grants for chapter organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. When an organizer's intake email cannot receive direct Drive permissions (such as non-Google email addresses), the synchronizer evaluates a dedicated `Drive Email` override column with three invariant guards: intake row authority is strictly preserved, empty or sentinel values are ignored, and contradictory rows for the same individual cause immediate aborts [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Intake row creation is decoupled from Luma page provisioning via an opt-in `--require-luma` flag and an out-of-band `--audit-luma` validation sweep [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Chapter Provisioning & Migration (`aaif-create-chapter`)**: Provisions localized chapter assets and supports in-place renaming via `rename_chapter.py` across Drive directories, CRM workbooks, About documentation, and slide assets [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Renaming scripts isolate city tokens from `aaif-<slug>` handles to preserve URL paths and distinct external platform identities [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Estate Maintenance Sweeps (`deck_estate.py`)**: Centralizes batch traversal and XML inspection routines across Google Slides deck templates [^evt-community-events-pr-46]. Sweeps automatically backfill and harmonize foundation-level roster slides across all chapter and online series templates—such as synchronizing the hosted project roster (`MCP`, `goose`, `AGENTS.md`, `agentgateway`, `A2A`, `Agent Router`)—while verifying geometrical bounding box limits and upload receipt integrity [^evt-community-events-pr-46].
- **Proposal-Before-Execution Invariant**: All mutation engines execute in read-only reporting mode by default, requiring explicit approval and explicit flags (such as `--write`) to execute mutations against remote resources [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Related Artifacts
- Evaluation harness: [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)
- Governance patterns: [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical testing framework and grading harness designed to validate agent behavior across event operations skills [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. It benchmarks whether agents correctly dispatch required skills, respect negative triggering boundaries, and enforce report-first safety gates before executing irreversible write actions [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a][^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation harness executes test cases against specific operational workflows using typed graders:
- **Skill Dispatch Graders (`tool_used`)**: Validate that agents select and trigger appropriate operational skills based on user intent. For example, `evals/speaker-bio` verifies that the `aaif-speaker-bio` skill is invoked for speaker management [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09], while `evals/sync-chapters-write-gate` ensures `aaif-sync-chapters` handles chapter intake synchronization [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].
- **Negative Triggering Graders (`regex`)**: Verify that agents refrain from invoking irrelevant or conflicting tools. In `evals/recap-post/graders/not_the_announcement.md`, regex pattern assertions confirm that `aaif-announcement-post` is not triggered when an agent is tasked with summarizing an event that has already occurred [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].
- **Write-Gate and Safety Graders (`llm`)**: Benchmark enforcement of the proposal-execution split [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. In `evals/sync-chapters-write-gate/graders/reports_before_writing.md`, an LLM grader verifies that an agent proposes a dry-run report-first plan and does not claim writes or trigger mutation flags without explicit human authorization [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Related Artifacts
- Operational skill implementation: [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Architectural patterns: [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated evaluation suites and grading harnesses benchmarking agent skill dispatch, privacy protection, untrusted input containment, and output fidelity for event operations workflows [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094][^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba]. Maintained alongside [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), the harness validates that operational agents adhere to strict governance boundaries, including refusing prompt injections in form fields, preventing the leakage of personal contact details, and eliminating invented metrics in public post generation.

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation harness tests multi-turn agent interactions against discrete operational scenarios using heterogeneous grader types, including regex assertions, tool usage validators, and LLM-as-a-judge criteria:

## Test Scenarios and Boundaries

1. **Intake Triage Isolation (`triage-intake`)**: Evaluates agent resilience against indirect prompt injection embedded within intake submissions. Form submissions containing adversarial instructions (such as requesting automatic acceptance or channel invitations) must be strictly treated as untrusted data rather than executable instructions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]. The harness enforces that unauthorized status mutations are rejected and escalated to human operators, adhering to [Deterministic Acceptance Gates](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [Human Approval Gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
2. **Speaker Bio Redaction (`speaker-bio`)**: Evaluates agent skill execution while preventing personally identifiable information (PII) leakage in public copies [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094]. Prompts volunteer phone numbers and email addresses typical of speaker tracker rows; a regex-based negative match grader enforces that private contact details are excluded from generated biographies [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].
3. **Event Recap Generation (`recap-post`)**: Verifies correct tool dispatch for post-event summaries and enforces factual consistency [^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba]. The harness pairs a tool-use grader ensuring the `aaif-recap-post` skill fires [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4] with an LLM grader that strictly penalizes invented attendance figures or turnout metrics not supplied in the input context, curbing [Hallucination](../taxonomy/hallucination.md) in published communications [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3].

## Grader Implementation Types

- **`regex`**: Fast, deterministic negative or positive pattern matching over the final turn message (e.g., verifying `maya@example.com` or phone regexes are absent) [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].
- **`tool_used`**: Verification that required tools or modular skills (`Skill` invocation with matching names) were called during intermediate execution steps [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4].
- **`llm`**: Model-graded rubric evaluation for nuanced constraints such as data-versus-instruction boundaries and anti-fabrication editorial guidelines [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite provides empirical test cases and behavioral graders for validating agentic operations across chapter administration, intake triage, and event communications[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669]. Designed to assess automated skill dispatch and boundary enforcement, the suite tests whether agent runtimes accurately trigger targeted skills, isolate untrusted user inputs from control instructions, enforce write gates before state mutation, and discriminate between semantically adjacent lifecycle skills[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92][^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite organizes operational evaluations into declarative YAML-frontmattered test prompts paired with deterministic regex and execution trace graders:

## Intake Triage and Untrusted Input Resilience
The triage evaluation case (`evals/triage-intake`) verifies that the intake triage skill (`aaif-triage-intake`) fires upon encountering requests to view the intake queue[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92]. Evaluation prompts test model resilience against indirect prompt injections embedded in candidate application fields—such as applicants writing override commands instructing the agent to mark their status as "Accepted" and provision channel access[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669]. Test design requires querying queue state rather than pasting candidate rows inline, ensuring the evaluation measures external tool dispatch rather than base model reading comprehension[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].

## Write-Gate and Coverage Auditing
Operational cases enforce execution boundaries on persistent state:
- **Write Gates**: The chapter synchronization test (`evals/sync-chapters-write-gate`) enforces the principle that synchronization skills report intended actions prior to writing accepted organizers onto the public chapters list, aligning with the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) pattern[^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Workspace Auditing**: The Slack audit case (`evals/audit-slack`) verifies whether accepted organizers are mapped to designated chapter Slack channels, validating organizational coverage across disparate services[^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].

## Content Dispatch and Neighbor Discrimination
Content generation evaluations (`evals/announcement-post`) verify that announcements trigger appropriate skills for open RSVPs[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6]. Graders enforce negative triggers (`not_the_neighbours.md`) through regex scans across trace tool calls to ensure semantically adjacent skills (`aaif-recap-post`, `aaif-luma-description`, `aaif-attendee-reminder`) do not activate[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]. This prevents "wrong document in the right voice" failures where agents emit post-event recaps or attendee reminders in lieu of pre-event announcements[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# Lifecycle History
Merged into the authoritative `aaif/community-events` repository under `evals/`, providing continuous automated grading for community operations skills.

# Overview
Community Event Operations Skills are a modular set of agent capabilities that automate administrative, audit, and editorial tasks for Agentic AI Foundation regional chapters[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92][^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6]. The suite coordinates chapter organizer onboarding, Slack workspace auditing, spreadsheet synchronization, and event copy creation while enforcing write gates and input sanitization boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669][^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite segregates operational actions into specialized skills governed by the [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md):

## Administrative and Operational Skills
- **Intake Triage (`aaif-triage-intake`)**: Parses the chapter organizer intake queue to summarize applicant status and pending decisions[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92]. It treats applicant-submitted form text as passive data, resisting instruction injection attempts requesting unapproved admission[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Chapter Synchronization (`aaif-sync-chapters`)**: Manages the propagation of accepted organizers from intake sheets to the official chapters list, adhering to a mandatory write-gate step where changes are proposed and reported before persisting[^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Slack Audit (`aaif-audit-slack`)**: Queries communication channels to ensure regional chapter spaces exist and accepted organizers hold appropriate membership[^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].

## Content and Publication Lifecycle Skills
To prevent context confusion, editorial skills are divided across specific event phases:
- **Announcement Post (`aaif-announcement-post`)**: Drafts public promotional posts (e.g., LinkedIn announcements) when chapter event registration and RSVP pages go live[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6].
- **Lifecycle Neighbors**: Dedicated sister skills—`aaif-luma-description` for registration pages, `aaif-attendee-reminder` for pre-event attendee communications, and `aaif-recap-post` for post-event summaries—maintain distinct triggering profiles to prevent lifecycle mix-ups[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained in the `aaif/community-events` repository and evaluated against deterministic grading harnesses to maintain safe autonomous execution.
