proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry standard modeling causal links between model calls, approval gates, tool executions, and external side effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry standard developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group that defines structured representations for multi-turn agent execution traces, causal context linkage, and downstream effect attribution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Rather than relying on coarse session grouping, the model explicitly links triggering work, model call invocations, policy approvals, and observed side effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Causal Linkage Requirements
Session membership alone does not explain which unit of work caused an LLM call or what external state changed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. The trace model formalizes explicit causal relationships across three key interactions:
1. **Model Calls and Retries**: Visible model call attempts (whether successful or failed) are explicitly associated with their triggering unit of work[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Reported token and resource usage is counted once across retries, while hidden runtime retries and unavailable metrics remain explicitly recorded as unknown rather than assumed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
2. **Approval Decisions**: Human or automated authorization decisions must bind directly to a specific proposed action record (`P1`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. A denial is formally modeled and prohibited from generating fictional tool executions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Crucially, an observed approval record is not treated as proof of downstream enforcement[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
3. **Tool Execution and External Effects**: When an agent initiates a tool execution (`E1`), external service receipts (such as ticketing or cloud provider mutation IDs) are correlated back to both the tool execution and original proposal[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. If an external confirmation receipt is missing, the downstream effect status remains marked as unknown[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

## Interoperability and Ecosystem Mapping
The trace model interfaces with distributed tracing standards such as W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry gen_ai semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. Integration efforts explore federating traces across runtime registries, agent routers, and the Agent Resource Discovery ([`../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md`](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)) ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08 / 2026-09**: The Observability and Traceability Working Group formulated a nine-task execution plan, with Task 6 standardizing relationships between model calls, approvals, tool invocations, and external side effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **2026-09-16**: Working group announced initial tasks targeting a reference implementation of the trace behavior model by late September 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

mutations.rationale: Update boundary matrix coverage and scoping criteria to reflect the six runtime boundaries and eight observable properties identified in the WG gap analysis.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Gap Model
proposed_concept.description: Matrix mapping agentic system execution boundaries against observable telemetry dimensions to identify coverage and gaps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Gap Model is an architectural reference framework mapping observability boundaries across agentic software stacks against required telemetry properties[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]. Maintained as an initiative of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it establishes which operational boundaries are covered by existing distributed tracing standards and flags unresolved gaps such as decision provenance and authorization downscoping[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

# Architecture / Specification

## Target Boundaries
The gap model evaluates telemetry capture across six distinct operational interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]:
- **Agent → Skill**: Invocation, parameter validation, and prompt injection filtering at the agent-to-skill boundary[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Skill → Tool**: Capability dispatch, schema conformance, and sandboxed tool execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Agent → Agent**: Direct peer delegation, coordination, and subagent state tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Agent → MCP Server**: Model Context Protocol client-server interactions, tool enumeration, and session boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Agent → A2A Peer**: Cross-domain agent-to-agent protocol communications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Agent → Gateway / Runtime**: Transport egress, policy proxying, credential injection, and runtime execution environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

## Observable Dimensions
At each boundary, the framework evaluates observability across eight core dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]:
1. **Identity**: Verification of caller, agent, and delegated principals.
2. **Context**: Causal tracking of conversational and task context propagation.
3. **Relationship**: Parent-child and caller-callee execution hierarchies.
4. **Lifecycle**: State progression from initialization through completion or failure.
5. **Outcome**: Structured status indicators and execution outputs.
6. **Provenance**: Lineage of decisions, tool calls, and model outputs.
7. **Security**: Policy gate evaluations, permission enforcement, and sandbox isolation.
8. **Timing**: Latency breakdown, queue delays, and runtime execution duration.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Scoped in the Observability and Traceability Working Group as a foundational gap analysis deliverable with planned alignment to the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG and Agent-to-Agent standard groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite and Plumbing Guards
proposed_concept.description: Testing harness evaluating agent skill dispatch triggers, neighbor collisions, and automated architectural drift guards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical benchmarking harness and architectural guardrail suite for skills within the `aaif/community-events` repository[^evt-community-events-pr-47]. It validates that skill dispatch triggers fire on realistic user queries without colliding with adjacent skills in prompt description space, while enforcing code-level invariants for data redaction and skill packaging portability[^evt-community-events-pr-47][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Dispatch Evals and Graders
The evaluation harness evaluates skill activation through declarative test cases and graders[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76][^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]:
- **Trigger Verification (`skill_fires.md`)**: Uses realistic user prompts rather than verbatim skill descriptions to verify that models invoke the intended skill tool[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]. For example, `aaif-announcement-post` is tested to verify it triggers on "RSVPs are open" rather than post-event recaps[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].
- **Neighbor Disambiguation (`not_the_neighbours.md`)**: Checks that attendee-facing skills with similar semantic descriptions (such as event announcements, attendee updates, and community pulse) do not fire erroneously when an adjacent skill is targeted[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

## Architectural Plumbing and Invariant Enforcement
The repository pairs functional evals with static invariant checks[^evt-community-events-pr-47]:
- **Centralized Redaction (`check_no_local_redaction.py`)**: Enforces that PII masking flags and email sanitization utilities remain unified in a single module (`lib/redact.py`), preventing bugs where split flags permit sensitive addresses into CI logs[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Portability Boundary (`check_portable_skills.py`)**: Distinguishes between standalone skills intended to run decoupled (such as zipped distributions) and skills coupled to internal repository helper libraries (`lib/aaif_events`)[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Rule Synchronization**: Enforces byte-identical markdown banner synchronization across `SKILL.md` files for tooling rules, public copy rules, and legal footers[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: PR #47 introduced the eval harness for skill firing and neighbor disambiguation, consolidated API retry and redaction logic, and introduced CI drift guards for skill banners and portability boundaries[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Subprocess Boundary
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and telemetry propagation model analyzing the direct agent-to-tool local CLI subprocess boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI subprocess boundary analyzes telemetry propagation and causality modeling between an AI agent runtime and a tool executed as a local subprocess [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. This specification distinguishes between the canonical `Agent → Tool` semantic interaction and the underlying `Agent Runtime → Local Process` operational boundary that realizes it in local environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification
The boundary realization addresses context propagation, span hierarchy, and telemetry alignment across process forks:

- **Context Carrier**: Utilizes the OpenTelemetry Release Candidate specification for environment variables (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`, and `BAGGAGE`) to propagate W3C Trace Context and Baggage across process boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Composition**: Differentiates between runtime-level `execute_tool` spans and CLI process execution spans, addressing whether the agent runtime suppresses, nests, or shares spans during direct command execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Pre-execution Span-ID Reservation**: Implements pre-execution span-ID reservation—validated in the LoongSuite pilot—enabling parent spans to register deterministic trace relationships prior to executing the tool binary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Detached and Asynchronous Work**: Recommends OpenTelemetry Span Links over direct parent-child causality when tools execute detached or asynchronous background tasks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Resource Bootstrap**: Isolates process-level OpenTelemetry resource bootstrap from invocation-level carrier contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Lifecycle History
The boundary model was introduced by the Observability and Traceability Working Group in PR #35 as the initial concrete matrix pass addressing direct tool invocation gaps identified in issue #29 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It links to broader cross-boundary telemetry mapping in [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md).

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate cap enforcement, and organizer sync.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill automates chapter lifecycle management, organizer roster reconciliation, and audit telemetry for the Agentic AI Foundation chapter estate [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. The operations enforce hard capacity limits, maintain synchronization between Google Sheets intake databases and Slack channels, and guard against reporting false audit conclusions derived from Slack API scope constraints [^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Architecture / Specification
The operational suite manages chapters and Slack workspaces according to strict operational constraints:

- **Estate Ceiling and Lifecycle**: Imposes a hard limit of 100 chapters (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`), requiring dormant or coalesced chapters to be retired before new chapters are provisioned [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Chapters track lifecycle states via an explicit `Status` field (`Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, `Deprecated`) and a `Merged Into` pointer [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Organizer Channel Sync**: Automatically maintains the global `#local-champs` channel alongside `invite_organizers.py` to prevent roster drift for accepted organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Silence vs. Ignorance Invariant**: Audits explicitly treat missing records, stale sweeps, and unread archived channels as 'cannot say' rather than inactivity, requiring positive human message timestamps before flagging chapters for dormancy [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Measurement Limits and Scope Guardrails**: Scopes are verified prior to audit execution to prevent missing permissions (e.g., `users:read.email`) from registering as missing user accounts [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. It explicitly forbids using bulk-migration reset timestamps (`updated`) as proxy metrics for channel or member activity [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Lifecycle History
The 100-chapter cap and `#local-champs` automated reconciliation were implemented in PR #48 after finding that manual roster curation omitted 28 of 155 accepted organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Evaluation harnesses for sync workflows are tracked in [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md).

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and structured schema mapping open-source agentic AI runtimes, protocols, security gateways, and tracing platforms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape provides a structured taxonomy and comparative catalog of open-source runtimes, agent-to-agent protocols, control planes, and observability tools across the agent ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. It tracks foundational infrastructure hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation and external open-source projects, detailing protocol maturity, deployment models, and boundary enforcement capabilities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification
Key project additions in the landscape include:

- **A2A (Agent-to-Agent)**: Joined AAIF as a hosted project in August 2026 to provide a vendor-neutral interoperability layer [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. While A2A v1.0 introduced signed agent cards for capability discovery, verifying card identity claims against runtime behavioral telemetry remains an open research and standard track [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **agentgateway**: Contributed by solo.io to AAIF in June 2026, providing traffic mediation, policy enforcement, and gateway controls for Model Context Protocol (MCP) and A2A communications across major cloud marketplaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **Evidence Layer Gap**: Highlights the architectural need for independent boundary enforcement points—such as gateways and proxies—to capture corroborating execution telemetry without relying exclusively on self-reported agent assertions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History
The landscape was updated by the Observability and Traceability Working Group in PR #31 to formally record the admission of A2A and agentgateway into AAIF governance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

mutations.rationale: Update the cross-boundary observability model with control-plane evidence dimensions and the three-state reconciliation framework from issue #36 and PR #35.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Matrix mapping agentic system execution boundaries against observable telemetry dimensions to identify independent evidence and coverage gaps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model maps architectural interfaces within agentic systems against observable telemetry dimensions to detect visibility gaps and verify execution claims [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]. By analyzing control-plane boundaries—such as gateways, proxies, and runtime sandboxes—the model defines how external observations corroborate or contradict self-reported agent telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework evaluates cross-boundary telemetry across standardized dimensions:

- **Observation Sources**: Disaggregates telemetry by generation origin, distinguishing agent runtimes, tool subprocesses, and independent intermediaries such as gateways (e.g., [agentgateway](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)) and kernel monitors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **Observation Relationships**: Categorizes boundary signals by their evidentiary relationship to the agent action: direct observation, corroborating evidence, contradictory evidence, or derived secondary telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
- **Three-State Reconciliation**: Evaluates claimed actions through a tri-state reconciliation model—*agreement*, *contradiction*, and *no independent evidence*—ensuring that missing independent telemetry is treated as an explicit non-verification state rather than an assumed corroboration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
- **Operational Boundary Mapping**: Details field mappings for execution boundaries, including context propagation across local subprocesses via [Agent-to-Tool CLI Subprocess Boundary](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md) and network gateways [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Lifecycle History
Formulated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model incorporated direct CLI subprocess mapping via PR #35 and control-plane evidence classification under issue #36 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

mutations.rationale: Define witness_scope as proposed in ws-taxonomy-landscape issue #53 to distinguish the custody axis of evidence from forgeability.

proposed_concept.title: Witness Scope
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy classification designating the custody category of an entity holding or attesting an agent action record.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`witness_scope` designates the custody category of a witness that holds or attests a record about an agent action [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53]. It isolates the question of who retains possession of the record from whether the underlying content is technically forgeable by the subject it describes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy partitions witness custody across three distinct levels [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53]:
- **`SELF`**: The record is held by the agent itself or its immediate local execution runtime [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].
- **`PEER`**: The record is held or attested by an immediate counterparty participating in the same shared transaction or agreement [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].
- **`EXTERNAL`**: The record is held or attested by an independent party operating outside the bilateral relationship [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].

### Separation of Custody and Forgeability
Witness scope captures record custody rather than forgeability vantage [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53]. For example, an `EXTERNAL` party holding an execution record may still hold an unverifiable account if it relies on symmetric keys or self-reported data produced by the emitting agent [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53]. Witness scope is formally paired with a planned companion contrast term, `verification-basis`, which addresses the substrate versus artifact vantage axis [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in issue #53 within the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream following cross-organization discussions within the OWASP GenAI-Security-Project agent-control-standard milestone [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-53].

# References
- [Self-Reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md)
- [Evidence Strength Labels](../taxonomy/evidence-strength-labels.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Emission Conformant
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy classification designating an artifact claim asserting structural schema validity at the emission boundary without operational behavioral guarantees.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`emission-conformant` defines an artifact claim asserting compliance exclusively at the boundary serialization layer, confirming that an emitted record matches a canonical schema without validating execution behavior or factual authenticity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].

# Architecture / Specification
An emission-conformant classification establishes minimal contract adherence for agent records [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50]:
- **Syntactic Conformance**: The payload parses successfully and adheres to field, type, and serialization rules defined by the target schema [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].
- **No Operational Guarantee**: The claim makes no representation regarding runtime invariants, policy compliance, or proper agent state transitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].
- **No Truth Assertion**: The classification does not verify whether the claims contained within the payload represent an accurate account of physical or logical execution [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].

This distinction prevents unqualified claims of system conformance from obscuring unverified agent operations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50]. It serves as a precursor to the contrast term `operationally conformant` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in issue #50 of the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream, emerging from claim-scope classifications introduced in the OWASP GenAI-Security-Project agent-control-standard discussions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-50].

# References
- [Witness Scope](../taxonomy/witness-scope.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated grading and test harness verifying agent routing, execution ordering, and copy compliance across the AAIF community events estate [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5] [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. It employs programmatic regex assertions and model-graded rubrics to prevent skill routing collisions and policy drift [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5] [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite targets several operational dimensions across event management workflows:

### Skill Routing and Neighbor Collisions
Estate-wide operational synchronization depends on hierarchical skill selection [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]:
- **Front-Door Orchestration (`skill_fires.md`)**: Verifies that high-level, drift-oriented operator requests invoke the `aaif-sync` orchestrator skill rather than triggering sub-phase skills prematurely [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
- **Neighbor Collision Isolation (`not_a_phase_skill.md`)**: Asserts that closely related sub-engine phase skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) do not activate autonomously when a generalized sync request is submitted [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

### Pipeline Sequencing Invariants
- **Ordered Operations (`order_is_respected.md`)**: Enforces an LLM evaluation standard ensuring multi-step maintenance plans run as ordered sequences rather than unconstrained steps [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]. Read/reporting phases must precede write operations, and chapter spreadsheets and CRM records must be confirmed prior to granting Drive permissions or mutating Slack channels [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

### Content Compliance and Legal Safeguards
- **Footer Validation (`legal_footer.md`)**: Enforces regex checks ensuring attendee-facing announcements include standing links to both the Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy, eliminating footer drift across publication workflows [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

mutations.rationale: Captures the newly proposed term from ws-taxonomy-landscape issue #51 establishing operational behavioral compliance as the paired contrast to emission-conformant.

proposed_concept.title: Operationally Conformant
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy classification designating a claim asserting that runtime system or agent behavior satisfies specification requirements regardless of record schema validation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`Operationally conformant` is a taxonomy term defining an assertion that a system or agent behaves in accordance with standard runtime requirements, without asserting whether emitted observation or telemetry records strictly validate against a canonical schema[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-51].

It serves as the paired contrast to [emission-conformant](./emission-conformant.md), which designates the inverse: structural schema validity of emitted records without guaranteeing behavioral adherence[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-51]. Together, the pair decomposes unqualified "conformant" labels to prevent conflating runtime behavior with data formatting.

# Architecture / Specification
The classification emerged from claim-scope vocabularies developed in the OWASP GenAI-Security-Project agent-control-standard discussions regarding witness scope splits[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-51].

- **Assertion target**: Runtime execution dynamics, policy enforcement, and operational behavior.
- **Excluded guarantees**: Syntactic or structural validity of serialization formats or trace records.
- **Relationship**: Paired with [emission-conformant](./emission-conformant.md) to decompose audit claims into independent data and execution dimensions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-51].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` issue #51 by the Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group as part of the paired-contrast definitions pass[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-51].

mutations.rationale: Captures the term proposed in ws-taxonomy-landscape issue #54 defining evidence evaluation resolved into agreement, contradiction, or absent independent evidence.

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy classification designating the comparison of an agent claim against independent observation into agreement, contradiction, or absent evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`Three-state reconciliation` is a taxonomy term defining an evidence evaluation model where an agent claim is compared against independent observations and classified into one of three distinct states: agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

The framework prevents silent defaults by elevating missing independent telemetry to an explicit evaluative state rather than treating it as verification failure or implicit confirmation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# Architecture / Specification
Formulated within the Observability & Traceability Working Group in discussion around control-plane telemetry as an evidence source[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54], three-state reconciliation prevents conflating checked claims with unchecked ones:

1. **Agreement**: The independent observation directly corroborates the agent's asserted action or state.
2. **Contradiction**: Independent boundary observations refute or diverge from the agent's asserted claim.
3. **No Independent Evidence**: No external observation exists to assess the claim, exposing an audit visibility gap rather than asserting fault.

This pattern operates in conjunction with [witness-scope](./witness-scope.md) evaluations and verification-basis frameworks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` issue #54 following initial framing in Observability & Traceability Working Group issue #36[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry standard modeling causal links between model calls, approval gates, tool executions, and external effects across multi-turn sessions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry contract and data model designed to trace causal and temporal relationships across autonomous and semi-autonomous agent operations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It establishes formal identity definitions for interactions and models the progression from prompt generation to real-world external impact.

# Architecture / Specification
The v0.1 draft shared contract defines core identity boundaries, relational topologies, and operational interpretation rules[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

### Identity Entities
The model formalizes distinct lifecycle identities:
- **Conversation**: The overarching goal-oriented user interaction.
- **Runtime Session**: The concrete hosting environment and process execution lifecycle.
- **Turn**: Bounded step demarcating prompt intake, evaluation, and output generation.
- **Model Call**: Invocation of an underlying foundation model or inference endpoint.
- **Proposed Action**: Agent-generated intent or invocation payload prior to execution.
- **Approval Decision**: Human or policy enforcement checkpoint sign-off or rejection.
- **Tool Execution**: Concrete runtime execution of an external capability or MCP tool.
- **External Effect**: Mutating or visible side-effect produced outside the agent boundary.

### Interpretation Rules
To ensure consistent analysis across distributed systems, trace evaluation mandates baseline interpretation rules[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Missing observation is unknown, not zero**: Missing spans or records represent absence of telemetry rather than an assertion of zero occurrences.
- **Deduplication by correlation key**: Duplicate event deliveries must resolve via deterministic correlation keys.
- **Order invariance**: Out-of-order trace ingestion must not alter analytical outcomes.

The specification also maintains formal crosswalks to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and standard AAIF terminology[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
Initial draft specification introduced under PR #51 in `aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability` as part of issue #41[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate synchronization, and human-gated workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`community-event-operations` is an operational skill suite managing the lifecycle, communication channels, and intake pipelines for AAIF community chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. It integrates automated directory audits, Google Workspace access control, and Slack estate synchronization behind human approval gates.

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture organizes around `aaif-sync` as a unified front door orchestrating an idempotent pipeline structured across a two-dimensional matrix of operational phase and execution stage[^evt-community-events-pr-49]:

### Phase × Stage Pipeline
- **Axes**: Execution traverses phases (chapters, organizers, Slack, Drive access) through sequential stages: `gather`, `plan`, and `execute`[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Human Gate Triage**: Triage operations are strictly human-gated; automated runners report queue depth and summarize unassigned items (exiting with status code 2 when rows wait) without autonomously deciding intake[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Configuration & Estate State**: Chapter matching is driven by the Community Chapters List spreadsheet rather than repository JSON configs[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]. An `Ops Notes` column is maintained by human operators and quoted without automated modification[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6][^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Structured Findings**: Engines emit standardized finding datasets containing severity, subject, and remediation recommendations into local run directories, compiling into a consolidated run report[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Ephemeral State**: Runners maintain no cross-run state; local caches have a one-day lifespan and are barred from version control commits[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History
Refactored in community-events PR #49 to migrate all skill instructions into code-driven procedural standards with consolidated front-door pipeline management[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry model and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping capturing continuity, model calls, approval gates, and downstream effects across agent sessions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification defined by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to follow an autonomous agent's reasoning, execution turns, pauses, and external system boundaries using [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Rather than prescribing isolated span schemas, the model standardizes how trace systems record causal relationships across asynchronous turn boundaries, model retries, governance decisions, and external mutations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

The standard addresses four foundational observability questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity:** Identifying which turns belong together across session pauses, process restarts, or durable waits.
- **Calls and Retries:** Correlating foundation model API invocations and provider-side retries to a distinct turn without double-counting work.
- **Approvals:** Linking governance evaluations directly to the concrete action proposed and tracking whether that action was authorized and executed.
- **Effects:** Associating an agent tool execution with independently observed external resource mutations.

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Correlation Model

The trace model uses standard OpenTelemetry span contexts enriched with domain-specific semantic attributes and causal link collections[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Turn Boundaries:** Evaluates a default candidate topology of one distributed trace per interaction turn while retaining root propagation when an incoming caller trace context exists[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Turn-entry spans record resume tokens, session identifiers, and parent turn links.
- **Governance and Approvals:** Bridges the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern to execution spans. The model establishes that an observed approval record reflects a recorded decision event, not cryptographic proof of runtime enforcement[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Downstream Effects:** Captures links between tool call spans and independent telemetry records produced by target systems (for example, ticket creation services or cloud resource APIs)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Observation Semantics:** Follows explicit three-state observation rules where missing telemetry indicates an unknown state rather than zero activity or guaranteed success[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

## Reference Workflow and Validation

The model's initial validation harness implements an order-support workflow covering an investigation step, ticket creation proposal, approval wait, and resumed action execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Validation requires concurrent reference implementations in [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and an independent secondary agent SDK to prevent vendor-specific coupling[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Telemetry outputs must be parsed by at least two independent query implementations to verify deterministic interpretation under delayed, out-of-order, or missing span conditions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History

Following working group sessions on 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-19, the working group ratified a formal 9-task execution plan targeting September 2026 delivery[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The tasks encompass baseline definitions, contract formalization aligned with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), multi-agent reference implementations, test fixtures, and upstream contribution into OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate synchronization, and idempotent Google Workspace API operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated execution capabilities for AAIF chapter intake, spreadsheet synchronization, badge management, and digital estate governance across Google Workspace services[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. It enforces strict isolation and validation boundaries to ensure that automated operations do not corrupt workspace structures, duplicate operational files, or leak sensitive tokens into public diagnostic logs[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

## Idempotency and Non-Idempotent Retry Guards

External API calls to Google Drive and Sheets that create or mutate structural resources—such as `drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, and `addSheet`—cannot safely use standard network retry logic[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Because transport timeouts cannot distinguish between a server-side success with a lost response and an unlanded request, automatic retries risk creating duplicate folders, files, or tabs that downstream tasks fail to reconcile[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

The operational suite standardizes on explicit mitigation layers[^evt-community-events-pr-51]:
- **Explicit Non-Retry Policy (`NO_RETRY`):** Structural write calls are explicitly flagged with `NO_RETRY` in the central `aaif_events.gws` library, disabling multi-attempt replay on indeterminate responses[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Static Guard Check (`check_non_idempotent_retries.py`):** An automated repository verification script analyzes call sites across Drive and Sheets integrations to statically detect unguarded non-idempotent write calls[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Consolidated Wrapper Architecture:** Local `gws` execution scripts across `create_chapter.py`, `create_series.py`, and `install_ops_notes.py` were retired in favor of the shared `aaif_events.gws` module to prevent wrapper logic drift and unscrubbed subprocess executions[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

## Telemetry and Environment Scrubbing

Subprocess invocations that execute Google Workspace CLI commands sanitize their execution context to protect credentials[^evt-community-events-pr-51]:
- **Token Scrubbing:** Environment variables matching sensitive token structures, including legacy `AAIF_SLACK_TOKEN` variants, are scrubbed prior to spawning child processes[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Error Log Redaction:** Command failure messages explicitly report only the API verb and error code via `stderr`, preventing sensitive file content or spreadsheet cell data in `stdout` from entering tracebacks or issue reports[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

## Schema and Validation Range Resolution

CRM synchronization logic (`sync_crm.py` and `migrate_interested_in.py`) evaluates spreadsheet data validation definitions using range unioning rather than naive whitespace splitting[^evt-community-events-pr-50]. Single-column dropdown ranges that span non-contiguous row intervals (e.g., `E2:E8 E10:E1002`) resolve into their constituent column indices without falsely triggering multi-column validation rejections[^evt-community-events-pr-50].

The workstream tracks monthly delivery milestones submitted to the Technical Committee under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]:

- **2026-08:** Reviewed 53 terms across three terminology syncs, selecting 37 terms and assembling four pull requests scheduled for a formal Technical Committee approval vote on 2026-09-14[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish vendor-neutral conventions, shared semantics, and reference implementations for agentic telemetry across execution frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill packages automated workflows, validation checks, and estate synchronization pipelines for AAIF community chapters, event registrations, and organizer directories [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The pipeline enforces deterministic reconciliation across external SaaS platforms including Slack and Google Workspace while providing regression evaluation via the [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The core sync runner coordinates multi-step estate reconciliation across an 18-step pipeline [^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53]. Key operational optimizations and safeguards include:
- **Ephemeral Run Memos**: Read operations against Google Workspace and Slack directories are memoized within thread-safe append-only files (AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO, AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO) during report runs [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Read memoization is bypassed during write runs to prevent serving stale state, and memo files are deleted immediately upon pipeline exit or interrupt [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Worker Concurrency**: Chapter workbook parsing executes across a dedicated six-worker thread pool in sync_crm [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Power Management Guard**: On macOS hosts, long-running sync executions spawn a background caffeinate process bound to the runner process ID to prevent system sleep and session timeouts [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# References
- Community events repository: https://github.com/aaif/community-events

proposed_concept.title: Intended Purpose
proposed_concept.description: The documented use, conditions, and context for which an AI system is designated by its provider prior to deployment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Intended purpose defines the explicit use, context, and operational conditions for which an AI system is designated by its provider or developer, as documented in accompanying instructions and specifications.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65] It stands in contrast to runtime intent—the dynamic objective an agent or human operator pursues during execution—by establishing the pre-deployment legal and architectural boundary for authorized system behavior.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]

# Architecture / Specification

Within the taxonomy coordinated alongside the [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), intended purpose functions as an authoritative benchmark for evaluating operational integrity and compliance.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]

Key characteristics include:
- **Provider ownership**: Intended purpose belongs strictly to the party designing or supplying the system and is authored prior to deployment, rather than being synthesized dynamically during an agent run.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]
- **Misuse baseline**: Derived from statutory standards such as European Union AI Act Article 3(12), intended purpose acts as the reference baseline against which "reasonably foreseeable misuse" (Article 3(13)), agent derailment, and unauthorized exploitation are measured.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]
- **Contrast with intent**: While runtime intent represents what an agent or principal attempts to achieve during task execution, intended purpose restricts the envelope of sanctioned functionality.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]

# Lifecycle History

Proposed in issue discussions within the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream to resolve ambiguity caused by treating intended purpose as a synonym for runtime intent.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-65]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and structured schema mapping open-source agentic AI runtimes, protocols, security tooling, and regulatory regimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and open-source data schema maintained by the Agentic AI Foundation to categorize runtime engines, communication protocols, developer tooling, and global regulatory regimes shaping agentic systems [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]. Maintained in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), it provides developers, auditors, and enterprise adopters with a transparent map of the agentic AI software ecosystem and adjacent compliance frameworks.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape repository maintains curated entries across technology layers and regulatory domains [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]. Key structural rules and category specifications include:

- **Editorial Schemas and Source Validation**: Entries must specify verified metadata including canonical homepage URLs and descriptions, while strictly prohibiting non-neutral marketing superlatives such as 'world's first' [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]. Statutory entries must link to primary authoritative upstream sources rather than third-party explainers [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].
- **Enacted Legislation & Acts**: Catalogs binding statutory frameworks governing automated systems and artificial intelligence. Maintenance tracking accounts for legislative supersession, such as updating Colorado listings to the Automated Decision-Making Technology Act (SB 26-189, repealing and reenacting SB 24-205 following the SB 25B-004 delay) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].
- **Standards & Risk Frameworks**: Distinct classification strictly separating voluntary guidance documents—such as Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI—from binding statutory enactments [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].

# Lifecycle History
- ws-taxonomy-landscape#67 identified structural corrections to the 'Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes' taxonomy section, enforcing primary legislative sourcing and distinguishing voluntary frameworks from binding law [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing identity, cryptographic attestation, delegation boundaries, and legal-role accountability for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral specifications, attestation models, and trust architectures for autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]. The group addresses machine identity, delegation chains, authorized execution policies, and alignment between technical mechanisms and international legal accountability regimes in collaboration with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on securing interactions across agents, platforms, and human sponsors through cryptographic identity, evidence verification, and unambiguous role accountability [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]. Key architectural priorities include:

- **Technical versus Statutory Semantic Disambiguation**: Resolving discrepancies where engineering terms conflict with statutory definitions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]:
  - *Operator*: Disambiguating operational execution roles from statutory umbrella designations under EU AI Act Article 3(8) (covering providers, product manufacturers, deployers, authorized representatives, importers, and distributors) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
  - *Relying Party*: Clarifying system-level consumption versus regulated eIDAS entities (Regulation 2024/1183 Article 5b) requiring pre-declared intended use [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
  - *Consent*: Distinguishing operational task authorization from GDPR Articles 4(11) and 7 lawful bases, ISO/IEC 27560 consent records, and PSD2 Article 64 strong authentication mandates [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
  - *Attestation*: Separating IETF RATS architectural evidence from eIDAS 2 qualified and non-qualified electronic attestations of attributes [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
  - *Mandate*: Differentiating agent authorization objects from civil-law agency contracts and European Digital Identity (EUDI) power-of-representation attestations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Delegation Chain Custody and Legal Roles**: Mapping legal-role attribution across architectural actors (sponsor, workspace device, logical agent, tool invocation) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]. Handoffs across organizational boundaries must account for legal log custody requirements, such as EU AI Act Article 19 provider logs, Article 26(6) deployer logs, and GDPR Article 28 processor versus controller disclosure records [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History
- wg-identity-and-trust#10 raised requirements to reconcile engineering terminology and delegation chain provenance with EU AI Act, eIDAS, and GDPR compliance structures prior to taxonomy publication [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing measurement methodologies, failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, and consistency guidance for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing rigorous measurement methodologies, empirical failure taxonomies, and testing frameworks for agentic AI workflows [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12]. The group develops standardized metrics, benchmark suites, and validation procedures to evaluate reasoning integrity, operational consistency, and behavioral boundaries across agent deployments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables around empirical benchmarks, failure taxonomy catalogs, and verification procedures [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12]. Key deliverable scopes and jurisdictional boundaries include:

- **Deliverable D4 (Quality Thresholds)**: Formulating operational thresholds for accuracy, robustness, and stability [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12]. Workstream guidance requires explicit jurisdictional scoping to avoid unstated presumptions of regulatory conformity—such as EU AI Act Article 15 requirements for accuracy and robustness harmonized under Article 40 standards (CEN-CENELEC JTC 21)—while clarifying applicability against voluntary frameworks like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].
- **Deliverable D6 (Evaluation and Conformance Guidance)**: Providing self-assessment tools, conformance verification artifacts, and pass/fail validation suites [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12]. Terminology is explicitly framed as consistency checks or conformance to AAIF technical vocabularies to avoid confusion with formal statutory 'conformity assessments' defined under EU AI Act Article 43 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

# Lifecycle History
- wg-accuracy-and-reliability#12 introduced naming and scoping guidance for deliverables D4 and D6 to ensure clear demarcation between technical foundation benchmarks and formal statutory conformity assessments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group aligning agentic AI architectures with global AI regulations, compliance regimes, and standardized governance themes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group evaluates emerging AI policy instruments and establishes technical frameworks to align agentic AI architectures with global regulatory requirements [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group synthesizes compliance obligations into engineering-grade reference baselines and gap analyses [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group standardizes regulatory mapping across a formal baseline of 16 evaluation themes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:
- **Governance & accountability**: Institutional ownership, human sign-offs, RACI matrices, and explicit risk acceptance.
- **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Prohibited versus permissible boundaries and tiered risk controls [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319], interfacing with [Agentic Use Case Classification](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md).
- **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundary enforcement, and control plane placement [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication and authorization models, acting-on-behalf-of semantics, and agent registries [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Machine-enforceable business rules, policy-as-code, and hard boundary constraints [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Data protection & privacy**: Personally identifiable information (PII) minimization, retention floors, and geographic residency [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Security & access controls**: Principle of least privilege, secrets protection, sandbox segmentation, and tool execution scopes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Model/agent risk management**: Pre-deployment validation, drift monitoring, robustness assessments, and change control [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) and human-on-the-loop (HOTL) oversight, escalation channels, and emergency [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) capabilities [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Action management**: Pre-execution verification gates, dual-control patterns, and action reversibility [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Monitoring & logging**: Verifiable audit trails, prompt and tool invocation logs, and decision rationale records [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection defenses, tool abuse mitigation, and autonomy boundary testing [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence and agent component provenance [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319], relating to [AI Agent Bill of Materials](../taxonomy/ai-agent-bill-of-materials.md).
- **Incident response**: Autonomous anomaly detection, blast radius containment, and statutory breach reporting [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Transparency & user disclosure**: Interaction notices, explainability mechanisms, and end-user disclosure standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
- **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Statutory retention schedules, execution trace reproducibility, and compliance evidence signing [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

To extract and analyze policies consistently across regional legal texts, the working group employs a standardized golden-source prompt harness [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, co-chairs Ryan Hagemann and Deborah Eng finalized the 16 baseline regulatory themes and standardized extraction prompts for Phase 2 of the comparative gap analysis across jurisdiction-specific instruments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and cross-boundary hardening standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security baselines, threat modeling methodologies, and defensive architectural patterns for autonomous AI agents and runtime environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. Led by chairs Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group drives cross-cutting security reviews and coordinates defenses against prompt injection, unconstrained tool invocation, and sandbox escape vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical agenda into four core deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive implementation guidance detailing static code smells, execution boundaries, and tool permissioning, transitioning into mainline acceptance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Structured gap analysis evaluating existing standards against agentic vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Hardened architectural patterns covering runtime isolation and boundary enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076], including [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Inter-group evaluation checklist driven by Govindaraj Palanisamy to audit security assumptions across other AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

The group formalizes contribution rules including standing pull request review windows in repository contributing documentation and coordinates external standards alignment with bodies such as ETSI TC SAI, OWASP, and Eclipse Enclave [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the group addressed protocol alignment following the donation of A2A to AAIF and initiated the cross-working group overlap checklist [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. In September 2026, the WG established standing PR review deadlines, integrated LLM provenance tracking via an automated taxonomy browser, and opened external dialogue with ETSI TC SAI [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry model and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping capturing reasoning continuity, model delegation, and execution causality.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a vendor-neutral telemetry specification and data model mapping agent reasoning loops, tool interactions, and subagent delegations to OpenTelemetry constructs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]. The model ensures that operational logs and traces maintain causal integrity and relationship verifiability across distributed multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model establishes explicit conformance criteria and test harnesses for exported telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]:
- **Relationship Conformance Testing**: Reusable validation suites that assert causal relationships and idempotency when records are delayed, dropped, or duplicated (such as confirming that duplicate action receipts result in a single confirmed state, or missing receipts result in unconfirmed states rather than phantom non-execution) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Language-Neutral Fixtures**: Synthetic test datasets and contribution templates enabling contributors to validate trace relationships without implementing a complete runtime engine [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Jurisdictional and Identity Harmonization**: Telemetry retention, audit-required events, and identity models are designed to adapt across regulatory regimes—distinguishing EU AI Act Article 12 event recording duties from Articles 19 and 26(6) retention windows, and handling pseudonymous persistent identifiers under GDPR Recital 30 versus US definitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].

The standard coordinates with [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) and provides trace schemas compatible with [Trace](../standards/trace.md).

# Lifecycle History
In August and September 2026, the Observability and Traceability Working Group advanced its nine-task execution plan, introducing Task 4 to build automated relationship test kits and contribution templates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42], while addressing cross-jurisdictional legal retention and identifier requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and classification schema mapping production agentic workflows across triggers, patterns, and boundary controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification provides an empirical taxonomy and inventory of real-world agentic workflows deployed in production systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Developed by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, it categorizes agent architectures by their triggers, human-in-the-loop governance patterns, coordination models, and execution boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification
The schema classifies production implementations across standardized workflow dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:
- **Trigger**: The invocation origin, such as manual invocation, external webhooks, or scheduled cron routines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Human Oversight Pattern**: The governing control checkpoint, spanning explicit human sign-offs, exception-based monitoring, or fully automated executions without gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Coordination Strategy**: Single-agent sequential executions, orchestrated subagent sweeps, or decentralized swarms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Workflow Structure**: Structural topology such as sequential pipelines, convergence loops, or directed acyclic graphs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

## Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis
A representative entry in the SDLC classification inventory is upstream SDK release impact analysis (derived from the Model Context Protocol Inspector `sdk-watch.yml`) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:
- **Classification**: Scheduled nightly trigger; no in-band HITL gate (informational issue comments); single-agent orchestrated execution; sequential pipeline workflow; short execution duration (<20 min) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Boundary Enforcement**: Implements the [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) at the job-permission level rather than through a runtime software gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. The analysis agent executes with a strictly read-only token and read-only tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`), prohibiting network and write operations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Output is deterministically scanned for leaked credentials before being passed as an artifact to a separate, write-scoped publishing job [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group expanded the SDLC inventory through PR #51, incorporating MCP Inspector's upstream SDK impact analysis as an architectural model for permission-enforced tool isolation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is a technical working group of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with surveying, coordinating, and standardizing vendor-neutral telemetry, behavioral trace specifications, and runtime observability models across agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

The group operates under the Linux Foundation umbrella to establish shared telemetry conventions across foundational technologies including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, AGENTS.md, Agentgateway, Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and AGNTCY [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group anchors its technical agenda across several living foundational documents and workstreams:

- **Prior Work and Landscape Survey (`PRIOR-WORK.md`):** Continuously tracks industry specifications and telemetry formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions (`semantic-conventions-genai`), Cursor Agent Trace, the OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS), AGNTCY Observe SDK, Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF 1.9 AI profiling), Monocle, and A2A traceability extensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Agent Observability Use Cases (`USE-CASES.md`):** Catalogs cross-cutting observability scenarios across nine categories: Debugging and Root Cause Analysis (A), Cost Management (B), Code Attribution (C), Evaluation and QA (D), Safety and Compliance (E), Multi-Agent Systems (F), Operational Monitoring (G), Research and Improvement (H), and Identity and Ownership (I) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. Recent additions include Use Case E4 for tamper-evident evidence supporting dispute resolution and I1 for cross-surface identity resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **Cross-Cutting Requirements:** Mandates explicit observation point identification (differentiating agent self-reporting from platform or security-sensor evidence), privacy minimization, sampling declarations, schema versioning, and causal correlation independent of clock synchronization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-15:** Initial publication of the Prior Work landscape survey and Use Cases catalog [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **2026-08-13:** Landscape refresh incorporating dedicated OTel GenAI repository restructuring, OCSF 1.9 agent profiling, and AGNTCY Observe SDK 1.0.43 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-18:** Adoption of Use Case E4 for tamper-evident audit evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]. Attribution corrections clarify chair Pavan Sudheendra's authorship of the cross-boundary observability framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-08-19:** Adoption of Use Case I1 addressing cross-surface identity resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the AAIF Observability and Traceability Working Group to standardize causal ordering, reasoning continuity, tool interactions, and delegation records across single and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

The specification standardizes how agent execution contexts, approvals, tool calls, and observed effects are emitted and correlated into portable trace records without reliance on proprietary runtime assumptions or vendor-specific telemetry wrappers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Architecture / Specification

The execution plan for the Agent Behavior Trace Model comprises nine phased implementation tasks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:

- **Independent Interpretation Verification (Task 7):** Mandates that telemetry exports must be interpreted consistently by at least two independently implemented readers or query paths without access to private runtime state, hidden fixture mappings, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Evaluation Criteria:** Verification suites evaluate trace reconstruction under variable record arrival orderings and incomplete or conflicting telemetry feeds. Test scenarios verify that approval records, execution observations, and external effects (such as external service tickets or receipts) are accurately and consistently reconciled by independent readers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08:** The Observability and Traceability Working Group established the nine-task execution plan to guide implementation, formalizing Task 7 to validate independent interpretation and reader conformance across multi-agent traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.description: Matrix mapping agentic system execution boundaries against observable telemetry dimensions to identify visibility gaps and instrumentation requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is an architectural matrix and evaluation framework that maps the operational boundaries of agentic systems against observable telemetry dimensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24]. The framework was authored by Pavan Sudheendra, chair of the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

The model identifies visibility gaps, trust assumptions, and instrumentation requirements when execution flows transition across the agent core, tool CLIs, remote MCP servers, and autonomous agent-to-agent interfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

# Architecture / Specification

The framework systematically analyzes observation fidelity across structural system boundaries:

- **Agent-to-Tool / CLI Boundary:** Evaluates telemetry leakage, process lifecycle capture, and exit code capture when tools are invoked directly via shell or subprocess mechanisms.
- **Agent-to-MCP Server Boundary:** Evaluates JSON-RPC message tracking, tool discovery handshakes, and transport-level context propagation.
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Boundary:** Evaluates task delegation cards, cryptographic identity attestation, and distributed trace context continuity.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-18:** Governance review of the monthly reporting cycle updated official records to confirm framework origination in the Observability and Traceability Working Group under Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing workflow execution models, reference architectures, and lifecycle integration patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops vendor-neutral execution models, reference architectures, and structural patterns for integrating AI agents into enterprise and developer workflows.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group was the first body within the Agentic AI Foundation to ship a formally voted asset with its Phase One Core Terms taxonomy draft.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates across three primary active workstreams:

1. **Reference Architectures**: Chaired by Mario and Zayne, this stream formalizes repeatable architectures. Deliverables for the initial charter scope include the core [architecture principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md), a contributing guide, the human-approved operation reference architecture ([Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)), and the [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) reference architecture.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Architectural fit is assessed against a standardized four-outcome evaluation methodology ([validated, partial, candidate, no fit]) published in [Reference Architecture Validation](../guidelines/reference-architecture-validation.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
2. **Critical Use Cases**: Led by Kevin and Jodee, this stream curates an inventory of real-world production use cases categorized into priority cohorts, including human-approved operations, autonomous remediation, and exception escalation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
3. **Taxonomy**: Led by Sumanth with Gala serving as cross-WG liaison, the taxonomy stream standardizes execution vocabulary. The stream resolved key terminology disputes, defining "activity" as the foundational atomic unit before defining "workflow" as an activity composition, while scoping out evaluation and gate definitions to sister working groups.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group achieved several foundational delivery milestones:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-38]
- Shipped the Phase One Core Terms taxonomy deliverable following approval at the August plenary session.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- Merged the core architecture principles and contributor guide (PR #27).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- Merged the human-approved operation reference architecture and finalized review for the bounded autonomous remediation pattern.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- Instituted a standing pull-request governance rule capping changes at approximately 10 files to prevent review bottlenecks.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
