proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, and boundary observability specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry models, cross-boundary distributed tracing specifications, and audit evidence formats for autonomous and agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group develops telemetry context extensions that bridge local execution runtimes, protocol gateways, and distributed observability platforms.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group conducts technical delivery across focused domain areas:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Led by Matthew Lee, this track formalizes portable telemetry context that preserves execution context and causal relationships across agents, SDKs, gateways, and backend platforms without replacing existing standards like OpenTelemetry GenAI.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Conformance testing coordinates against reference architectures authored by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Protocols & Primitives Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, this track standardizes telemetry mapping across agent boundaries, specifically covering [Agent-to-MCP Server Boundaries](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md), [Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundaries](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md), and Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) lifecycle verification pipelines.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: The working group coordinates domain terms with the cross-WG taxonomy team; in August 2026, seven terms—Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability—were formally accepted.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group published its Working Methods and Contributor Checklist, delivered a full-stack tracing landscape survey, and demonstrated a proof-of-concept for tracing ARD discovery, trust verification, and skill execution via Agent Gateway.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] During this cycle, the Multi-Agentic Observability focus group was folded into the general working group to consolidate community participation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry model and portable context specification capturing agent reasoning continuity, decision causality, and boundary executions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to preserve execution context and causal relationships across heterogeneous agent runtimes, tool boundaries, gateways, and observability backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Designed as an extension mechanism using portable telemetry context, it complements rather than replaces OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, establishing verifiable linkages between agent planning, tool execution, and outcomes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification

The specification defines structural contracts for tracing agent systems through several core capabilities:

- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Propagates execution identity and causal graphs across SDK boundaries, gateways, and external services without mandating a specific backend.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Causal Linking**: Links intentions, plans, and decisions directly to downstream tool executions and state mutations without requiring the capture of raw proprietary chain-of-thought tokens.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Cross-Boundary Identification**: Employs canonical identifiers to track multi-agent delegation, long-running durable sessions, and asynchronous resume triggers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Audit and Verification**: Integrates tamper-evident evidence fields to satisfy audit, dispute resolution, and regulatory transparency demands.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group confirmed the initial model scope and established an implementation plan led by Matthew Lee (Datadog).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] The plan utilizes a reference library, synthetic test suites, and conformance tests aligned against workflow patterns from the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to identify gaps for upstream OpenTelemetry contributions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Validation Methodology
proposed_concept.description: Four-outcome evaluation methodology validating workflow reference architectures against real-world use cases by verifying architectural boundary fit.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture Validation Methodology defines the criteria and evaluation framework used by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to validate whether reference architectures accurately represent real-world use cases.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] The methodology focuses exclusively on architectural fit—verifying that an architecture addresses the same operational job and respects identical structural boundaries—without imposing runtime implementation requirements.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Architecture / Specification

Validation evaluations assign each candidate architecture-to-use-case relationship into one of four standard outcomes:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

- **Validated**: The reference architecture precisely matches the operational role, boundary transitions, and safety constraints of the production use case from which it was abstracted or against which it was tested.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Partial**: The reference architecture captures core interactions but omits structural variants or topological nuances (e.g., parallel remediation branches or alternative subagent structures).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Candidate**: The architecture is theoretically aligned with a class of use cases but awaits formal verification against multiple inventory entries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **No Fit**: The operational problem exhibits fundamentally mismatched control planes, approval mechanics, or security boundaries, requiring a distinct architectural archetype.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Lifecycle History

Formulated in August 2026 during the finalization of the charter deliverables for the Reference Architectures workstream.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] The model was initially applied to classify the [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) architecture as validated against its source case, and the [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) architecture as candidate pending broader multi-case inventory verification.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey evaluating production agent adoption, failure modes, consequence severity, and reliability requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Accuracy and Reliability Survey is an empirical, platform-neutral instrument developed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather quantitative data on agent failures, verification practices, and operational consequences in production.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9] Comprising 16 structured questions, the survey defines explicit respondent response behavior, validation rules, and early-exit screen-out mechanics.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]

# Architecture / Specification

The survey instrument is structured across five sequential sections:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]

1. **Eligibility (Q1)**: Establishes respondent eligibility based on active development or deployment of agentic systems, routing non-qualifying respondents through a dedicated early-exit termination path.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]
2. **About the System (Q2–Q5)**: Captures agent architectures, deployment environments, autonomy levels, and functional domains. Q2 incorporates structured options with required write-in fields for unspecified architectures; Q5 is optional.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]
3. **Benefits and Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Assesses realized capabilities, operational impediments, and security concerns using standardized five-choice response matrices (including "Not sure").[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]
4. **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Evaluates observed failure types, hallucination rates, error propagation, verification barriers, and impact severity.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]
5. **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Surveys organizational tooling roadmaps, benchmark utility, and desired open standards; Q16 is optional.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the complete survey specification and question framework was authored and merged into the working group repository under PR #9, accompanied by a Google Forms prototype for internal working group review prior to public dissemination.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and cross-working group review standards for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream tasked with developing threat modeling frameworks, actionable security best practices, and security design patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group evaluates attack surfaces across agent harnesses, execution sandboxes, tool integration boundaries, and agent-to-agent communication protocols [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

The working group coordinates closely with other AAIF bodies, including the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), while maintaining an open review posture with public meeting recordings by default [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

# Operations and Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical agenda into five primary initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating baseline industry frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) alongside STRIDE and PASTA methodologies, human-user-agent (HUA) interfaces, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, establishing baseline operational guidance across tool sandboxing, secrets isolation, and user delegation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, authoring structured reference implementations for secure agent execution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, building a cross-cutting assessment checklist to review deliverables across peer AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Harmonization**: Delegated to Jay White and Katherine Druckman, triaging agent-specific security and privacy terminology before formal committee submission [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Governance and Cross-WG Inquiries
The working group interfaces with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on boundary definitions, specifically seeking guidance on how protocol donations like Agent-to-Agent (A2A) affect cross-group remits across agent security, runtime gateways, and protocol design [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Published August 2026 report detailing threat modeling framework progress, security pattern templates, cross-working group review checklists, and clarification requests regarding A2A protocol scope [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling analysis evaluating traditional and AI security frameworks against agentic boundaries, protocol vulnerabilities, and human-in-the-loop interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a foundational study developed under the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) evaluating how existing cybersecurity and artificial intelligence risk standards apply to autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the initiative assesses where standard threat models fail to account for multi-agent delegation, autonomous tool execution, and dynamic context assembly [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

The deliverable bridges classical software security methodologies with AI-specific taxonomies, ensuring emerging architectures address agent-specific attack vectors such as context poisoning and privilege hijacking [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

# Framework Assessment Scope
The analysis examines coverage gaps across established industry frameworks and classical modeling approaches [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **OWASP**: Analyzed against the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications and emerging agentic threats, identifying risks associated with unconstrained tool invocation and prompt injection cascades [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **MITRE ATLAS**: Evaluated for threat actor tactics targeting agent-specific execution stages, model-to-tool bridges, and autonomous persistence [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **MAESTRO and NIST AI RMF**: Assessed for organizational governance and runtime risk mapping against high-autonomy decision loops [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **STRIDE and PASTA**: Classical threat modeling paradigms examined to establish structured risk scoring and asset decomposition suited to agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Protocol and Interface Vectors**: Incorporates analysis of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool exposure surfaces and human-user-agent (HUA) / UI interaction points where spoofing or indirect prompt injection can alter approval flows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Active review under PR #8 in the Security & Privacy Working Group repository, integrating STRIDE/PASTA alignments, MCP security evaluation, and human-in-the-loop threat considerations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, and cross-boundary audit specifications for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and verifiable audit records for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. The working group defines behavioral observation models bridging LLM runtime generation, tool invocations, inter-agent messaging, and underlying infrastructure systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].

Key focus areas include the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), cross-boundary telemetry propagation models, and alignment with external distributed tracing and security observability consortia [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

# Operations and Workstreams
The working group maintains several active initiatives and governance registers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM)**: Developing a neutral recommendation plan evaluating candidate standards across adopt, extend, or new specification pathways, targeting multi-turn agent decision reasoning and lifecycle handoffs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].
- **Liaison Management**: Maintaining an active liaison roster tracking formal interfaces with external standards groups (OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, W3C Trace Context, OWASP AOS, Agent Trace, Monocle, AGNTCY, and protocol maintainers) and peer AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].
- **Evidence-Grade Taxonomy & Jurisdictional Requirements**: Standardizing evidence-grade classification ladders (grades E1 through E4) and separating technical cryptographic integrity mechanisms (such as RFC 3161 timestamping) from legal regime qualifications and relying-party obligations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Publishing analysis matrices spanning the [Agent-to-MCP boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) and direct agent-to-tool command lines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Established external and internal cross-WG intake and liaison roster tracking OpenTelemetry, W3C, and OWASP alignment [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].
- **2026-07**: Initiated the Trace Model Recommendation Plan defining decision pathways across candidate telemetry specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **2026-08**: Published monthly report covering ABTM scope, taxonomy contributions, and cross-boundary proposals for Technical Committee review [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].
- **2026-09**: Disambiguated evidence-grade ladder terminology and introduced explicit jurisdiction and legal role requirements into cross-cutting telemetry registers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification and recommendation framework capturing agent reasoning continuity, decision state transitions, and cross-boundary tool dispatches.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM) is a vendor-neutral specification framework developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture the operational context, reasoning continuity, and delegation lifecycle of autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. The model addresses the visibility gaps left by traditional APM and distributed tracing systems, which treat multi-step agent decisions, context window states, and prompt mutations as opaque runtime events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

The working group operates under a formal recommendation plan designed to evaluate existing candidate industry specifications before determining whether to adopt, extend, or author a greenfield specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Architecture / Specification
The recommendation planning framework defines structured evaluation criteria to harmonize agent telemetry across heterogeneous runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]:

- **Candidate Baseline Evaluation**: Benchmarks candidate models and emerging industry telemetry schemas, including OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, W3C Trace Context extensions, and project-specific schemas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Decision Path Matrix**: Defines structured criteria governing an adopt, extend, or author decision path based on taxonomy alignment, gap analysis findings, and stakeholder focus group feedback [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Trace Dimensions**: Standardizes state representations across cognitive reasoning loops, subagent task delegations, dynamic prompt alterations, and tool invocation contracts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07**: Framed the decision-neutral Trace Model Recommendation Plan under issue #12 to evaluate existing standards without pre-committing to a proprietary format [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **2026-08**: Working group August report submitted to the Technical Committee detailing the trace model scope and scheduling the implementation plan for September [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral workflow execution models, reference architectures, integration patterns, and operational controls for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group bridges abstract agentic designs and enterprise systems of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output across three coordinated workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]:

- **Reference Architectures**: Develops specification-driven architecture blueprints generated from machine-readable YAML definitions into executable patterns, operational diagrams, and documentation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. It defines 7 execution profiles spanning from profile 1 (fully deterministic) to profile 7 (fully agentic) under a "least agentic default" recommendation principle, as well as 6 charter-derived architectural archetypes (e.g., bounded automation, gated operation) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Catalogs and categorizes empirical enterprise use cases across core workflow primitives including trigger types, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent count, coordination models, and workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Coordinates with the cross-working-group taxonomy workstream to align primitive naming, execution profile parameters, and domain vocabularies to eliminate semantic drift [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, the Reference Architectures workstream demonstrated its specification-driven design flow end-to-end on invoice processing and autonomous maintenance use cases across deterministic and agentic variants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Concurrently, the Critical Use Cases team categorized 89 use cases across a consolidated set of under 10 reusable workflow patterns, including the autonomous convergence loop [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# References

- [WG Workflows & Process Integration Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI triage agent utilizing GitHub Actions, Copilot inference, and multi-model fallback to validate incoming issue submissions in a read-only environment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless continuous integration (CI) triage agent designed to parse, validate, and evaluate incoming GitHub issue submissions against foundation requirements [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. It executes automated first-pass evaluations within containerized workflows without requiring persistent interactive execution environments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Architecture / Specification

The analyser incorporates specific architectural resilience and security mechanisms:

- **Model Access Canary**: Employs an out-of-band scheduled daily canary workflow running in dry-run mode (`DRY_RUN=1`) against a fixed issue baseline to proactively detect expired PATs, broken Copilot individual endpoints, and header drift before live triage failures occur [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Dual-Matrix Fallback Validation**: Operates an independent primary and fallback execution matrix (running `fail-fast: false`), preventing a broken fallback model configuration from being masked when the primary endpoint is healthy [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Least Privilege Execution**: Uses scoped repository permissions (`contents: read`, `issues: read`, `copilot-requests: write`) and eliminates third-party publication credentials during validation runs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. Model inference utilizes repository-level GITHUB_TOKEN Copilot entitlements rather than external personal access tokens [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# References

- [Submission Analyser Repository](https://github.com/aaif/submission-analyser)

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing inside hardware-attested trusted execution environments while leaving untrusted agent execution outside.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern establishes verifiable policy evaluation and cryptographic evidence generation inside a hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), separating policy enforcement from the untrusted agent workload.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb] Also known as confidential agent execution or an attested enclave gateway, the pattern addresses scenarios where an agent operates on sensitive, regulated, or classified data hosted on untrusted infrastructure such as public cloud regions, partner multi-tenant clusters, or customer environments subject to audit.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

When the host platform and infrastructure operator are within the threat model, software-only controls cannot prevent host administrators or compromised host kernels from swapping policy bundles, tampering with in-memory decisions, or fabricating execution logs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb] By constraining the enclave boundary strictly to policy evaluation, secret unsealing, and evidence signing while leaving the resource-heavy agent orchestration outside, the pattern minimizes the enclave trusted computing base.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

# Architecture / Specification

## Architectural Roles
The pattern defines four discrete organizational roles with divergent security interests:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
- **Data Owner:** Requires that inputs and execution context remain confidential and unexposed during processing.
- **Agent Operator:** Executes the workload and seeks broad runtime adoptability across heterogeneous environments.
- **Infrastructure Operator:** Controls the host operating system, hypervisor, and orchestration fabric; sits inside the threat model.
- **Relying Party:** A downstream tool, peer agent, auditor, or regulator that verifies proof of compliance without directly inspecting private data.

## Core Mechanics
1. **Isolate the Enforcement Point:** The policy engine and cryptographic signing modules run inside a hardware TEE, while the primary agent process, LLM inference, and external tooling run in the untrusted host environment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
2. **Internal Key Generation:** Signing and sealing keys are generated inside the enclave boundary and cryptographically bound to hardware measurement registers, ensuring private keys cannot be extracted by the host.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
3. **Measurement Sealing and Appraisal:** Policies are sealed to enclave measurement quotes. Protected state and execution authorization are released only after appraisal passes against expected reference measurements.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
4. **Verifiable Evidence Emission:** The isolated runtime emits signed [Action Records](../taxonomy/action-record.md) for each discrete unit of work, enabling external relying parties to independently verify policy enforcement and execution integrity.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

# Lifecycle History
The draft pattern was authored by the Design Patterns workstream within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) as the first pattern in the privacy-preserving execution topic area, evaluated across five independent hardware attestation architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as shared disciplines across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] It develops open threat models, domain taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

The working group operates under the governance of the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates with peer groups including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Governance
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, with an alternate-week APAC trial session at 10:00 PM ET.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

## Governance and Merge Policies
- **Deliverables Separation:** Authors cannot merge their own pull requests into the `deliverables/` folder, requiring independent review; workstream leads retain direct stewardship over their respective `workstreams/` subfolders.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
- **Living Documents:** Major deliverable milestones freeze core guidelines such as the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), converting subsequent changes into issue-driven tracking and dedicated pull requests.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

## Active Workstreams
1. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg, Erin Farr, and Matthew Khouzam; establishes baseline security recommendations and static-analysis compliance rules.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
2. **Threat Modeling and Gap Analysis:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg; evaluates standard security frameworks against agentic-specific threat surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Sagar and Dan; standardizes governance patterns such as [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
4. **Taxonomy and Landscape:** Joint initiative with Katherine Druckman and Juliana Milan defining agentic security classifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy; audits cross-WG specifications for identity, authorization, and telemetry consistency.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was initially adopted on April 14, 2026, and confirmed following Technical Committee review on May 26, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] Repositories were made public in June 2026, followed by community-wide contributions across best practices, threat modeling, and attestation patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling analysis evaluating traditional and AI security frameworks against agent-specific surfaces including tool delegation and multi-agent persuasion.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an ongoing workstream deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) evaluating whether existing AI security frameworks adequately address agentic AI attack surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85] It determines whether foundational models such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) sufficiently protect against autonomous behaviors or whether dedicated agentic modeling frameworks are required.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]

The resulting gap analysis provides foundational input for the AAIF [Design Patterns Catalog](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]

# Architecture / Specification

## Target Threat Surfaces
The gap analysis specifically targets five failure modes and architectural vulnerabilities distinctive to agentic deployments:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion:** Cooperative or adversarial prompt manipulation across autonomous subagents and peer agents.
- **Tool Invocation Risks:** Unauthorized execution, parameter tampering, and ambient authority exploitation during tool and API execution.
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries:** Privilege escalation, identity impersonation, and boundary confusion when delegating permissions across agent-to-agent boundaries.
- **Supply-Chain Integrity:** Tampering with system prompt definitions, agent skill packages, and tool manifest declarations.
- **Model and Runtime Provenance:** Lack of cryptographic provenance or measurement verifying underlying foundation models and harness runtime configurations.

## Workstream Organization
- **Leads:** Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]
- **Working Group Cadence:** Biweekly dedicated threat modeling sessions scheduled in alternating sequence with security best practices reviews.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# Lifecycle History
The deliverable draft was initiated in July 2026, with an initial gap analysis skeleton submitted to the working group repository in August 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] Dedicated threat modeling working sessions launched in October 2026 following the completion of the baseline best practices guide.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural recommendations and control baselines for credential elimination, Model Context Protocol security, and tool supply chain verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide defines prescriptive implementation baselines and architectural patterns for builders deploying autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Authored as Deliverable 4 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) under the lead of Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), the guideline structures technical defenses across secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]. Broad identity federation frameworks and workload attestation mechanisms (such as SPIFFE/SVID and UCAN tokens) are explicitly scoped out to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Secrets Management and Credential Elimination
Static, long-lived API keys, passwords, and environment variables represent persistent attack vectors subject to deserialization exploits (e.g., CVE-2025-68664) and prompt injection extraction [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates moving toward ephemeral, on-demand credentials across four architectural tiers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Cloud Workload Identity**: Primary baseline for containerized workloads (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) leveraging cluster OIDC to exchange short-lived tokens without storing persistent credentials in execution environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Dynamic Secrets Engines**: Issuance of per-request credentials with short time-to-live (15–60 minutes) and automated revocation via engines such as HashiCorp Vault for legacy APIs and databases [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Network-Layer Injection**: Intermediary proxy or sidecar credential attachment for legacy services unable to support dynamic rotation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Confidential Enclaves**: Application of hardware-protected environments (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) for highest-sensitivity data paths and multi-tenant isolation with attested key release [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

### 2. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Security
Because Model Context Protocol (MCP) leaves OAuth 2.1 optional and standard stdio transports exempt, systems using MCP must enforce rigorous operational invariants [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Pre-Deployment Auditing**: Verification of public server source repositories, adherence to a 90-day activity threshold, cross-referencing CVE/NVD and the Vulnerable MCP Project tracker, and mandatory static and dynamic inspection (e.g., Cisco MCP Scanner, Invariant mcp-scan) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Transport Enforcement**: Stdio transport servers must be isolated in restricted sandboxes and treated as untrusted binaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]. All HTTP-based MCP traffic must enforce TLS, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and token audience binding under RFC 8707 to avoid cross-server token reuse [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Gateway and Invariant Enforcement**: Multi-server deployments require routing through dedicated policy enforcement gateways with per-tool permissions and payload recording [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]. Tool descriptions must be hashed across session restarts to prevent rug-pull attacks, permission expansion, and prompt injection encoded via invisible Unicode tag ranges (U+E0000–U+E007F) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

### 3. Supply Chain and Skill Verification
Third-party skills and plugins undergo tiered ingestion safeguards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Tier 1 Automated Scanning**: Static signature checks and behavioral dataflow scans (via tools like Cisco Skill Scanner or Snyk Agent Scan), automatically failing builds on High or Critical findings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Tier 2 Elevated Review**: Manual review of requested tool permissions (`allowed-tools`), structural validation of network domains, and identification of obscured execution primitives such as `eval()` or base64 decoding [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History

Draft v0.1 was developed within the AAIF Security & Privacy Working Group and submitted for working group review as Deliverable 4 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Accompanied by a comprehensive security feature matrix, the document is actively maintained by designated working group leads and community contributors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Engineering standards for packaging multi-client agent plugins and skills across repository checkout boundaries without client vendor lock-in.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent plugin portability guidelines define standardized conventions for distributing agent skills and operational tooling across heterogeneous AI agent harnesses—such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor—without maintaining redundant codebases or proprietary configurations[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. By separating vendor-neutral manifests from client-specific compatibility layers and modeling execution requirements around abstract capabilities, plugins maintain portability across local developer workstations and headless CI environments[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

Related standards and guidelines include [Agent Skills Specification](../standards/agent-skills.md) and [Workflow Architecture Principles](workflow-architecture-principles.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Manifest Structure and Compatibility Overlays
Portable agent plugins organize manifests in a hierarchical structure to serve both vendor-neutral and vendor-specialized clients[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Root Portable Manifest (`plugin.json`)**: Acts as the canonical manifest for clients implementing the open Agent Plugins specification (including Codex and Cursor), defining canonical identity and version metadata[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Claude Compatibility Overlays (`.claude-plugin/`)**: Houses `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` for Claude Code compatibility and `marketplace.json` for marketplace cataloging[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Overlay Minimization**: Where plugins contain no client-specific component configuration, client-specific overlay directories such as `.codex-plugin` or `.cursor-plugin` are deliberately omitted to avoid drift[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

## Capability-First Instruction Design
To prevent brittle dependencies on client tool naming conventions (such as specific bash execution tools or proprietary tool calls), skill definitions in `SKILL.md` specify requirements in terms of generic runtime capabilities[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Read bundled files**: Loading workflows, references, or local static assets; missing assets trigger explicit execution halts rather than improvised recovery.
- **Run Python and subprocesses**: Executing deterministic scripts without re-implementing mutating business logic ad hoc.
- **Read web pages**: Fetching external event or public documentation facts.
- **Show local files**: Surfacing generated HTML, images, or documents for operator inspection.
- **Request user approval**: Halting execution before executing mutations or notification gates until explicit approval is granted[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

Instruction paths in `SKILL.md` must remain strictly relative to the containing skill directory, represented as `<skill-root>` for execution engines to resolve dynamically[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Client invocation patterns (e.g., slash commands in Claude Code, `$` syntax in Codex, or GUI menus in Cursor) remain external to skill declarations[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

## Authorization Gates and Safe Mutation Boundaries
Plugin loading or skill invocation does not imply authorization to execute state-changing operations on external systems[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Plan-by-Default Execution**: Operations must run in read-only reporting or planning mode by default unless an explicit mutation flag (e.g., `--write`, `--apply`, or `--create`) is supplied[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Explicit Human Affirmation**: Flags denoting human authorization (such as `--i-have-approval`) must never be autonomously provided by agents[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Credential Hygiene**: Secrets and API tokens must be sourced from environment variables, gitignored local `.env` files, or OS keychains, strictly prohibited from command line arguments (`argv`), prompt contexts, or generated reports[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
- **Centralized Redaction**: Operational logging and triage output must route through unified redaction helpers to prevent personally identifiable information (PII) from leaking into terminal output or public CI streams[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

# Lifecycle History
The portable plugin framework was adopted by the AAIF community events engineering team to support simultaneous development across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor without duplicating operational skill scripts or risking unsanctioned production mutations[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate sweep backfills, and multi-surface asset synchronization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill Suite provides specialized automation tools for managing AAIF community chapters, event collateral, workspace communications, and organizer rosters across Google Drive, Slack, and ticketing platforms[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb][^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. The suite enforces plan-by-default execution, strict boundary approvals, and four-surface consistency checks across cloud directories, spreadsheets, presentation XML, and messaging channels[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

Related patterns and guidelines include [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), and [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Slack Workspace Auditing Engine
The workspace auditing subsystem (`audit_organizers.py` within `aaif-audit-slack`) cross-references the canonical Google Sheets chapter roster against live Slack channels and users[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]:
- **Identity Resolution**: Organizers are matched between intake records and Slack users strictly via email addresses as an upper-bound heuristic, requiring human name reconciliation before destructive administrative actions[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **State Handling (`--planned-ok`)**: Supports pre-provisioned chapters and held-private channels without aborting runs due to missing channels or incomplete admin handoffs[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Critical Findings**: Flags public organizer channels (`-organizers` marked `public!`) as the highest-severity vulnerability, identifying workspace leaks of private budgets, venue contracts, and speaker negotiations[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Roster Anomaly Detection**: Highlights active organizer channels containing zero accepted organizers, isolating unreviewed rosters[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

## Estate Sweep and Slide Deck Backfills
Estate maintenance scripts execute idempotent batch updates across chapter presentation decks stored in Google Drive[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]:
- **Map Dots Backfill (`backfill_map_dots.py`)**: Re-positions chapter markers on world maps using a Gall Stereographic projection calibrated against latitude and longitude coordinates in the central sheet, replacing legacy pixel overrides[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Tolerance and Idempotence**: Decks with marker drift within 1 pixel are skipped as rounding artifacts; decks lacking exactly one green dot and label on slide 5 are skipped to prevent unverified overwrites[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Host Footer and Projects Rosters**: Updates shared host and project listings across existing decks using direct Open Packaging Conventions (OOXML) XML surgery without modifying layout templates[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Irreversible Write Safety**: Plan runs output per-chapter pixel drifts and template diffs by default; `--write` replaces live presentations in place with Drive revision history serving as the sole recovery fallback[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].

## Four-Surface Chapter Renaming (`rename_chapter.py`)
Renaming an existing chapter requires coordinated, atomic updates across four distinct surfaces to avoid orphaned references[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]:
1. **Drive Folder**: Renaming root chapter directories while maintaining folder ID links[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
2. **File and Subfolder Names**: Updating filenames (e.g., CRM workbooks, local asset folders)[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
3. **OOXML Document Content**: Substituting city references inside `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` internal XML streams[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
4. **Document Metadata (`docProps`)**: Updating Dublin Core and application metadata titles[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

Relationship targets (`.rels`) are explicitly shielded from arbitrary city-name replacements to prevent corrupting relative zip package URIs[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. Furthermore, ticketing slugs (e.g., Luma event URLs) are decoupled from city renames unless explicitly passed via `--slug-from` and `--slug-to`, preventing broken links for established community hubs[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

# Lifecycle History
The Community Event Operations skills evolved from manual administrative runbooks into a portable Python and OOXML automation suite to support rapid global expansion while enforcing strict data hygiene[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb][^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation and Validation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and CI validation architecture evaluating skill dispatch, agent plugin manifests, OOXML transformations, and security guardrails.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation and Validation Suite is an automated testing harness and CI workflow architecture enforcing structural, semantic, and security invariants across the AAIF community events skill ecosystem[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]. Designed around credential-free public evaluation, the harness combines static pre-commit linting, dual-format manifest conformance checks, synthetic pytest unit tests, and design token synchronization[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

Related concepts include [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md), [Agent Skills Specification](../standards/agent-skills.md), and [Community Event Operations Skill Suite](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Credential-Separated CI Pipeline
The automated pull-request validation workflow (`validate.yml`) runs entirely in an unprivileged, read-only security context[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]:
- **Zero-Secret Boundary**: The validation workflow never receives API keys or service credentials for external services (Google Workspace, Slack, or Luma), preventing credential exfiltration from untrusted pull requests originating from forks[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
- **Gated Skill Execution**: Live operational skills requiring production credentials execute strictly via manually triggered, gated workflows (`run-skill.yml`) under controlled repository environments[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

## Multi-Stage Validation Jobs
The suite partitions evaluation across three primary CI jobs[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]:
1. **Pre-commit Quality Checks**:
   - Executes standard code hygiene including `ruff` bug-focused linting, `codespell` spell checks, and `gitleaks` secret detection[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
   - Validates portable `SKILL.md` YAML frontmatter against the Agent Skills specification and root `plugin.json` against Agent Plugins v1 schemas[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
   - Asserts tooling-rule banner consistency across skills to prevent silent prompt drift when downstream clients consume isolated skill bundles[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
   - Enforces single-module PII redaction surfaces, disallowing unmanaged logging pathways[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
2. **Plugin Conformance Validation (`plugin-validate`)**:
   - Uses the Anthropic Claude Code CLI (`claude plugin validate .`) to verify `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and marketplace catalogs against client standards alongside portable schema checks[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
3. **Deterministic Pytest Suite**:
   - Tests core helper libraries (`lib/aaif_events`) and operational skill scripts using offline synthetic fixtures without network calls[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
   - Requires full git history (`fetch-depth: 0`) during repository checkout to ensure end-to-end OOXML regression tests can inspect historical document states and font-embed stripping without silent test skips[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
   - Executes design token validation (`extract_design_tokens.py --check`) ensuring generated presentation decks conform directly to the upstream AAIF design system[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# Lifecycle History
Created to support community event automation across distributed open-source contributors, the validation suite established automated guardrails to prevent schema drift, accidental secret exposure, and OOXML corruption during automated batch updates[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and classification schema mapping production agentic workflows against multi-dimensional properties and strict deployment evidentiary standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to document recurring agentic workflow shapes from real-world production deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]. The initiative provides an explicit, evidence-backed inventory of named workflows rather than hypothetical architectures, enabling practitioners to identify patterns across multiple industries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream repository is organized into distinct documentation components [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]:
- `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`: Defines column schemas, valid categorical property values, and open taxonomy questions for workflow classification.
- `use-case-inventory.md`: The central matrix recording deployed workflows, associated runtime properties, and verified production references.

## Evidentiary Standard
To ensure reliable taxonomy derivation, the workstream enforces an evidentiary threshold for all inventory entries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]:
- **Citation Minimums**: Each use case requires at least one publicly accessible, independently verifiable citation of confirmed production deployment, with a target of three independent citations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].
- **Preferred Evidence**: Primary announcements or vendor product documentation demonstrating a named customer deployment (such as Cohere Health with BSIM or PagerDuty with Chicago Trading Company) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Vendor documentation showing strong technical evidence of production usage at scale, even without an identified customer [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].
- **Unacceptable Sources**: Secondary blog posts, market analyst commentary, academic publications, market projections, or unverifiable implementer claims [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].

# Lifecycle History
The classification schema, category groupings, and evidentiary criteria were codified for working group vote in PR#46 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46], moving row-level verification into an active multi-contributor phase.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural recommendations and control baselines structuring agent security measures across people, process, and technology operational dimensions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline, developed by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), establishes architectural controls, credential baselines, and implementation requirements across autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]. The framework organizes required mitigations across administrative, human, and engineering domains to address threat vectors specific to agent execution loops.

# Architecture / Specification
The security best practices framework maps required capabilities against a tripartite implementation model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]:
- **People**: Capabilities requiring human training, developer awareness, operational competencies, and security culture across all personnel designing or operating agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Process**: Capabilities mandating formal governance documentation, incident response runbooks, threat assessment procedures, and operational policies governing safe execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Technology**: Technical enforcement mechanisms, including physical or digital tools, hardware roots of trust, policy proxies, sandboxed runtimes, and automated monitoring systems enforcing controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

## Control Matrix Integration
Each cataloged security best practice links directly to corresponding feature requirements across these three dimensions, ensuring that technical controls (such as tool sandboxing or secret masking) are paired with corresponding governance processes and operator training [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

# Lifecycle History
PR#20 introduced the initial security best practices feature matrix to provide granular capability categorization across people, process, and technology pillars [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Engineering standards for packaging multi-client agent plugins, portable manifests, path tokens, and separated execution workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines specify engineering conventions for distributing reusable agent skills, manifests, and execution recipes across diverse client runtimes [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. By standardizing manifest schemas, decoupling interface contracts from execution procedures, and eliminating runtime-specific path assumptions, plugins maintain cross-platform interoperability across coding assistants and automated harnesses [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification
Portable agent plugins adhere to standardized metadata structures and packaging invariants [^evt-community-events-pr-54]:
- **Manifest Coexistence**: Plugins publish root Agent Plugins v1 manifests (`plugin.json`) alongside runtime-specific descriptors (such as Claude manifests), using `PORTABILITY.md` to document client capabilities, authorization gates, and operational limits [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Compatibility Declarations**: Every skill declares an explicit `compatibility` array and isolates client-specific arguments (e.g., slash-command hints) inside namespaced `metadata` blocks rather than top-level fields [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Path Abstraction**: Client-specific path variables (such as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) are abstracted using vendor-neutral placeholders such as `<skill-root>` [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Contract Decoupling**: Complex procedures separate the concise runtime interface contract in `SKILL.md` from the step-by-step human or subagent instructions documented in an accompanying `WORKFLOW.md` [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

## Validation and Linting
Portability compliance is enforced in pre-commit and CI via automated validators, including `check_manifests.py` and `check_skill_portability.py`, preventing regression into single-vendor packaging conventions [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Lifecycle History
Standardized in PR#54 within `aaif/community-events`, which refactored the skill suite to the dual-manifest specification and isolated operational workflows [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skills Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open file-based packaging format and progressive disclosure standard for extending AI agents with procedural knowledge, executable scripts, and resources.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Skills specification defines an open, file-based packaging format for extending AI agent capabilities with specialized domain knowledge, repeatable multi-step workflows, and operational resources [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]. Structurally composed of a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file alongside optional scripts, templates, and reference documentation, the standard establishes a portable capability layer across heterogeneous agent runtimes and development environments [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

Originally developed by Anthropic and published as an open standard, Agent Skills was formally submitted for project intake under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to transition canonical stewardship, specifications, and reference tooling to neutral governance under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

# Architecture / Specification

## Three-Stage Progressive Disclosure
To manage context window utilization effectively, agents load skills via progressive disclosure across three operational phases [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]:
1. **Discovery**: At runtime startup, an agent inspects only the lightweight metadata (such as skill name and descriptive summary) of all installed skills, maintaining an intentionally small baseline context footprint [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].
2. **Activation**: When an incoming prompt or operational objective matches a skill's activation description, the agent ingests the complete procedural instructions of `SKILL.md` into active context [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].
3. **Execution**: The agent executes the prescribed instructions, optionally running bundled code scripts, querying referenced datasets, or invoking client tools as needed [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

## Interoperability and Complementary Protocols
Agent Skills addresses capability packaging alongside adjacent foundational standards [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Operates at the connectivity and tool execution layer; Agent Skills provides procedural guidance defining when, how, and in what order to invoke specific MCP tools [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].
- **AGENTS.md**: Operates as a persistent, repository-level instruction file describing project-specific setup, whereas skills provide modular, portable capabilities reusable across repositories [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].
- **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**: Defines IDE-to-agent communication channels over which skill execution and file modification requests are mediated [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

# Lifecycle History
Anthropic originally introduced Agent Skills on October 16, 2025, and published the open specification on December 18, 2025 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]. In 2026, an official proposal was submitted to the AAIF to transfer the specification repository, reference implementations, and associated domains to foundation ownership [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Publishing Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, contributor eligibility rules, style guidelines, and intake workflows for Agentic AI Foundation blog publications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Blog Publishing Guidelines establish editorial criteria, structural standards, and intake review processes for public articles published across official Agentic AI Foundation communication channels [^evt-foundation-pr-7]. These standards govern contributions from foundation working groups, project maintainers, and community participants to preserve technical credibility and vendor neutrality [^evt-foundation-pr-7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Editorial Style Requirements
Content submitted for publication must satisfy specific technical and stylistic baselines [^evt-foundation-pr-7]:
- **Sentence Case and US English**: Headings, section titles, and page headers must adhere to sentence case capitalization, with prose written in standard US English [^evt-foundation-pr-7].
- **Substantiation of Categorical Claims**: Authors must avoid unsupported categorical assertions; performance metrics, market assessments, and architectural assertions require empirical validation or verifiable benchmarking references [^evt-foundation-pr-7].
- **Primary-Source Referencing**: Assertions referring to specifications, standards, research findings, or regulatory mandates must link directly to authoritative primary sources rather than third-party commentary [^evt-foundation-pr-7].
- **Official Project Designations**: References to AAIF projects, working groups, and external open-source technologies must consistently employ their official, canonical names [^evt-foundation-pr-7].

## Submission and Review Workflow
Articles are proposed via pull request against the foundation repository and reviewed by designated maintainers to verify factual accuracy and adherence to the [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) [^evt-foundation-pr-7].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate synchronization, and data hygiene.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill automates directory synchronization, estate auditing, and intake validation for Agentic AI Foundation community chapters, organizers, and event hosts [^evt-community-events-pr-55] [^evt-community-events-pr-56]. It integrates automated data validation scripts, non-destructive synchronization engines, and visual exception flags to protect estate data integrity without human-in-the-loop disruption [^evt-community-events-pr-55] [^evt-community-events-pr-56].

# Architecture / Specification

## Non-Destructive Chapter Synchronization
The `sync-chapters` workflow enforces an invariant that live chapter records are never deleted or blanked out automatically [^evt-community-events-pr-55]:
- **Candidate Classification**: When a live chapter row lacks a corresponding qualifying organizer, the synchronization script records it as a retirement candidate rather than purging the entry [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. This preserves existing hand-maintained metadata, including chapter summaries, imagery, and operational notes [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Retirement**: Candidate chapters require an explicit operator decision to transition to `Status=Deprecated` or `Status=Merged` (referencing an active chapter via `Merged Into`) [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Ambiguity Holds**: Synchronization halts automated state progression if organizer city entries represent malformed data, near-misses, or renamed municipalities [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

## Visual Data Hygiene Flagging
The `clean-data` tool provides automated linting and triage formatting across intake form responses [^evt-community-events-pr-56]:
- **Other-City Highlighting**: The `clean.py chapter-flags` subcommand applies red conditional formatting to submitted city cells starting with `Other`, directing triage attention to unmapped chapter requests [^evt-community-events-pr-56].
- **Read-Only Invariants**: Formatting operations inspect and style cells without altering underlying text values, formula bindings, or role-tab chapter records [^evt-community-events-pr-56].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry framework capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, and OpenTelemetry semantic alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry specification defining semantic conventions, execution hierarchies, and conformance benchmarks for capturing agent reasoning continuums, tool dispatches, and multi-turn state transitions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. Stewarded by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the initiative focuses on harmonizing telemetry across disparate agent frameworks by aligning directly with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md).

# Architecture / Specification
While many agent software development kits emit OpenTelemetry spans and metrics, they frequently interpret core semantic attributes and boundary hierarchies inconsistently[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. The specification addresses these divergences through three coordinated tracks:
- **Semantic Gap Remediation**: Identifying semantic divergences across commercial and open-source agent SDKs and proposing unified GenAI attribute mappings upstream to OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Conformance Framework**: Developing an automated conformance suite to validate trace emission structure, context propagation integrity, and span hierarchy across agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Inter-Organizational Standardization**: Coordinating alignment with external standards consortia and industry bodies to establish unified trace conventions for compliance auditing and behavioral diagnostics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group updated its strategic roadmap, choosing to pivot away from publishing a competing standalone trace format in favor of developing an upstream OpenTelemetry conformance framework and resolving SDK semantic inconsistencies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines and control baselines covering credential hygiene, context leakage prevention, boundary isolation, and human oversight.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline defines architectural patterns, threat vectors, and engineering controls required to protect agentic systems against credential theft, runtime context leakage, and oversight failure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]. Developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document outlines defense-in-depth principles spanning developer configuration files, runtime transcript sanitization, and human-in-the-loop verification.

# Architecture / Specification
Active working group proposals focus on four critical attack surfaces and control enhancements:
- **Configuration and Skill Auditing**: Secret auditing must expand beyond cloud environment variables to cover client configuration files (including `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and desktop client settings) and agent skill definitions, which frequently contain committed API keys[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Context and Memory Redaction**: Tool execution payloads returning sensitive tokens or environment details must be scrubbed before passing into session transcripts, execution traces, or long-term cognitive storage, mitigating OWASP ASI03 memory-based privilege retention[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Host Credential Boundary Controls**: Local coding agents require explicit boundary hook deny rules preventing access to sensitive host directory paths—such as SSH keys, cloud profiles, and browser sessions—alongside short-lived authorization tokens to minimize blast radius during sandbox escapes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Approval Fatigue Mitigation**: Human approval prompts suffer from steep degradation under repeated exposure, with empirical studies demonstrating high rubber-stamping rates where human interception of hazardous actions drops significantly after continuous prompts, mandating automated acceptance checks over uncalibrated confirmation dialogs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# Lifecycle History
The guide was introduced under PR #9 in the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md). Subsequent triage issues expanded the threat model to address local configuration audits, memory privilege persistence, and empirical fatigue metrics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
