proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing decentralized agent identity, hardware attestation layering, cryptographic delegation, and authorization boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group standardizes identity frameworks, cryptographic attestation mechanisms, authentication protocols, and delegation boundaries across autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]. Operating under the technical governance of the Agentic AI Foundation, the working group establishes reference architectures and interoperability baselines allowing relying parties to verify agent execution integrity and authorized delegation.

# Architecture / Specification
To address architectural divergence across hardware environments, the group is restructuring attestation specifications into a three-part model[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]:
- **Platform Evidence**: Signed hardware or firmware reports and endorsement chains (such as AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, or GPU attestation) certifying the underlying execution environment and boot state[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
- **Identity Binding**: Cryptographic statements binding an agent key or identifier to hardware measurements using transport structures such as guest report data, paravisor runtime claims, or TPM qualifying data[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
- **Appraisal**: Verification logic and policy verdicts executed by relying parties to confirm evidence satisfies security and compliance thresholds[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

This structural division resolves cross-platform inconsistencies between direct guest attestation, hypervisor-managed paravisor runtime structures, and multi-accelerator environments[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

# Lifecycle History
Following charter establishment, reference architecture discussions in Issue #12 identified gaps in monolithic attestation representations, leading to proposals decomposing attestation into platform evidence, identity binding, and appraisal layers[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between proposal generation and action execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval reference architecture establishes a verifiable runtime governance boundary that intercepts agent-generated actions and mandates authorized human sign-off before executing side effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45]. Developed by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this architecture decouples proposal synthesis from execution authority using durable state checkpoints.

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture balances strict boundary enforcement with runtime implementation flexibility:
- **Proposal and Execution Decoupling**: While practical agent harnesses frequently resume within the existing runtime process upon approval, isolating the final executor into a distinct process provides a clean security boundary and clears accumulated transcript drift, traded off against the overhead of re-hydrating context[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].
- **Durable State and Cache Management**: Suspending workflows via [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) invalidates ephemeral caches during extended human review; systems must explicitly manage minimal context reconstruction upon approval resumption[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].
- **Deliberation vs Action Limits**: The architecture clarifies boundaries between single-agent task loops and multi-agent critique, recognizing that independent verification often requires isolated session contexts rather than unified context reasoning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History
The architecture was drafted to define standard human-in-the-loop workflows. In Issue #45, technical feedback clarified that separate execution processes are architectural recommendations rather than universal runtime mandates, accounting for cold-cache and session management constraints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

mutations.rationale: Update the cross-boundary observability model with the three-layer boundary architecture and coordination scope defined in the merged working document.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Multi-layer analysis framework evaluating agent observability gaps across LLM primitives, protocol boundaries, and underlying infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is an analytical framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to evaluate telemetry and observability gaps across execution boundaries in agentic systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]. Rather than specifying a new telemetry protocol, the model serves as a coordination artifact for benchmarking existing standards, identifying where cross-system interoperability fails, and focusing targeted upstream contributions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25].

# Architecture / Specification

The model organizes observability gap analysis across three distinct operational layers to expose breakdowns in context propagation, provenance, delegation, and responsibility chains[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]:

- **LLM Primitive Layer**: Models primary execution entities including agents, skills, tools, foundation models, and memory stores.
- **Protocol Boundary Layer**: Evaluates interaction semantics across external interfaces (such as MCP, A2A, and streaming HTTP) across discovery, negotiation, request/response, delegation, streaming, cancellation, and error handling.
- **Infrastructure Boundary Layer**: Analyzes underlying runtimes, AI gateways, microservices, and network boundaries transporting agent requests.

By evaluating cross-boundary observability questions against this layered topology, the working group systematically identifies unobserved context drops and unverified agent delegations across multi-system handoffs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a].

# Lifecycle History

The model was proposed and merged as a working draft within the Observability and Traceability Working Group to support gap analysis and interoperability evaluations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary of modular workflow building blocks, execution boundary contracts, and topology primitives for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Workflow primitives are standardized building blocks and boundary contracts defined by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) for assembling modular single-agent and multi-agent reference architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]. They establish vendor-neutral execution units covering triggers, operational budgets, discrete agent steps, and handoff boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification

The primitive framework formalizes workflow decomposition into reusable components and boundary guarantees[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]:

- **Primitive Vocabulary (P1–P19)**: Modular execution units including triggers, agent execution steps (`AgentStep`), operational budget limits (`Budget`), and handoff transfers (`Handoff`).
- **Boundary Contracts**: Explicit invariants required whenever execution crosses primitive boundaries, specifically governing `AgentStep` inputs/outputs and cross-agent `Handoff` transitions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].
- **Multi-Agent Topologies (T1–T6)**: Structural shapes and routing topologies governing agent coordination, supervisor hierarchies, and peer-to-peer delegation flows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].
- **Approval Integration**: Specialized control subsets (P1–P12) integrating deterministic checks and human approval gates into single-agent workflows, as used in the [Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# Lifecycle History

The primitive catalog was drafted to unify the underlying components of single-agent and multi-agent reference architectures into a shared taxonomic baseline[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream standardizing agentic AI terminology, SKOS-Lite vocabulary schemas, and multi-working-group review processes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with maintaining a shared, horizontal vocabulary across technical working groups and cataloging the broader agentic ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]. The workstream is co-chaired by Maintainers Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

Current active operations are exclusively focused on the shared Taxonomy glossary, while submissions to the ecosystem Landscape remain deferred until formal intake processes are accepted[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates a structured tripartite governance model to curate and validate terminology[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]:
- **Contributors (Anyone):** Community members and working group participants who propose new glossary terms, submit pull requests, or file taxonomy issues[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
- **Domain Editors (Working Group Delegates):** Nominated technical delegates representing each of the seven active AAIF Technical Working Groups (including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)). Domain Editors act as primary curators who author and guide entries within their domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
- **Maintainers (Workstream Chairs):** Maintainers hold administrative write access and final merging authority on the repository[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

### Contribution and Review Lifecycle
1. **Working Group Sourcing:** Terms are initially formulated within individual technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
2. **Staging & Queueing:** A delegate brings the term into the centralized taxonomy spreadsheet and flags it in the dedicated Discord channel[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
3. **Weekly Workstream Triage:** During weekly meetings, terms are reviewed for real-world usage, novelty, relevance, and correct working group attribution[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]. Terms receive one of three formal votes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]:
   - `KEEP`: The term is accepted and cleared for a definition pull request[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
   - `CULL`: The term is rejected[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
   - `DEBATE`: The term requires broader discussion before acceptance[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
4. **Pull Request Submission:** Once marked `KEEP`, a delegate from the owning working group submits a pull request with a single-sentence definition and supplementary details in `scopeNote` conformant to SKOS-Lite schemas[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
5. **Cross-Domain Peer Approval:** Pull requests require approval from at least two Domain Editors representing different working groups; any delegate holds veto authority[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
6. **Rebase Merge & Finalization:** Maintainers merge approved pull requests using a rebase-and-merge strategy, marking the spreadsheet item as `FINALIZED`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

# Lifecycle History
The taxonomy contribution workflow was formalized to establish the explicit KEEP/CULL/DEBATE evaluation lifecycle, cross-working-group review thresholds, and scope fencing favoring the core taxonomy over ecosystem landscape mapping[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate synchronization, and regional chapter folding.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated pipeline synchronization, workspace management, and directory integrity auditing for Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community chapters and regional events[^evt-community-events-pr-57]. The skill ensures consistency across intake forms, chapter tracking spreadsheets, Google Drive estates, CRM databases, access control lists, and communication channels[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite coordinates automated chapter synchronization workflows across multiple backends, enforcing canonical chapter boundaries and regional hierarchy mappings.

### Regional Chapter Folding
To enable regional flexibility across local event organizers, municipal chapters can be folded into unified national country chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-57]:
- **Tokyo Chapter:** Consolidated into AAIF Japan (`japan-organizers` channel)[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Wellington & Auckland:** Consolidated into AAIF New Zealand (`new-zealand-organizers` channel)[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

### Synchronization Engines and Invariants
- **City Resolution (`lib/aaif_events/cities.py`):** Provides a centralized `chapter_for()` resolver that normalizes municipal intake values (such as Tokyo or Wellington) to their overarching country chapter before downstream ingestion[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Ingestion Boundaries:** `sync_chapters`, `sync_about`, `sync_crm`, `sync_access`, and Slack audit engines process intake cities through `chapter_for()` to prevent dual-chapter assignments and duplicate row creation[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Clean Verification (`clean.py`):** Evaluates `COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS` with priority over master chapter list rows to ensure retired municipal entries do not reclaim folded territory during audits[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Migration Ordering Invariant:** Sheet rows, Drive folders, About documentation, and CRM files must be renamed in live infrastructure prior to merging runtime code changes to avoid triggering conflicting row creation or accidental organizer overwrites[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
- Municipal chapters for Tokyo and Wellington were formally folded into AAIF Japan and AAIF New Zealand with centralized normalization in `cities.py` and `clean.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group aligning agentic AI architectures with global AI regulations, compliance frameworks, and checkable audit record standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (WG-GRR) within the Agentic AI Foundation evaluates regulatory instruments, assurance requirements, and risk management standards affecting autonomous AI agents. The group establishes technical mappings between legal compliance mandates—such as the EU AI Act, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4.0.1, China TC260 agent guidelines, and ISO/IEC 42001—and concrete architectural controls, focusing on turning high-level compliance outcomes into machine-verifiable artifacts [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its compliance mapping across major policy and assurance themes, specifically contrasting self-reported telemetry with independently attestable records:

- **Record-Shape Standardization**: Evaluating converging technical standards including ISO/IEC 24970 (AI system logging), prEN 18229-1 (AI Trustworthiness Framework Part 1: Logging), and IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail to establish verifiable schemas for agent audit trails [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Tamper-Evident Logging**: Specifying hash-chained, timestamped records, external timestamp anchoring, and decision reproducibility metadata necessary to satisfy auditability mandates [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Recording Independence Gradient**: Enforcing boundary requirements where an agent cannot serve as the sole recorder of its own high-trust actions, capturing pre-execution denials and escalations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Related Frameworks**: Correlating these record requirements with the [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md) and [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) developed across AAIF workstreams.

# Lifecycle History

WG-GRR conducts ongoing gap analyses mapping external policy instruments to technical controls. Phase 2 initiatives expanded the analysis from legal outcome requirements to emerging machine-checkable logging standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, palette, and asset specifications governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets and mark usage.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Guidelines establish the visual identity, typography, color palette, and asset management rules for the Agentic AI Foundation and its community initiatives. The guidelines ensure consistent presentation across public repositories, digital events, presentations, and technical documentation, providing explicit routing for both human contributors and automated tooling [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification

Brand assets and visual identity standards are governed by strict usage constraints:

- **Official Vector Assets**: Primary brand assets are maintained as official SVGs under repository asset manifests. The primary logo lockup is distributed as `aaif-mark.svg` [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Prohibition on Redrawing**: Contributors, automated scripts, and AI agents must never redraw, approximate, or trace the AAIF mark from screenshots or raster images; official SVG assets must be resolved directly via source-of-truth asset tables [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Agent Asset Discovery**: Repository design documentation maintains explicit top-level asset inventories to ensure AI agents can resolve brand assets in single-hop queries without traversing long documentation narratives [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

# Lifecycle History

Asset discoverability and rendering rules were refined in community event documentation to prevent automated agents from synthesizing approximate marks from low-resolution context [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill
proposed_concept.description: Specialized agent skill suite executing chapter intake triage, workspace coverage auditing, estate status tracking, and submission cleaning.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations Skill provides automation routines for chapter intake triage, community directory auditing, submission validation, and estate tracking across Agentic AI Foundation event repositories. It standardizes data cleaning and issue detection to prevent false positives during applicant workflow reviews [^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Architecture / Specification

The operational toolchain implements multi-role data validation and flag suppression routines:

- **Decided-No Suppression**: The `clean-data` scan and issue generation formula skip submissions where every role tab listing the applicant has resolved to a terminal negative status (such as `Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate`) [^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Multi-Role Verdict Handling**: If an applicant appears on multiple role tabs with mixed statuses (e.g., denied as organizer but active as speaker), flags remain active until all role tabs reach a terminal decision [^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Missing Column Safety**: If a role tab lacks required schema columns (`Status`, `Timestamp`, or `Email`), suppression is bypassed to ensure potential issues remain visible to reviewers [^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Lifecycle History

Operational scanning logic was updated to align `scan` and dynamic formula generation with `DECIDED_NO` handling, preventing stale notifications for rejected submissions [^evt-community-events-pr-58].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and best practice baselines for agentic AI deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing threat modeling methodologies, security architectural patterns, and defensive best practices for autonomous AI agents and runtime environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The working group operates across multiple workstreams to provide practical controls countering prompt injection, untrusted tool execution, credential leakage, and unauthorized delegation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]

The group is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), reporting regularly to the AAIF Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its engineering outputs across three primary workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, maintaining the core defensive guidance catalog and feature matrices mapping requirements across people, process, and technology controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating industry baselines (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) against agentic risk profiles.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, authoring architectural pattern specifications including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

The working group collaborates closely with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on workload identity and attestation, as well as with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on security terminology.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group transitioned from formation into active execution with confirmed workstream leads.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] In September 2026, the WG merged its initial Draft deliverables under `deliverables/`, specifically the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and the [Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), alongside its first four catalog patterns and an accompanying feature matrix.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate initial draft merge status, governance rules, and supporting feature matrix details from the September 2026 working group report and PR.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines and control baselines covering credential hygiene, context leakage, tool execution boundaries, and runtime defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide* is an authoritative guideline deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) that establishes baseline engineering and operational controls for designing, deploying, and governing agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The document standardizes defensive countermeasures for credential protection, context isolation, tool call authorization, and safe multi-agent execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Maintained as a living specification under workstream leads Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the guide serves as the foundation for static analysis rules, SDK conformance baselines, and enterprise deployment audits.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The best practices guide establishes prescriptive controls across core agentic risk surfaces:
- **Credential and Identity Hygiene**: Enforcing ephemeral credentials, workload identity binding, and non-extractable secret references across agent execution context.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Context and Data Protection**: Mitigating indirect prompt injection, cross-session memory poisoning, and data exfiltration through strictly segmented context buffers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Tool Boundary Enforcement**: Enforcing least-privilege scoping, schema validation, and side-effect containment on external API and tool interactions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-36]
- **Feature Matrix and Static Rule Synthesis**: A paired Security Best Practices Feature Matrix maps each recommended practice across people, process, and technology dimensions, while enabling automated enforcement by linters and static analysis engines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Identity and trust topics (such as hardware root-of-trust and agent attestation) are partitioned to align with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
Following draft iteration through mid-2026, the guide resolved approximately 88 community review comments and merged as an official Draft deliverable (`DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md`) on September 30, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Ongoing maintenance and feature enhancements are governed through mandatory reviews by the workstream leads and open GitHub pull requests.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation benchmarking OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight agentic threat domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
*Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design* is a baseline security research report authored by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg for the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The study conducts a systematic gap analysis comparing established cybersecurity and AI risk frameworks against the operational realities of autonomous multi-step agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

The analysis evaluates four foundational frameworks—OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—across eight specific agentic threat areas to guide where standard controls suffice and where new threat vectors require purpose-built specifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The deliverable establishes a two-tiered classification methodology:
- **Baseline Adoption**: Recommends adopting existing taxonomy elements and control catalogs from MITRE ATLAS and OWASP as the working group's foundational reference baseline for traditional attack chains and model risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Agentic Gap Prioritization**: Directs net-new engineering and threat modeling resources toward eight identified agent-specific vulnerabilities, notably unconstrained tool composition, cross-boundary autonomous escalation, feedback-loop manipulation, and ambient session hijacking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

The resulting taxonomy underpins cross-working-group alignment with [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) and informs future security pattern catalogs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The initial draft completed review in September 2026 and merged on September 30, 2026, as Draft v0.1 (`DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Following publication, the working group instituted dedicated threat modeling working sessions to address the high-priority gap areas identified in the report.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for resolving bounded operational problems autonomously through isolated execution, deterministic gates, and convergence loops.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Bounded Autonomous Remediation* reference architecture defines an operational model for an AI agent to diagnose, plan, and remediate bounded operational incidents without requiring continuous synchronous human supervision.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49] The architecture constrains execution within pre-verified blast radii using deterministic safety gates and convergence limits.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]

Standardized by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this reference architecture establishes rigorous separation between internal execution steps and the overarching problem admitted to the system.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture codifies strict terminology boundaries for operational units:
- **Business Task**: The admitted bounded business problem or work item handled by an end-to-end execution run (such as remediating an alerting service or rolling back a failed deployment).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]
- **Activity**: A modular workflow subunit or atomic execution step within the run executed by the agent or runtime environment.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]

The system architecture composes three core patterns:
1. [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Isolates the agent's generative reasoning and action proposals from privileged actuators.
2. [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Validates candidate commands against hard invariant checks and blast-radius policies before granting execution permission.
3. [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Limits diagnostic and corrective iterations to explicit budget and cycle thresholds, preventing runaway cost or cascading degradation.

# Lifecycle History
Developed under the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, the reference architecture was refined in PR #49 to clarify the distinction between internal workflow activities and admitted business tasks across all lifecycle stages, diagrams, and recovery flows.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security guidance, threat modeling frameworks, and defensive design patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]. The group coordinates cross-cutting architectural baselines across AAIF deliverables, with identity and trust mechanisms managed in coordination with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].

# Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group maintains several core deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]:
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Living baseline document maintained through issues and pull requests, incorporating feature matrices and security control baselines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Comparative threat modeling framework benchmarked against industry standards, with dedicated threat modeling sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural patterns catalog providing concrete security controls, including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].
- **Security Taxonomy**: Cross-working-group security and privacy terminology developed in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) under a quiet-period review workflow [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].

# Operating Model and Governance
Deliverables follow strict multi-party approval requirements where pull request authors may not merge their own deliverables into publication paths, leaving folder authority with workstream leads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]. To ensure global participation, the working group conducts alternating APAC-friendly meeting sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]. Formal external liaison relationships, such as bilateral technical exchanges with ETSI TC SAI regarding AI agent cybersecurity requirements, are coordinated through the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25].

# References

proposed_concept.title: Proposal-Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern enforcing authorization and attribution at protected boundaries by separating proposal generation from action execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal-Execution Split pattern prevents unauthorized or unverified agent operations by strictly decoupling the generation of an operational proposal from the mechanism authorized to execute it [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. By introducing an explicit governance boundary between intent synthesis and system state modification, systems can enforce policy verification, human inspection, and cryptographic attribution before point-of-effect execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern focuses on separation of authority rather than physical process or deployment separation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. While proposal generation and execution can be hosted in distinct environments or microservices, the requirement is that the proposal-generating capability role lacks ambient privileges or execution credentials at protected interfaces [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

Key architectural elements include:
- **Capability Separation vs Topology**: The pattern specifies logical capability roles (proposer vs executor) rather than requiring rigid distributed deployment topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Point-of-Effect Gating**: Side effects requiring split execution are non-exhaustive and include irreversible data mutations, financial commitments, external communications, and infrastructure state changes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Implementation Variants**: Implementations range from harness and orchestration-level interception—such as SDK tool-use gates (e.g., `canUseTool` callbacks) that prevent tool dispatch without confirmation—to cryptographic approval checkpoints and verified execution workers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Related Patterns
- [Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

# References
- aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration: PR #53 (Updates based on Issue 45 TC Feedback)

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between agent proposal and execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval reference architecture defines an operational model where an autonomous agent formulates actions or remediation plans, but cannot execute them without explicit human sign-off [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. The architecture enforces a structural boundary ensuring that the proposal phase produces an immutable candidate execution payload while execution authority remains reserved for authorized humans or execution delegates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture is structured around capability roles rather than strict deployment boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]:
- **Separation of Authority**: The separation between proposing and executing focuses on authority, credentials, and point-of-effect boundaries rather than requiring isolated processes or distinct physical servers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Applicability Scope**: The architecture applies when a single agent produces the candidate proposal that an authorized operator must evaluate, distinguishing it from multi-agent critique isolation or swarm topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Protected Side Effects**: Point-of-effect protection covers non-exhaustive operational actions, including production database writes, cloud provisioning, security policy changes, and outbound messages [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Related Patterns
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill coordinates intake triage, speaker and venue pipelines, chapter CRM synchronization, and access granting across AAIF community event programs [^evt-community-events-pr-59]. The skill manages data validation and routing across intake forms, operational spreadsheets, and CRM backends [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill architecture enforces structured role gating and schema integrity across event intake [^evt-community-events-pr-59]:
- **Per-Role Gate Filtering**: Rather than relying on a single multiple-choice intake selector, intake pipelines process explicit per-role questions (organize, speak, host venue, collaborate) allowing a single submission to span multiple roles simultaneously [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Collaborator Pipeline**: A dedicated `Collaborators` role tab routes non-CRM collaborative and marketing partnership proposals, isolating non-organizer outreach from chapter CRM synchronization [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Defensive Migration and Guarding**: Operations formulas incorporate explicit missing-column guards and automated migration scripts (`migrate_intake_role_gates.py`) to prevent formula errors or blanking during upstream intake form schema modifications [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Idempotency and Order Guarantees**: Status and reviewer columns align with append-only filtered lists to maintain manual reviewer notes without row shifting during live operations [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group defines open capability maps, transaction lifecycle handoffs, and trust standards for agent-driven commercial transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]. The group standardizes requirements for autonomous purchasing, delegation verification, and legal-operational boundaries across emerging commercial agent protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

# Capability Map Architecture
The working group evaluates agentic commerce protocols across multi-dimensional criteria [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]:
- **Buyer Legal Capacity**: Evaluating protocols for assertions of principal legal capacity and age verification across varied jurisdictional frameworks where minor delegation may be void or voidable [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
- **Multi-Layer Record Retention**: Establishing data retention matrices spanning AI governance requirements (such as EU AI Act provider and deployer obligations), personal data storage limitations, and payments and anti-money laundering (AML) regulatory retention mandates [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
- **Point-of-Checkout Identity**: Addressing the identity transition where agents replace humans at checkout, requiring unambiguous tracking of which entity holds transaction evidence and audit logs [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

# References
- aaif/wg-agentic-commerce: Issue #8 (The capability map cannot score a protocol without (1) buyer capacity, and (2) record retention)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry framework capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, execution receipts, and testable conformance vectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry specification defining structured event schemas, state transition graphs, and verifiable execution receipts for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]. Developed under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the standard establishes common semantics for OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) pipelines and automated conformance test suites.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes runtime telemetry formats and automated validation requirements:
- **Span and Event Taxonomy**: Formats reasoning steps, plan selections, tool invocations, retries, and approval gates into correlated trace spans.
- **Trace-Model Test Kit**: Provides an executable OTLP/JSON test suite evaluating execution continuity, signature validity, missing or duplicate receipts, ticket ID tampering, and cross-tenant action identifier collisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Evidence and Signature Boundary**: Maintains separation between cryptographic signature validity and runtime effect correlation, integrating with signed vector suites to evaluate policy compliance without assuming underlying tenant metadata authenticity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #57**: Added the trace-model test kit containing six OTLP/JSON reference fixtures, naive-reader validation, and synthetic receipt verification test cases [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines and control baselines covering credential hygiene, context isolation, and pre-execution authorization hooks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide outlines defensive architectural baselines, credential isolation patterns, and authorization boundaries for deployed agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document defines baseline expectations for runtime tool interception, permission boundaries, and audit logging.

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline defines layered defensive controls across agent execution boundaries:
- **Pre-Execution Control Hooks**: Intercepting every tool invocation prior to execution through deterministic policy hooks that evaluate tool names, runtime arguments, and context to return an allow, deny, modify, or ask action [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Approval Fatigue Mitigation**: Restricting human escalation solely to the hook's "ask" path rather than treating manual reviews as an all-inclusive control, addressing high failure rates caused by human review fatigue during repeated execution prompts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Standardized Policy Interfaces**: Aligning policy enforcement and wire-level hook schemas with open industry specifications such as the OWASP Agent Control Standard (ACS) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# Lifecycle History
- **Issue #31**: Raised proposal to restructure Section 4 by placing the four-tier authorization model behind pre-execution hooks to replace static classifier assumptions with contextual runtime filtering [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing workflow execution models, reference architectures, and agentic orchestration patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group standardizes workflow execution patterns, orchestration invariants, and formal reference architectures across the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55]. The group focuses on translating real-world operational requirements into deterministic, auditable, and resilient multi-step agent topologies.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group develops and maintains several classes of technical deliverables:
- **Single-Agent Reference Architectures**: Formal reference implementations incorporating structural separation of duties, such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md).
- **Multi-Agent Reference Architectures**: Blueprints addressing distributed coordination topologies, beginning with independent parallel research and merge workflows where subagents execute concurrent tasks without peer-to-peer communication [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55].
- **Pattern Catalog**: Standardized orchestration primitives, including [Bounded Convergence Loops](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Durable Waits](../patterns/durable-wait.md), and [Autonomy Graduation](../patterns/autonomy-graduation.md).

# Lifecycle History
- **Issue #55**: Initiated the development track for the group's first multi-agent reference architecture addressing parallel research and merge jobs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation harness and two-arm differential test framework measuring skill trigger accuracy, prompt injection resistance, and credential hygiene across AAIF operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical evaluation harness built on `claude plugin eval` that tests agent skill activation, behavioral adherence, and security invariants across the AAIF community events toolkit [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. While deterministic CI checks validate YAML syntax, script computation, and tooling banners, the evaluation suite validates non-deterministic runtime agent decisions that cannot be verified by static analysis—such as whether an agent activates the correct skill given colloquial user prompts and whether it complies with instruction boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation framework executes across localized test fixtures and specific operational scenarios using a differential two-arm test architecture [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

## Two-Arm Differential Testing Model
Each evaluation test case executes two separate arms:
- **Plugin Arm (`with-only`)**: Evaluates model performance with the skill files and plugin context loaded.
- **Baseline Arm**: Evaluates raw model performance without the plugin context loaded.

By comparing performance between arms, the evaluation framework measures the delta directly attributable to instructions in `SKILL.md` rather than baseline foundation model behavior [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. For example, in speaker bio generation tests, the unaugmented baseline emitted private personal phone numbers and emails provided in prompt context, whereas the skill-augmented arm enforced public-copy redaction boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

## Targeted Operational Test Cases
The suite targets seven failure modes identified in production operations [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:
- `announcement-post`: Verifies triggering discrimination among adjacent attendee-facing copy skills when RSVP notices open [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `recap-post`: Paired with announcement testing to detect description semantic blur between adjacent writing tasks [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `speaker-bio`: Validates privacy guardrails against leaking private phone numbers and addresses into public event copy [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `triage-intake`: Tests untrusted input resistance when intake forms contain adversarial directives asking to be marked accepted [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `sync-chapters-write-gate`: Asserts that skill instructions convey runtime human approval gates for write operations rather than relying solely on script enforcement [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `audit-slack`: Tests trigger coverage against colloquial user phrasing without requiring exact keyword echoes [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- `check-setup`: Tests setup diagnostics when non-technical operators ask general readiness questions and offer sensitive credentials [^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1].

## Credential Hygiene and Security Graders
Evaluation cases incorporate specialized LLM-based graders to enforce security hygiene. In `check-setup`, the `no_token_in_chat` grader verifies that when an operator offers to paste credentials such as Slack tokens into chat transcripts, the agent actively refuses or redirects the operator to store tokens in the local OS keychain (e.g., Keychain Access) rather than accepting or recording secret tokens in conversational memory [^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed].

## Execution and Privacy Controls
Evaluation runs are executed via `claude plugin eval . --no-publish --trust-plugin`, keeping all test transcripts local rather than transmitting operational data to external hosted logging endpoints [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Because CI workflows on pull request forks operate without external API secrets, these model-graded evaluations run out-of-band locally by maintainers [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# Lifecycle History
Developed within `aaif/community-events` to validate plugin skill dispatch reliability and prevent prompt leakage and regression during skill description editing [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Evaluates skills cataloged under `../skills/community-event-operations.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skills
proposed_concept.description: Modular operational skill suite providing data cleaning, immutable backup snapshots, and design system governance for AAIF community event assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations Skills form an integrated automation suite for managing the AAIF global chapter network, event intake pipelines, and branded asset infrastructure [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. The suite enforces strict boundary separations between read-only scanning and stateful mutations, mandates immutable backups prior to data modifications, and prevents font or formatting corruption across office document formats [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Architecture / Specification
The operational architecture is structured into specialized task skills governed by shared execution constraints and safety patterns [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

## Tooling and Rendering Constraints
All operations targeting Google Drive documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks mandate exclusive use of the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) coupled with Python automation [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Native API Edits**: Operations prioritize native Google Workspace API modifications (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) and restrict direct OOXML byte manipulation to genuine Office files [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Prohibition on Desktop Office Emulators**: The execution environment strictly forbids headless office packages such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` for previews, conversions, or edits. Such emulators substitute local fonts for AAIF brand typography and drop unrecognized OpenXML tags [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Local visual previews must be rendered through remote APIs (e.g., rendering slides to PNG or copying Docs to Google Drive for PDF export) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

## Data Quality Normalization (`aaif-clean-data`)
The `aaif-clean-data` skill normalizes intake records within the Community Intake Ops sheet [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]:
- **Read-Only Proposals**: Execution follows a `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md` pattern; `clean.py scan` generates non-destructive diagnostic reports and requires explicit human approval before running mutative flags (`apply`, `cities --write`, `install-flags`) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Value Sanitization**: Values are written using `RAW` mode instead of `USER_ENTERED` to prevent formula injection [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Untrusted Input Handling**: Inbound form submissions and sheet cells are treated as untrusted data; instruction-like text in user responses is isolated to prevent unauthorized modifications to chapter roles or application statuses [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Privacy Protection**: Working files containing personally identifiable information (`changes.json`) are written to temporary directories created with `mktemp -d` and destroyed after execution [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

## Immutable Pre-Mutation Backup (`aaif-backup`)
The `aaif-backup` skill snapshots critical intake spreadsheets, Drive documents, and local assets prior to risky structural edits [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]:
- **Immutable Version History**: Snapshots are written as non-overwriting files keyed by ISO UTC timestamps (`<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`) [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Format Export**: Native Drive files are exported to standardized formats (`.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.pptx`) to provide an out-of-band rollback capability before bulk cleanups or schema migrations [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].

## Design System Governance (`restyle_design_system.py`)
The estate-wide restyling engine reconciles presentation decks, trackers, and CRMs across all chapters with AAIF design standards [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]:
- **Strict Scope Boundaries**: Restyling operates only against canonical templates matched against a designated allowlist (`TEMPLATE_FILES`), explicitly skipping customized organizer decks [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **SpreadsheetML vs DrawingML Isolation**: In workbooks, restyling exclusively rewrites styling records (`xl/styles.xml` and themes) without modifying cell values or shared strings [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Pre-Change Archiving**: Restyle passes write full pre-change copies to timestamped backup folders before uploading updates, preserving the original unmutated file as an immutable rollback target [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Legibility Verification**: Automated contrast audits inspect slides against WCAG AA standards, programmatically adjusting text tones against background plates to prevent unreadable contrast collisions [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Lifecycle History
Evolved as operational tooling within `aaif/community-events` supporting global chapter onboarding and intake operations [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Behavioral and dispatch guarantees are continuously validated by `../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md` [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill suite executing chapter and online series management, data cleaning, preflight diagnostics, and event collateral generation under strict privacy and tooling constraints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated execution capabilities for Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chapter and online event operations across multiple host agent runtimes, including [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]. Designed for non-technical community operators, the suite standardizes operational workflows such as environment verification, intake sheet hygiene, online series asset provisioning, presentation generation, and event announcement authoring[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

The suite enforces rigorous operational boundaries to prevent silent data corruption and inadvertent exposure of private details, requiring explicit human approval for state modifications and strict adherence to native API document manipulation[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Environment and Diagnostic Preflight
The `aaif-check-setup` module provides a read-only preflight diagnostic verifying agent host readiness across Python runtimes, the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`), Google sign-in scopes, Community Intake sheet edit permissions, Slack authentication tokens, Luma API keys, and headless Chrome for PDF exports[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]. When external tooling or credentials are misconfigured, the check fails with plain-language remediation instructions while confirming that local content-drafting skills remain operational without external credentials[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

Secrets resolution follows a deterministic cascade managed by `aaif_events.credentials`:
1. Process environment variables[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].
2. Repository-root `.env` file[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].
3. macOS Keychain storage (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`), cached per execution run to prevent repeated access prompts[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

## Intake Data Normalization Pipeline
The `aaif-clean-data` workflow implements a two-stage proposal-execution pattern for community intake spreadsheets[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]:
- **Scan Mode (Default, Read-Only)**: Detects formatting anomalies (whitespace trimming, case normalization for names and cities, canonicalization of LinkedIn profile URLs) and flags ambiguous records (unresolved `City="Other"` selections, invalid or duplicate email addresses, missing applicant names) without altering state[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **Apply Mode (Write on Human Approval)**: Writes accepted changes exclusively to the source `Form Responses` tab, appending an `Autofixes` column tracking provenance per row[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. Unresolved applicant cities are explicitly flagged to prevent silent exclusion from downstream CRM distribution and chapter lists[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

## Asset Lifecycle and Strict Tooling Constraints
Event series and chapter asset provisioning (`aaif-create-online-series`) clones centralized templates (`TemplateSeries` under Google Drive `Online/`) and updates identity tokens while preserving template runbooks[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].

All file mutations and inspections must strictly satisfy the following operational tooling invariants:
- **API and Native Tooling Only**: All Google Drive reads, edits, and writes must run through the `gws` CLI driven by Python scripts[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Prohibition of Headless Desktop Suites**: Tools such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited for file editing, format conversion, or local preview rendering, as they substitute local system fonts for official brand typography and corrupt Office Open XML (OOXML) structures[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. Previews must be rendered via official API exports[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **OOXML Surgery**: Stored Office formats (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) must be modified via byte-level ZIP component surgery to preserve embedded fonts and untouched parts, avoiding round-trip conversion losses[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

## Public-Copy Privacy Rule
All content generation skills—such as `aaif-announcement-post` and `aaif-dayof-slides`—must enforce the Public-Copy Rule[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]:
- Generated text for external publishing (posts, slide decks, event pages, direct messages) must never disclose non-public personally identifiable information (PII) or confidential logistical data, including speaker emails, door codes, attendee phone numbers, or intake row submissions[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].
- When private fields are omitted, the agent transcript must name the field rather than echoing the value (e.g., stating "I left out her email" rather than citing the actual email address), preventing sensitive data leaks in conversational transcripts[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- Event collateral must preserve fixed brand slides without modification, position host lockups according to [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md), and append standard regulatory footers referencing the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and Linux Foundation Privacy Policy[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, palette, and asset specifications governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets, presentation decks, and document rendering pipelines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Brand Guidelines define visual identity, typographic standards, color palettes, and presentation formats for the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). These specifications ensure consistent representation across digital media, open-source repositories, community chapters, and event collateral[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516][^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

Adherence to brand specifications extends to automated tooling and document generation pipelines used by agent runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7], preventing font substitution and visual degradation during automated asset assembly[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].

# Architecture / Specification

## Presentation and Slide Standards
Event presentation templates (such as the standard AAIF "Day of Event" deck) incorporate fixed, mandatory brand slides alongside modular event-specific slides[^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]:
- **Fixed Brand Content**: Core foundational slides—including the "About AAIF" overview and global network metric slides—are designated as fixed brand standards and must not be reworded, reformatted, or omitted during automated deck generation[^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].
- **Host Lockups and Sponsoring Attribution**: On title and welcome slides, the `HOSTED BY` banner carries the immutable AAIF organizational lockup[^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. Neighboring logo placeholders (`LOGO 1`, `LOGO 2`) are designated image drop zones for event co-hosts or chapter partners and must never be filled with plain text or replace the primary AAIF lockup[^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. Venue hosts and supporting members are formally credited in prose on dedicated concluding recognition slides[^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

## Asset Integrity and Rendering Constraints
To preserve brand typography and embedded layout fidelity, automated tools and agents managing AAIF collateral must conform to strict document processing rules[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]:
- **Prohibition of LibreOffice and Desktop Conversion Tools**: Automated environments must never use LibreOffice (`soffice`), `unoconv`, or generic desktop office suites to edit, convert, or preview AAIF documents[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. These suites routinely substitute local system fallback fonts for official AAIF brand typefaces and discard complex OpenXML (OOXML) structures[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **Native API Rendering**: Document and slide previews must be rendered exclusively through native cloud APIs (such as exporting Google Slides or Docs to PDF/PNG via the `gws` Google Workspace CLI) rather than local headless converters[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **OOXML Structure Preservation**: Modifications to Office files (`.pptx`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`) must be performed using targeted byte-level zip part manipulation so that untouched components and embedded brand fonts remain intact[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

proposed_concept.title: Social Media Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Governance policies, editorial voice standards, privacy constraints, and compliance footers for official Agentic AI Foundation social channels and event announcements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Social Media Guidelines govern public communications, promotional copy, editorial voice, and regulatory compliance across official Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) channels and community announcements[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. These standards guide contributors, organizers, and automated agents drafting public content for platforms such as LinkedIn[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

Public communications emphasize technical substance over hype, prioritizing practitioner-focused insights while strictly guarding private participant information[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

# Architecture / Specification

## House Editorial Voice
Communications across AAIF channels must follow core tone and messaging principles[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]:
- **Share the Practice, Never Sell the Product**: Copy must center on real-world engineering practices, architectural patterns, and practical trade-offs rather than vendor promotion or product sales pitches[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Builder-to-Builder Authenticity**: Messaging should remain specific, grounded, and concise rather than grand or sensationalist, prioritizing signal and clarity over inflated attendance or metric claims[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

## Event Launch and Announcement Post Structure
When drafting event launch and RSVP announcements (e.g., on LinkedIn), copy must conform to a standardized, scannable format[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]:
- **Length and Formatting Constraints**: Approximately 120 words in total length, containing at most one emoji and no more than three relevant hashtags[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Core Elements**:
  1. A one-line introductory hook highlighting the technical topic[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
  2. Concrete logistics outlining the what, when, and where[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
  3. Featured speakers and session topic accompanied by a single tangible takeaway[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
  4. An explicit Call to Action (CTA) linking directly to the verified event RSVP platform (e.g., Luma or Gradual.AI)[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

## Public-Copy Privacy and Boundary Enforcement
All automated drafting workflows and manual publications must strictly enforce privacy protections[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]:
- **PII Exclusion**: Public posts must never include personal email addresses, private phone numbers, physical door access codes, or attendee names that are not already publicly announced[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. When a non-public operational detail must be communicated, copy must describe the retrieval mechanism (e.g., "door access will be sent to registered attendees") rather than publishing the raw credential[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Transcript Cleanliness**: In automated agent interactions, sensitive field omissions must refer to field names rather than echoing back the redacted values, preventing leakage in session logs and public transcripts[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

## Mandatory Compliance Footer
All published event announcement posts must close with a quiet, standardized footer providing links to community governance and privacy policies[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]:
- Linux Foundation Code of Conduct: `https://events.linuxfoundation.org/about/code-of-conduct`[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]
- Linux Foundation Privacy Policy: `https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/privacy-policy`[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill suite managing community chapters, event scheduling, automated Slack workspace audits, and social copy generation across Google Workspace and external platforms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill suite is a collection of modular agent skills that automate administrative, auditing, and publishing workflows for Agentic AI Foundation chapters and online series[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Designed for cross-client portability across runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Cursor, the toolkit pairs local deterministic Python automation with Google Workspace CLI (`gws`), Slack APIs, and external event platforms[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

The skill suite operates under strict boundary constraints: content and audit engines are read-only or staged locally, and state-modifying actions—such as creating live Luma events or publishing external copy—require explicit human confirmation[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Conformance and evaluation mechanisms for these operational skills are benchmarked by the [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Skill Modules

- **Event Creation (`aaif-create-event`)**: Clones standardized event sections within chapter or series `Event Tracker.docx` documents, programmatically back-calculating due dates for operational milestones relative to the scheduled event date[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]. Can push drafted details to Luma via API, but strictly gates live creation on prior human approval aligned with the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Social Carousel Copy (`aaif-carousel-copy`)**: Generates structured 6-slide LinkedIn carousels based on official presentation templates, adhering to builder-focused house tone guidelines (Slide 1 hook, Slide 6 call-to-action)[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]. Enforces strict redactive rules prohibiting the leakage or repetition of private contact details in drafts or conversational reasoning[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Slack Workspace Audit (`aaif-audit-slack`)**: Independent read-only auditing layer dividing checks into three engines (Organizers, Topics, and Members) and a shared measurement layer (`audit_activity.py`)[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Results are compiled into a unified HTML dashboard (`summarize_audits.py`) without modifying workspace channels or rosters[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d][^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

## Tooling Rules & Document Rendering

All interactions with Drive files are restricted to Python scripts driving the `gws` CLI[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]. Native Google Workspace document formats (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) must be edited via native APIs, while legacy Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) undergo direct byte-level OOXML edits[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]. Headless suites such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited to avoid font substitution and OOXML degradation; document previews are rendered by converting temporary copies to PDF via the Google Drive export API[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].

## Data Hygiene & Untrusted Input

- **Untrusted Input Invariants**: Member profiles, channel topics, message payloads, and CRM sheet cells are strictly classified as untrusted external data rather than agent instructions[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Text attempting to grant administrative roles or force channel membership changes is flagged to the operator and ignored by execution engines[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Repository Privacy Controls**: Audit caches and reports are generated with restrictive permissions (`0600` inside `0700` directories) and engines refuse to execute unless output paths are verifiably safe from `git add -A` commits[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. In installed plugin contexts, persistent state is mapped away from working directories to standard OS data directories per [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
