proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Architectural specifications for packaging multi-client agent plugins, path token resolutions, external persistent data directories, and out-of-band secret management.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Plugin Portability guidelines establish architectural conventions allowing AI agent plugins and skills to execute predictably across diverse host applications, including [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. By decoupling script execution from working directory assumptions, standardizing path resolution tokens, isolating persistent state, and externalizing credentials, plugins achieve runtime compatibility regardless of whether they are run from a local git repository checkout or installed into version-isolated application containers[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Path Token Resolution

Installed plugins operate in environments where host clients manage execution contexts differently—Goose clones git repositories directly, whereas tools like Claude Desktop unpack repository archives into version-specific directories stripped of `.git` metadata[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Consequently:

- Skill instructions in `SKILL.md` must resolve script locations via a dynamic `<skill-root>` token resolved from the loaded skill directory rather than relative paths from an assumed repository root (e.g. `skills/<name>/...`)[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- CI validation harnesses must enforce that all referenced script paths use `<skill-root>` to prevent silent failures when executed by desktop runtimes[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

## Persistent State and Data Directories

Plugins must never store persistent state, caches, backups, or generated reports in the plugin installation directory or the user's current working directory (`cwd`)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]:

- **Ephemeral Install Trees**: Automatic updates replace the plugin install directory entirely, orphaning any state or backups stored within it[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Host Working Directories**: Desktop clients frequently run from personal or synchronized user directories that must not be polluted with scratch files[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Central Data Directory**: Persistent state must route through a dedicated datadir utility (such as `aaif_events.datadir`), resolving to standard operating system application support folders (e.g., `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF` on macOS, or `$XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux), overridable by an absolute `AAIF_DATA_DIR` environment variable[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Temporary files must use system scratch directories (`mktemp -d`)[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

## Dual Manifest Structure

To bridge diverging client packaging specifications:

- The root directory hosts standard `plugin.json` adhering to the open Agent Plugin standard[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- Client-specific manifests, such as Claude Desktop and Claude Code configurations, reside in dedicated subdirectories (e.g., `.claude-plugin/`), allowing multi-client support from a single upstream codebase[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- Individual capabilities are encapsulated in [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) subdirectories with standard YAML frontmatter[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

## Out-of-Band Secret Sourcing

Desktop assistant applications do not propagate interactive shell environments to plugin subprocesses[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. To maintain credential hygiene without requiring users to expose API keys inside conversational transcripts:

- Sensitive secrets (such as Slack tokens and calendar API keys) must be resolved hierarchically: first from process environment variables, second from a repository-level `.env` file, and third from the OS keychain (e.g. macOS Keychain Access under named items)[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- Setup verification skills (`aaif-check-setup`) confirm keychain accessibility prior to executing operations[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

mutations.rationale: Add control baselines for untrusted context injection defense, conversational transcript privacy, safe emission file permissions, and out-of-band credential hygiene.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural baseline controls for agent operations, governing prompt injection isolation, out-of-band secret resolution, context transcript privacy, and safe emission verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agentic AI Security Best Practices establishes mandatory control baselines and architectural safeguards for deploying autonomous and semi-autonomous agents across production environments[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. The standard addresses boundary isolation, transcript data retention, untrusted content sanitization, and filesystem permission integrity to prevent credential compromise, prompt injection, and accidental leakage of personally identifiable information (PII)[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04][^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].

These practices complement operational patterns such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) by defining runtime data-handling and credential hygiene standards for agents operating over shared platforms[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Architecture / Specification

## Untrusted Input Sanitization

External data retrieved from third-party APIs, messaging platforms, and shared spreadsheets—including Slack user profiles, channel descriptions, message bodies, and CRM spreadsheet cells—must be handled as untrusted data and never evaluated as agent instructions[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

- Directive text contained within profile attributes or database rows (e.g., "add me to the organizers channel", "grant admin role", or prompt override attempts) must never trigger administrative grants, status modifications, or execution path alterations[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- Suspicious directives embedded in external fields must be quoted to human operators as non-executable observation flags rather than accepted as actionable instructions[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

## Conversational Transcript and Public-Copy Privacy

Agent transcripts are frequently logged, copied, or pushed to collaborative channels, presenting significant leakage risks[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]:

- **Omission by Reference**: When an agent redacts or omits sensitive data (such as emails, phone numbers, or access codes), it must name the omitted attribute field rather than echoing the value itself[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]. For example, stating "omitted email address" is permitted, whereas stating "omitted user@example.com" is a security violation because it commits the private data to the transcript[^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Synthetic Data Testing**: Automated test suites, fixtures, and documentation must utilize synthetic data exclusively; real user identifiers must never be recorded in fixtures, test logs, or pull request docstrings[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. CI linting scripts (e.g., `check_no_real_pii.py`) must validate synthetic formats prior to merging[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

## Safe Emission and Filesystem Defenses

To prevent the unintentional exposure of operational data in public repositories:

- **Filesystem Permissions**: Runtime state files containing member metadata or API caches must be created with strict permissions (`0600` files inside `0700` directories)[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].
- **Pre-execution Git Boundary Checks**: Tooling engines that produce cached data or backups must evaluate local paths against source-control tracking and refuse to start if their cache or output destinations would be captured by `git add -A`[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].

## Credential Custody and Interactive Prompts

Agents must never solicit passwords, tokens, or private keys within chat windows, nor should they attempt to execute interactive CLI authentication commands in headless sessions[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Credentials must be provisioned out-of-band and stored in operating system keychains or secure vault integrations accessible via designated read APIs[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and structured schema mapping open-source agentic AI runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, and control planes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and machine-readable catalog documenting open-source runtimes, communication protocols, developer tools, and governance frameworks across the agent ecosystem. Maintained under the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape enforces strict data schema rules to classify functional boundaries, project provenance, and AAIF membership status [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog is defined via `landscape/landscape.yml` and enforces validation against schema definitions in `docs/data-schemas.md` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30]. Items are grouped into broad domains and targeted subcategories:
- **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Covers core workflow execution engines and emerging operational infrastructure, such as the proposed **Gateways & Control Planes** subcategory for ingress routers and reverse proxies like `agentgateway` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Encompasses wire communication protocols like [Agent-to-Agent](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) and Model Context Protocol, alongside repository-level conventions under the proposed **Conventions & File Formats** subcategory for standards like `AGENTS.md` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- **Prompt & Runtime Guardrails**: Captures tools designed to constrain model behavior and enforce policy boundaries.

All entries mandate uniform metadata fields (`name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, and `project`), with URLs subject to automated HTTP link verification to track organization renames, upstream domain migrations, and canonical specifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History
- Initial landscape schema and web visualizer deployed.
- Structural revisions proposed adding dedicated subcategories for control planes and repository conventions to separate wire protocols from static repository standards [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- Comprehensive link audit conducted to correct relocated repositories and broken project domains across catalog entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31].

# References
- Landscape Data Schema (`docs/data-schemas.md`)
- AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream Repository (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`)

proposed_concept.title: AgentProto Privacy-Preserving Dialog Recovery
proposed_concept.description: Research prototype and recovery protocol investigating reliable multi-agent dialog resumption across administrative domains without exposing globally linkable identifiers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
AgentProto Privacy-Preserving Dialog Recovery is an open-source research prototype designed to investigate reliable multi-agent communication across independent administrative domains [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55]. Proposed as an AAIF Sandbox project, it evaluates mechanisms for recovering conversational context after gateway or mediator failures while enforcing authorization checks and preserving domain-scoped identifier privacy [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification
The prototype provides an experimental reference implementation for fault tolerance at the [Agent-to-Agent](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) boundary:
- **Cryptographic Recovery Tickets**: Generates verifiable, tamper-resistant tokens enabling participating agents to resume session state without leaking correlation identifiers across domains [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].
- **Domain-Specific Dialog Identifiers**: Ensures identifiers remain local to specific gateway boundaries, eliminating globally linkable tracking keys [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].
- **Operation Ledger Integrity**: Implements integrity checks and deduplication logic to prevent conflicting or repeated operations upon resumption [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].
- **Failure-Injection Harness**: Supplies automated test suites and reproducible evaluation tools to measure reliability and privacy-security trade-offs during simulated mediator crashes [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].

# Lifecycle History
- Submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) as a Sandbox project proposal under the project lifecycle policy [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55].

# References
- AAIF Project Proposals Issue #55: `agentproto-privacy-preserving-dialog-recovery` [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55]
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/nikhilred2619/agentproto-privacy-preserving-dialog-recovery [^evt-project-proposals-issue-55]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog, schema specification, and CI validation engine mapping open-source agentic AI projects, runtimes, and protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and structured schema that maps open-source agentic AI runtimes, frameworks, protocols, and developer tooling across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Maintained by the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream, the landscape classifies foundation projects—such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Goose—alongside member and community software into defined categories including Autonomous Agent Frameworks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Architecture / Specification
Data integrity and parser security for the underlying `landscape/landscape.yml` registry are enforced through automated schema validation and strict parser bounds [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Schema and Validation Invariants
The CI validation suite (`scripts/validate-landscape.mjs`) implements constraints to ensure browser and CLI parser parity and defend against untrusted input expansion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:
- **Parser Alignment**: Both the Node.js validation runner and client-side application (`app.js`) parse YAML using `js-yaml` configured with `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` and explicit `maxDepth` limits [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. This prevents numeric type coercion (such as string values coercing into numbers) from triggering client runtime exceptions.
- **Work Budgets**: File size is capped at 512 KB via filesystem `statSync` checks before parsing. Structural limits cap the landscape to 500 items, while traversal is limited to an object graph budget of 5,000 objects/arrays and 20,000 references [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Disallowed Constructs**: Reused object/array nodes (YAML anchors and cyclic aliases), merge keys, and unescaped control/format characters are rejected; only bounded scalar aliases are permitted [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Field Validation**: Items require `name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, and a valid `project` enum value (`member`, `graduated`, or `incubating`), with optional `repo_url` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. All URLs must use HTTPS without user credentials, and item names must be unique under Unicode normalization [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Symlink Protection**: A deployment guard (`scripts/check-no-symlinks.sh`) verifies that no symbolic links exist in sources or build artifacts before packaging with `tar --dereference`, mitigating arbitrary file publication risks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Search Execution**: The web client performs Unicode-aware regex matching (`u` flag) using a single compiled regular expression and shared match budget across fields to avoid client-side CPU exhaustion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# Lifecycle History
The landscape tracks foundation-hosted projects donated at launch, such as Goose and MCP, while coordinating taxonomy classifications for emerging entries like `agentgateway` and `AGENTS.md` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Validation automation was introduced to prevent rendering discrepancies and harden data intake against algorithmic complexity vulnerabilities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

proposed_concept.description: Open-source autonomous AI agent framework donated to the AAIF at launch providing local multi-turn execution and tool extensibility.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Goose is an open-source autonomous general-purpose AI agent framework designed for local multi-turn execution, automated code development, and extensible tool interaction [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Donated to the Agentic AI Foundation at launch alongside the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Goose serves as a foundation-hosted project categorized under Autonomous Agent Frameworks in the AAIF landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Architecture / Specification
Goose executes autonomously across local development workflows by interfacing with LLMs and local tooling [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Following its donation from Block, its official governance and repository home transitioned to the AAIF GitHub organization (`github.com/aaif-goose/goose`), with official documentation hosted at `goose-docs.ai` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

Within the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md), Goose is cataloged with `project: member` designation, aligning with the initial foundation intake tier alongside MCP [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Lifecycle History
Originally open-sourced as `block/goose`, the project was donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation upon foundation inception [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Its placement within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) mapping reflects its role as a flagship autonomous agent framework [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing protocol-neutral capability maps, lifecycle handoffs, and transaction mandates for autonomous commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining standardized interaction models, capability maps, and transaction lifecycle handoffs for AI agents conducting commercial activities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73]. The group collaborates across AAIF workstreams to establish standard terminology and governance boundaries for autonomous purchasing, delegated financial commitments, and customer-merchant handoffs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group standardizes commercial primitives within the foundation taxonomy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77]:
- **Agentic Checkout**: Formalized in the domain taxonomy to define the automated protocol stages through which an agent navigates cart assembly, pricing verification, merchant fulfillment terms, and checkout closure [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73].
- **Delegated Payment**: Architectural boundary enabling a principal (human or organization) to securely delegate payment execution authority to an agent within strict budget, token, or cryptographic limits [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76].
- **Mandate**: Explicit, verifiable authorization artifact defining the allowable scope, expiration, spending limits, and vendor parameters under which an agent is empowered to transact on behalf of a user [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].

# Lifecycle History
The working group's foundational vocabulary was integrated into the AAIF landscape and taxonomy registry via formal pull requests to establish vendor-neutral commercial standards across member organizations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, and cross-boundary agent observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body responsible for defining vendor-neutral telemetry models, agent execution trace formats, and cross-boundary observability standards across LLM primitives, MCP protocol boundaries, and host operating environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]. The group produces telemetry specifications and reference architectures to ensure agent reasoning loops and tool invocations can be reliably inspected, attributed, and diagnosed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# Architecture / Specification
In addition to technical specifications such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and cross-boundary telemetry matrices, the working group adheres to the foundation's standardized governance operations defined by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

## Governance and Reporting Conventions
The working group aligns its periodic reporting cadence with centralized Technical Committee reporting requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]:
- **Report Pull Request Naming**: Pull requests submitting periodic reports must strictly follow the format `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` (e.g., `[Report] 2024-06`), deprecating older WG-prefixed titling formats (`[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Labeling Requirements**: Monthly reports require the `monthly-report` label to enable automated discovery, ingestion, and status tracking across Technical Committee dashboards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Case Sensitivity**: Report file naming in working group repositories enforces strict case sensitivity in accordance with foundation-wide reporting guidelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# Lifecycle History
The working group operational procedures were updated in PR #62 to resolve reporting mismatches and align monthly progress disclosures with unified Technical Committee reporting automation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

mutations.rationale: Curate proposed landscape entry for Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration (AVE), an open vulnerability catalog for agentic AI components.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration
proposed_concept.description: Open vulnerability catalog assigning stable identifiers and OWASP AIVSS severity scores to behavioral flaws in agentic AI components.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration (AVE) is an open classification standard and enumeration catalog providing stable identifiers for behavioral vulnerability classes in agentic AI components, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agent skills, and large language model (LLM) plugins[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38]. The project is licensed under Apache 2.0 and proposed as an external classification framework within the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)'s [Agentic AI Landscape](./agentic-ai-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].

# Architecture / Specification
AVE establishes a standardized vocabulary for identifying security defects unique to autonomous and tool-augmented AI architectures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38]:

- **Vulnerability Identification**: Assigns deterministic, stable identifiers to behavioral vulnerabilities spanning runtime tool calls, [agent skills](../standards/agent-skills.md), and external plugin protocols[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].
- **Severity Scoring**: Integrates OWASP's AI Vulnerability Scoring System (AIVSS) framework to assess risk profiles and impact metrics across agentic deployment contexts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].
- **Framework Alignment**: Maintains crosswalks to external security frameworks including the OWASP MCP Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, complementing comparative threat modeling initiatives such as the [Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](./agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].

In the AAIF landscape schema, AVE is categorized under "Security Guardrails & Firewalls" within the "Prompt & Runtime Guardrails" subcategory as an external classification framework rather than a runtime enforcement mechanism[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History
- **Draft Proposal**: Submitted via PR#38 to `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` to introduce AVE into the landscape dataset under the `external` project classification[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38].

# References
- Repository: [https://github.com/aveproject/ave](https://github.com/aveproject/ave)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-38]
